1001tracklists.shortDescription: Track support tracking and DJ chart rankings.
1001tracklists.description: 1001Tracklists is the standard for tracking which DJs play your tracks. Support from big names is the ultimate validation in the dance industry.
1001tracklists.useCase: Monitoring track support, DJ charts, and scene relevance.
1001tracklists.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI pulls your 1001Tracklists data and shows which tracks get played most, by whom, and how that correlates with your streaming growth.
problemsSolved: You do not know who is playing your tracks in their sets
Track support is not translated into marketing actions
1001tracklists.stevinAngle: In the dance world, 1001Tracklists is where track support becomes visible: who plays your record, in which set, on which stage. That is not invented authority, it is what the scene itself looks at. What it is not is a marketing tool. It records that a big name spun your track, and then does nothing further with it. That is where artists and labels get stuck: the validation sits in the profile, the action never comes. A sudden run of plays after a festival is exactly the moment to promote something, but that moment slips by while no one is watching. Stevin runs as a layer over 1001Tracklists, reads the support in via scrape or feed, and turns a spike in plays into a concrete proposal: turn on a region here, push the release there. The person decides, Stevin signals it in time.
1001tracklists.stackImpact: Choosing 1001Tracklists as a source means accepting that the connection is rough: there is no clean public API, so count on a scrape or a manual export and on data that is not real time. It tells you who is playing your tracks, but nothing about what that earns, so you need your streaming and social data alongside it to give a play spike meaning. On its own it is a nice scoreboard, not a steering tool. So the real question is not whether you see the support, but whether something is ready to act on a spike before the moment passes.
pitfalls: Treating support as a goal in itself, when a big name spinning your track only has value once you tie promotion to it.
Relying on real-time data when the scrape can be delayed or incomplete.
Seeing a play spike but having no streaming data alongside it to know whether it earned anything.

12build.shortDescription: Tendering and quoting platform for construction.
12build.description: 12Build is the platform contractors use to put out work packages and invite subcontractors to quote. It runs the request and bidding process between parties.
12build.useCase: Put out quote requests, invite subcontractors and compare bids.
12build.howWeUseIt: Stevin reads along with the quotes and bids from 12Build and puts a layer on top that flags differences: a subcontractor who has not responded, a bid that excludes scope or sealing work, a price gap that needs explaining. Stevin does not do the tendering, it watches whether the work can actually start afterward. Connect through an export or a mail parser.
problemsSolved: Subcontractors do not respond to a request in time
Scope differences between bids get overlooked
An exclusion in the quote only surfaces later
No bridge between the chosen bid and the execution planning
12build.stevinAngle: 12Build does one specific thing well: it puts out work packages, invites subcontractors and runs the request and bidding process between parties. For the tendering itself it is strong. What it does not do is watch what happens after the bid, and that is where the damage tends to occur. We see contractors stall on the handover from quote to execution: a subcontractor who does not respond, a bid that quietly excludes sealing work or a piece of scope, a price gap that only needs explaining later. 12Build collects the bids, but it does not lay the differences side by side and it does not tie them to your planning. Stevin reads along with the quotes and bids, through an export or a mail parser, and flags those differences before they punch a hole in your execution. The estimator sees the signal and decides, Stevin does the comparison work underneath.
12build.stackImpact: Choosing 12Build solves the request side, not the execution side. You keep the bidding process tidy, but the bridge to your project planning is something you have to organize yourself, because it is not in 12Build. The connection runs through an export or a mail parser, so the data comes out. The question is whether something is watching for a chosen bid that is missing scope or for a subcontractor who stays silent. Without that, you only discover the gap once the planning is already running and it is expensive to correct.
pitfalls: Ticking off the tender process without watching the handover to execution, so the start stalls.
Missing scope differences between bids because no one lays them side by side.
Only noticing an exclusion in the quote once the work has already started.
Following up too late on an unresponsive subcontractor because no signal is set on it.

activecampaign.shortDescription: Marketing automation and CRM in one platform.
activecampaign.description: ActiveCampaign combines strong marketing automation with a built-in CRM. It offers advanced options for email, scoring, and follow-up.
activecampaign.useCase: Marketing automation with CRM features for lead nurturing.
activecampaign.howWeUseIt: Stevin sets up ActiveCampaign as the hub of your lead nurturing: from scoring and segmentation to automated follow-up flows that line up with your campaigns.
problemsSolved: Lead nurturing is not automated
Scoring and segmentation are not set up
Follow-up is not aligned with how a lead behaves
activecampaign.stevinAngle: ActiveCampaign sits in a sweet spot between Mailchimp (too simple the moment you segment seriously) and HubSpot (too expensive and too heavy unless you also use it for sales). The automation builder is actually visually logical instead of the Mailchimp tinkering, and you get CRM features without the HubSpot price. We regularly migrate accounts off Mailchimp when they hit 10,000 plus contacts or need multistep automations that Mailchimp cannot scale. Watch out: ActiveCampaign's own reporting is mediocre, so use an external BI tool or GA4 for real performance analysis.
activecampaign.stackImpact: Pair it with your website CMS (event tracking via the API or the Site Tracking script), Stripe or another payment platform for revenue attribution, and a dedicated landing page tool if you run a lot of campaigns (Unbounce, Instapage). The built-in forms are fine for simple opt-ins, but for conversion-optimized landing pages you miss A/B testing.
pitfalls: Sticking to list-based thinking instead of tag-based. Segmentation gets rigid and hard to maintain.
Tying automations to 'subscribe to list' triggers instead of event-based ones. Leads get stuck in too many flows at once.
Letting lead score run without ever calibrating it against sales feedback. The score becomes a vanity metric instead of a triage tool.
Turning on Site Tracking without cookie-consent integration. GDPR risk.

adform.shortDescription: Full-stack adtech platform for campaign management and programmatic.
adform.description: Adform is a European adtech platform that gives advertisers and agencies tools for campaign management, programmatic buying and tracking. It combines a DSP, ad server and DMP in one platform.
adform.useCase: Programmatic advertising, campaign management and cross-device tracking.
adform.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI connects Adform to your tracking and reporting stack so programmatic campaigns become part of your total view of marketing performance.
problemsSolved: Programmatic data sits isolated from other channels
No centralized overview of all media buying
adform.stevinAngle: Adform is a European adtech platform that combines a DSP, ad server and DMP, and for some advertisers that European part is the whole point: your media buying does not have to run through the American walled gardens. Functionally it is broad and solid. The weakness is not the platform itself but where it lands in the stack: programmatic data from Adform often sits isolated from the rest of your channels, so no total picture of your media buying emerges. We see teams stall on this: Adform runs, the ad server does its job, but the figures do not sit next to search, social and your CRM. The platform centralizes the buying, not the insight. Stevin runs as a layer on top, connects to your tracking and reporting through the API and brings the programmatic results into your total picture. A person judges the conclusion before anything shifts.
adform.stackImpact: Choosing Adform gives you a European alternative with a DSP, ad server and DMP in one, so you have to stitch less loose adtech together. The connection with your broader tracking and reporting is something you do have to organize, otherwise the data stays isolated. The connection runs through the API. The real question is whether the programmatic results come to sit next to your other media buying, because without that overview you judge each channel separately and miss where budget overlaps or reinforces.
pitfalls: Leaving programmatic data isolated from search, social and CRM, so no total picture.
No centralized overview of media buying, so overlap stays invisible.
Assuming a platform that centralizes the buying also centralizes the insight.
Judging each channel on its own because the figures come together nowhere.

admicom.shortDescription: ERP and project administration for construction and installation.
admicom.description: Admicom delivers business software for the construction and installation trades: from estimating and project administration to hours, materials and invoicing.
admicom.useCase: Manage the full project administration of construction and installation firms.
admicom.howWeUseIt: Stevin connects to Admicom and turns project data into signals and actions: a budget line with an out-of-date price, a project where margin is under pressure, a step that is left sitting. The judgment and the execution stay with the person, Stevin makes sure the right information surfaces in time. Connect through the API or an export.
problemsSolved: Out-of-date prices in the estimate go unnoticed
Margin risk on a project is seen too late
Project information is scattered and lacks an overview
Follow-up on open actions happens by hand
admicom.stevinAngle: Admicom is heavy machinery for construction and installation: from estimating and project administration to hours, materials and invoicing, all in one ERP. For anyone who uses it fully it is powerful, but that is exactly where the trap is. The more the system tracks, the easier it is for a deviation to sink into the numbers. We see firms stall on margin: a budget line with last year's price, a project where margin quietly comes under pressure, a step that is left sitting without anyone raising the alarm. Admicom calculates it correctly, but it does not ring the bell. Stevin connects to it through the API or an export and turns that project data into signals with a concrete action underneath. The judgment and the execution stay with the person. Stevin only makes sure the right line surfaces in time, not at the after-the-fact costing.
admicom.stackImpact: Admicom covers the whole administrative chain, so there is little you need to add to it functionally. The gain is in the monitoring on top, not in yet another tool. The connection runs through the API or an export, and the real question is which deviations you want to see early: out-of-date estimate prices, margin pressure per project, open actions. Without something scanning for that, you lean on the monthly cycle and only see a problem once it has already cost money. That is late, and usually no longer reversible.
pitfalls: Trusting that the system surfaces deviations on its own, while they sink into the figures.
Estimating with last year's prices because no one has a signal on out-of-date lines.
Only seeing margin pressure at the after-the-fact costing, when correcting is no longer possible.
Working through open actions by hand, so dependent on whoever remembers.

adobe-analytics.shortDescription: Enterprise web analytics within Adobe Experience Cloud.
adobe-analytics.description: Adobe Analytics is the enterprise standard alongside GA4, especially within Fortune 1000 organizations already running on Adobe Experience Cloud. It offers deep segmentation, journey analysis, and connections to Adobe Target and Real-Time CDP.
adobe-analytics.useCase: Enterprise web analytics, journey analysis, and segmentation within the Adobe ecosystem.
adobe-analytics.howWeUseIt: Stevin connects Adobe Analytics to your ad channels, CDP, and MMM. We make sure segments, calculated metrics, and journey data line up with the rest of your marketing stack, not as a standalone silo.
problemsSolved: Adobe Analytics data sits apart from campaign and CRM data
Segmentation is not pushed through to advertising and email
Journey analysis stays inside Adobe and never reaches decision makers
adobe-analytics.stevinAngle: Adobe Analytics is the enterprise standard alongside GA4, especially at organizations already running on Adobe Experience Cloud. The strength is in the depth: segmentation, journey analysis, and ties to Adobe Target and the Real-Time CDP that go further than what you find in lighter tools. We use it where that depth is genuinely needed and the Adobe ecosystem is already in place. Where teams get stuck is that all that richness stays inside Adobe. The segments and calculated metrics are valuable, but they rarely get pushed through to advertising and email, and the journey analysis never reaches the decision makers who should act on it. It becomes a deep silo. Stevin runs as a layer over your stack and reads Adobe Analytics through the API, alongside your ad channels, CDP, and CRM. A segment that suddenly behaves differently or a journey that stalls somewhere then becomes a signal a person reviews, instead of insight that stays stuck in Adobe.
adobe-analytics.stackImpact: Choosing Adobe Analytics means a powerful but heavy tool that only pays off once the insights flow out to your advertising, email, and CDP layer. Count on work to push segments and journey data through, because that does not happen on its own. The data comes in through the API, so the question is not whether the analysis is deep, but whether it reaches the places where decisions get made. Without that bridge you pay for an enterprise tool whose richness stays in its own silo, far from the people and channels that should be steering with it.
pitfalls: Leaving rich segments sitting in Adobe without pushing them through to advertising and email.
Keeping journey analysis inside the ecosystem, where decision makers cannot reach it.
Reviewing Adobe data apart from your campaign and CRM data, so it becomes a silo.

adobe-creative-cloud.shortDescription: Creative production tools with AI-driven variation and optimization.
adobe-creative-cloud.description: Adobe Creative Cloud (including Photoshop, Illustrator, and Firefly) is the industry standard for creative production. Combined with AI tools like Generative Fill, it makes it possible to produce variations at speed based on data insights.
adobe-creative-cloud.useCase: Fast creative iteration based on Stevin AI briefs.
adobe-creative-cloud.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI delivers the creative brief with specific recommendations (color, composition, hook). The creative team uses Adobe tools to produce variations that get tested for effectiveness right away.
problemsSolved: The creative process is too slow for the pace of digital campaigns
Variations get made at random instead of driven by data
No link between the creative brief and the production tool
adobe-creative-cloud.stevinAngle: Adobe Creative Cloud is and remains the heaviest gear there is, and with Firefly and Generative Fill you make variants in an afternoon that used to cost a week. That is exactly what it is strong at: production. What it does not do is tell you which variant to make. Generative Fill produces what you ask for, but the direction still comes from a brief, and in practice that brief is vague or arrives too late. That is where teams get stuck: the tool moves faster than the thinking in front of it. We put Stevin as a layer in front of the creative work. Stevin reads performance from your ad channels via API, sees which hook or color scheme lands with an audience, and delivers a concrete brief underneath: make this, not that. The designer makes it in Adobe, and a person approves every brief with budget impact first.
adobe-creative-cloud.stackImpact: Choosing Adobe means you buy production power, not direction. Count on a separate source for the creative brief and a tool that links ad results per creative back to what you make, because Adobe does not know how an ad performs once it is live. The files come out of Adobe, but what goes into them comes from somewhere else. Without a layer that feeds performance back into the next round, it stays iteration on instinct. That is the gap you have to close yourself, or have closed.
pitfalls: Making variants at speed without a brief steering: lots of output, little direction.
Assuming generative AI makes the creative choice instead of executing it.
Cutting production off from performance: the lesson from one campaign never reaches the next.
Paying for Adobe licenses for team members a lighter tool would serve just as well.

adobe-experience-manager.shortDescription: Enterprise CMS and digital asset management within Adobe Experience Cloud.
adobe-experience-manager.description: Adobe Experience Manager (AEM) is an enterprise CMS and DAM platform for brands that manage content at scale across markets, languages, and channels. A standard in many Fortune 1000 marketing stacks.
adobe-experience-manager.useCase: Enterprise content management, multi-market sites, and managed personalization.
adobe-experience-manager.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI connects AEM to your tracking, CDP, and advertising channels so content variants per market are tied back to performance data and personalization is fed with first-party signals.
problemsSolved: Content variants per market are not measurably tied to campaigns
Personalization runs apart from the CDP
Multi-market content deploys have no shared measurement layer
adobe-experience-manager.stevinAngle: Adobe Experience Manager is enterprise machinery: managing content and assets across markets, languages, and channels at scale. In many large marketing stacks it is the standard, and rightly so for brands that keep hundreds of sites running. The flip side is the weight. AEM is powerful but heavy, and most teams use a fraction of what it can do. Where it goes wrong: content variants per market get rolled out without anyone tying them measurably to campaigns, personalization runs apart from the CDP, and multi-market deploys lack a shared measurement layer. You publish a lot and know little. Stevin connects to AEM through the API, ties content variants to performance data, and feeds personalization with first-party signals, so it becomes visible per market what works and the consultant reviews every change that carries weight first.
adobe-experience-manager.stackImpact: Choosing AEM is a commitment to the Adobe ecosystem and the implementation cost and maintenance load that come with it. Apart from a CDP and your advertising channels, it stays an expensive publishing machine with no feedback. Count on work to tie content variants, tracking, and personalization together, because that is not built in ready-made and needs maintenance the moment you add markets. The practical approach: get a shared measurement layer across your markets first, otherwise you roll out content without knowing which variant is worth its money.
pitfalls: Rolling out content variants per market without tying them measurably to campaigns.
Letting personalization run apart from the CDP, so signals do not come together.
Multi-market deploys with no shared measurement layer, leaving results that cannot be compared.
Paying for AEM's weight while the team uses only part of the platform.

adobe-real-time-cdp.shortDescription: Enterprise CDP from Adobe for real-time customer profiles.
adobe-real-time-cdp.description: Adobe Real-Time CDP is the customer data platform within the Adobe Experience Cloud ecosystem. It builds unified customer profiles in real time and activates them across all channels.
adobe-real-time-cdp.useCase: Building and activating real-time customer profiles across all marketing and service channels.
adobe-real-time-cdp.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI implements Adobe Real-Time CDP and makes sure customer data from all sources comes together in unified profiles that are immediately usable for personalization and campaigns.
problemsSolved: Customer data is fragmented across multiple systems
No real-time customer profiles available for personalization
Activating customer data is slow and manual
adobe-real-time-cdp.stevinAngle: Adobe Real-Time CDP builds unified customer profiles in real time and activates them across channels, and within the Adobe Experience Cloud ecosystem it does that well. For organizations already deep in Adobe it is the logical CDP, because the profiles and the activation hook into what is already there. Outside that ecosystem the complexity weighs more than it returns. Where teams get stuck: bringing fragmented data from many systems together into one profile is exactly the hard part, and the promise of real-time activation tempts you to underestimate the setup. A profile is not an action. Stevin connects to Adobe Real-Time CDP through the API, reads the unified profiles and the segment shifts, and turns them into signals with concrete follow-up, with a person seeing every change that carries weight first.
adobe-real-time-cdp.stackImpact: Choosing Adobe Real-Time CDP means, in practice, choosing the Adobe house around it, with the license and maintenance load that comes with it. Apart from the rest of Experience Cloud you lose much of the reason to be here. Count on serious setup work to bring sources together into reliable profiles, because that is not a button but a project with data engineering underneath. The practical approach: make sure the data sources are clean and connected before you expect real-time activation, otherwise you quickly activate on profiles that do not hold up.
pitfalls: Using Adobe Real-Time CDP apart from the Adobe ecosystem and missing most of the value.
Underestimating the setup of profile unification because real time sounds simple.
Activating on profiles before the underlying sources are clean.
Confusing a unified profile with an action that follows from it on its own.

adobe-target.shortDescription: Enterprise A/B testing and personalization within Adobe Experience Cloud.
adobe-target.description: Adobe Target is the enterprise standard for A/B testing, multivariate testing, and personalization. It works closely with Adobe Analytics and Real-Time CDP for data-driven experimentation at scale.
adobe-target.useCase: A/B testing, MVT, and personalization at enterprise scale.
adobe-target.howWeUseIt: Stevin connects Adobe Target to your tracking, CDP, and campaign data so experiments are fed with the right audiences and results loop back into your media mix.
problemsSolved: Experiments run apart from campaign and audience data
Personalization is not tied to first-party CDP segments
adobe-target.stevinAngle: Adobe Target is the enterprise choice for A/B testing, multivariate testing, and personalization, and it works closely with Adobe Analytics and the Real-Time CDP. The strength is experimenting at scale on data that already lives in the Adobe ecosystem. We use it where that ecosystem is in place and personalization genuinely matters. Where it pinches is that experiments and personalization are only as good as the data feeding them. In practice tests run apart from campaign and audience data: you personalize on segments that do not line up with your first-party CDP, and test results never loop back into your media mix. You optimize in a vacuum. Stevin runs as a layer over your stack and connects Target to your tracking, CDP, and campaign data, so experiments are fed with the right audiences and an outcome that matters becomes a signal a person reviews, instead of a result that stays inside Target.
adobe-target.stackImpact: Choosing Adobe Target means you have to get the right data into it, otherwise you test and personalize on segments that do not match your real first-party picture. Count on a connection to your tracking and CDP, because without it experiments run apart from your campaigns. The data and results move through the Adobe ecosystem, so the question is not whether you can test, but whether the outcomes land back in your media mix. Without that loop you optimize in a vacuum and the learnings stay inside Target, apart from the channels where they would make a difference.
pitfalls: Personalizing on segments that do not line up with your first-party CDP data.
Keeping test results inside Target without looping them back into your media mix.
Running experiments apart from campaign and audience data, so you optimize in a vacuum.

adroll.description: AdRoll offers retargeting across multiple channels, including web, social and email. It is accessible for small and mid-sized firms that want to scale up their retargeting.
adroll.useCase: Cross-channel retargeting for webshops and lead generation.
adroll.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI connects AdRoll to your webshop and analytics and makes sure retargeting audiences and conversions are tracked correctly.
problemsSolved: Retargeting runs apart from other marketing channels
No centralized overview of retargeting performance
adroll.stevinAngle: AdRoll makes cross-channel retargeting accessible for smaller firms: retargeting across web, social and email in one platform, without needing a media agency. That accessibility is the value and at the same time the limit. It is a broad layer across several channels, but it does not go deep in any of them and it does not tell you whether the spend genuinely produces extra revenue. We see small webshops stall on this: AdRoll runs along nicely, but apart from the rest of the marketing, and there is no place where its performance sits next to Google and Meta. It optimizes within itself and stops there. Stevin runs as a layer on top, connects to your webshop and analytics through the API and puts the retargeting data in the context of your other channels. It flags overlap and double-counting, and a person decides before budget moves.
adroll.stackImpact: Choosing AdRoll gives you a fast way to set up retargeting across several channels, but it quickly becomes an island next to your real advertising channels. Count on a connection with your webshop and analytics, otherwise it runs on its own and you do not know whether the budget adds anything. The data comes out through the API. The real question is whether the claimed conversions overlap with what Google and Meta were already bringing in. Without that overview you are paying three channels for the same purchase.
pitfalls: Letting retargeting run apart from Google and Meta, then you do not see the double-counting.
No central overview of performance, so budget shifts on gut feeling.
Assuming accessible also means deep, while it does not go deep in any channel.
Letting three channels claim the same purchase with nothing that strips out the overlap.

ads-and-data.shortDescription: Belgian advertising platform from DPG Media and Proximus.
ads-and-data.description: Ads & Data is a Belgian advertising platform that combines telecom data from Proximus with the media reach of DPG Media. It offers unique targeting options based on behavioral data.
ads-and-data.useCase: Data-driven advertising in Belgium with unique telecom and media data.
ads-and-data.howWeUseIt: Stevin uses Ads & Data for campaigns aimed at the Belgian market and connects the results to your total campaign reporting.
problemsSolved: Belgian audiences are hard to reach with specific targeting
No view of how Belgian media campaigns perform
ads-and-data.stevinAngle: Ads & Data is a Belgian approach that combines telecom data from Proximus with the reach of DPG Media. That gives a targeting option you will not easily find elsewhere in Belgium: behavioral data tied to large media reach. We use it for campaigns aimed specifically at the Belgian market, where that data genuinely makes a difference. Where it pinches is that the added value sits in the data, but the proof of it does not flow into your own reporting on its own. You get sharp targeting, but whether that sharpness translates into better results than a broader channel, you only see once you place it side by side. Stevin runs as a layer on top of your stack and pulls the campaign data in through export, next to your other channels. A Belgian campaign that runs notably well or poorly then becomes a signal a person reviews, so you can weigh the extra targeting against what it costs.
ads-and-data.stackImpact: Choosing Ads & Data means you want to place the results next to your other channels to see whether the telecom targeting is worth its premium. You need your media mix and analytics alongside it, because on its own sharp targeting always looks good. It is a channel for the Belgian market, so count on it standing next to your broader effort rather than replacing it. The question that remains is whether the extra data leads to better outcomes than a plain channel, and you only see that by comparing.
pitfalls: Paying for sharp targeting without checking whether it really performs better than a broader channel.
Keeping Belgian campaign data separate from your other mix, so the comparison is missing.
Assuming more data automatically leads to better results.

adverity.shortDescription: Marketing data integration and harmonization platform.
adverity.description: Adverity is a marketing data integration platform that brings together 600+ data sources, harmonizes them and pushes them on to BI tools and warehouses. Widely used by enterprise media and marketing teams.
adverity.useCase: Marketing data harmonization across markets, channels and agencies.
adverity.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI uses Adverity feeds as an alternative or complement to Fivetran when marketing sources, naming conventions and agency reporting first need to be harmonized for MMM.
problemsSolved: Marketing data from agencies and platforms is inconsistent
Naming conventions differ per market
No common measurement layer for multi-market reporting
adverity.stevinAngle: Adverity brings together 600-plus marketing sources, harmonizes them and pushes them on to BI tools and warehouses. The real work it does is not so much fetching data, but getting data from different agencies, platforms and markets onto one line before you can use it. For enterprise media teams wrestling with inconsistent naming conventions and divergent agency reporting, that is exactly the pain it removes. Where it fits less well: if your sources already come in clean and consistent, a pure ELT platform is often simpler and cheaper. Where teams get stuck is expecting harmonization to make the strategy. Adverity puts the data on a measurement layer, but what that layer tells you stays interpretation. Stevin uses Adverity feeds as a complement or alternative to Fivetran when sources first need harmonizing, reads the harmonized data and turns it into signals with follow-up, with a person reviewing every action that carries weight first.
adverity.stackImpact: Choosing Adverity pays off when harmonization is the real problem: multiple markets, agencies and platforms with divergent naming that you first have to bring onto one line. If your sources already come in consistent, a simpler ELT platform is often a better and cheaper fit. It delivers a harmonized measurement layer, no ready-made conclusions and no analysis. In practice: use Adverity for the harmonizing and build the analysis and signal layer explicitly on top, because consistent data across markets and agencies is the precondition for good reporting, not the reporting itself.
pitfalls: Deploying Adverity while your sources are already clean: you pay for harmonization you do not need.
Expecting harmonized data to lead to conclusions on its own.
Letting naming conventions differ per market despite the harmonization layer.
Building a common measurement layer without anyone pulling signals out of it.

agencyanalytics.shortDescription: Dashboard and reporting platform for agencies.
agencyanalytics.description: AgencyAnalytics is a reporting platform built specifically for marketing agencies. It combines data from more than 80 marketing channels into automated dashboards and reports for clients.
agencyanalytics.useCase: Automated client reports that combine data from every marketing channel.
agencyanalytics.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI uses AgencyAnalytics to automate client reports and bring together data from advertising, SEO and social channels into clear dashboards.
problemsSolved: Reports take too much time to put together manually
Clients have no central overview of their marketing performance
Data from different channels is not combined
agencyanalytics.stevinAngle: AgencyAnalytics is built for a specific problem and solves it well: putting together client reports without an agency losing hours on it every month. Many channels in it, tidy templates, done. We use it for agency clients who want to send a polished report fast. Where it pinches is that it reports what already happened, and that is where it stops. The nice monthly report tells the client neatly that a campaign declined, a week after it should have. AgencyAnalytics brings the data together, but it does not look ahead and it does nothing. That is exactly the layer Stevin adds on top. Through the same channel data, Stevin reads along and raises a signal the moment something turns, not at month end but in the moment itself, with the follow-up underneath and a person reviewing every action that carries weight first.
agencyanalytics.stackImpact: AgencyAnalytics covers reporting broadly, but it is not a place where work originates: it shows, it does not steer. Count on it living alongside your advertising, SEO and social sources and bringing them together neatly at fixed moments, but the action that follows from a deviation is not in it and it does not look ahead. In practice: use it to show the client what happened, and put something next to it that notices what is going on now, in the moment itself. A monthly report is a look back, not an early warning, and that difference decides whether you intervene in time.
pitfalls: Confusing a monthly report with intervening in time: the signal comes too late.
Assuming combined data equals follow-up.
Keeping refining templates while nobody reacts to the numbers.
Only looking back and missing ongoing deviations as a result.

ahrefs.shortDescription: Backlink analysis and SEO tool suite.
ahrefs.description: Ahrefs is one of the most extensive SEO tools, particularly strong in backlink analysis, keyword research and content analysis.
ahrefs.useCase: Backlink analysis, keyword research and technical SEO audits.
ahrefs.howWeUseIt: Stevin uses Ahrefs for technical SEO audits and backlink analysis as part of a broader marketing strategy.
problemsSolved: No view of the backlink profile
Technical SEO issues stay unnoticed
ahrefs.stevinAngle: Ahrefs is one of the strongest SEO tools, particularly in backlink analysis where few packages come close. For mapping your link profile and running technical audits, it is what we reach for. The depth on backlinks is the real reason to choose it. Where it pinches is the same as with other SEO suites: it is a research source you have to keep consulting yourself. A lost backlink from a strong site, a technical problem that surfaces after a release: Ahrefs sees it, but does not act and does not warn on its own. The data stays in the tool until someone looks. Stevin runs as a layer on top of your stack and reads Ahrefs through the API, so that the development of your link profile and your technical health gets tracked. A notable drop in referring domains or a new audit issue then becomes a signal a person reviews, instead of something you only find at the next manual check.
ahrefs.stackImpact: Choosing Ahrefs means you have a strong research source, but you have to dig into it yourself to get anything out of it. Count on the value depending on how often someone looks. The data comes in through the API, so the question is not whether you can see your backlinks and audits, but whether someone picks up the changes that matter. Without a layer that tracks the link profile and the technical state, Ahrefs stays a deep report you consult occasionally, while a lost link or a new problem stays unnoticed until you happen to look for it.
pitfalls: Only consulting Ahrefs manually, so changes between checks slip away.
Only noticing a lost backlink from a strong site once the effect is already visible.
Not picking up technical audit issues after a release because nothing points to them.

aircall.shortDescription: Cloud telephony integrated with your CRM.
aircall.description: Aircall is a cloud-based phone system that integrates with your CRM. Ideal for sales teams that follow up on leads by phone.
aircall.useCase: Phone-based lead follow-up with CRM integration.
aircall.howWeUseIt: Stevin connects Aircall to your CRM so call history, notes, and outcomes are logged automatically on the right contact.
problemsSolved: Call notes are not saved to the CRM automatically
No view of phone follow-up on leads
aircall.stevinAngle: Aircall handles cloud telephony cleanly and connects to your CRM, so call history, notes, and outcomes land on the right contact automatically. For sales teams that follow up on leads by phone, that saves the manual searching and retyping, and that is exactly what we use it for. Here is the limit: Aircall logs the call, but it does not think about what should happen next. The note sits neatly on the contact, and then it goes quiet. A logged call is not follow-up, and anyone who confuses the two leaves value on the table. Where teams get stuck is exactly that: call notes that get saved but never lead to a next action, and no view of phone follow-up as a whole. Stevin connects to Aircall through the API, reads the calls, and turns them into a draft and a signal: a lead who asked for a next step, a promise that needs keeping. The person sees every action that carries weight first.
aircall.stackImpact: Choosing Aircall means you hang telephony neatly off your CRM, but logging a call is not yet follow-up. Count on a layer that turns the calls into actions, because Aircall stores and stops there, it does not draft anything or queue a next step. For a team that barely calls it is overkill, the value is in phone-based lead follow-up and that has to genuinely happen to justify the cost. In practice: let Aircall do the calling and logging and put intelligence on top that decides what should happen after the call.
pitfalls: Assuming a logged call is the same as follow-up.
Letting call notes pile up without anyone turning them into a next action.
Choosing Aircall for a team that barely calls: the core function then sits idle.
Losing sight of phone follow-up as a whole because the data stays scattered.

albert-heijn-retail-media-services.shortDescription: Retail media advertising on Albert Heijn channels.
albert-heijn-retail-media-services.description: Albert Heijn Retail Media Services lets advertisers reach audiences through Albert Heijn's digital channels. From sponsored products in the app to display on ah.nl.
albert-heijn-retail-media-services.useCase: Growing product visibility and conversion through Albert Heijn's digital channels.
albert-heijn-retail-media-services.howWeUseIt: Stevin integrates Albert Heijn Retail Media into your media plan and reporting so that retail media results become part of your total campaign view.
problemsSolved: Retail media at Albert Heijn is not included in your total reporting
No comparison possible between retail media and other channels
albert-heijn-retail-media-services.stevinAngle: Albert Heijn Retail Media brings you to shoppers in the app and on ah.nl, close to the purchase moment at one of the best-known retailers in the Netherlands. For brands that want to sit on that shelf, that is strong: you reach people who are already doing their shopping. We use it where the audience genuinely shops at AH, not as general awareness. Where teams get stuck is that retail media at AH is its own environment with its own reporting, separate from the rest of your media. You see what a campaign did inside AH, but not how that compares to your other channels or what it adds to your total picture. Stevin runs as a layer on top of your stack and pulls the AH data in through export, so that results stand next to your other channels. A shift in performance or spend then becomes a signal a person reviews, not a loose figure in a dashboard nobody opens.
albert-heijn-retail-media-services.stackImpact: Choosing retail media at AH means you want to place the figures next to your other channels, because inside AH alone they lack the comparison. You need your media mix and reporting alongside it to see whether the euro works better here than elsewhere. The danger is that AH becomes a separate report that lives next to the rest. In practice: pull the data out and place it in the same view as your other spend, otherwise you cannot fairly weigh retail media against everything else you do.
pitfalls: Leaving AH results in their own report without comparison to other channels.
Using retail media as broad awareness when the strength sits in the purchase moment.
Being unable to weigh whether the euro works better at AH than elsewhere in your mix.

amazon.description: Amazon is the largest ecommerce platform in the world. For many brands an essential sales channel that needs to be integrated well with the rest of their marketing.
amazon.useCase: Selling through Amazon, integrated into your marketing stack.
amazon.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI connects Amazon sales data to your dashboards and marketing reporting for a complete multichannel picture.
problemsSolved: Amazon data is not connected to your marketing reporting
No overview across all sales channels
amazon.stevinAngle: Amazon is the largest ecommerce platform in the world and for many brands a channel you do not leave alone. That is the reality and at the same time the discomfort: you sell in someone else's house, with data that stays inside Amazon and rules that Amazon sets. We run into it at brands where Amazon drives a serious part of revenue, alongside their own shop. Where teams get stuck is the overview: the Amazon sales sit apart from the rest of the marketing data, so you never have a complete picture of your revenue and your media spend. Stevin adds a layer on top, pulls the sales data out of Amazon through the connection, and brings it together with your other channels in your dashboards, so a person sees what is going on and where it chafes in one place.
amazon.stackImpact: Choosing Amazon as a channel means part of your revenue runs on someone else's platform: the data sits in Amazon and has to come out to sit next to your own channels. Count on a connection to get the sales data into your reporting, otherwise Amazon stays a separate world. It is a sales channel, not a marketing stack, so integrating it into your total picture is your work. The question is not whether Amazon delivers revenue, but whether you can weigh it next to your other channels.
pitfalls: Keeping Amazon data separate from your other channels, so your multichannel picture stays incomplete.
Becoming too dependent on a channel you do not own and where the rules can change.
Not making a connection, so Amazon revenue falls outside your marketing reporting.

amazon-ads.shortDescription: Sponsored Products, Brands and Display within the Amazon ecosystem.
amazon-ads.description: Amazon Ads is the advertising platform for brands that sell on Amazon. Sponsored Products, Sponsored Brands and Sponsored Display drive purchase intent directly within the marketplace ecosystem and are essential for retail and CPG brands.
amazon-ads.useCase: Growing product visibility, conversion and share of shelf on Amazon.
amazon-ads.howWeUseIt: Stevin integrates Amazon Ads with your product feeds, inventory and MMM. We connect on-Amazon performance to your full media mix so you know how Amazon Ads contributes to incremental revenue and not just to ACoS.
problemsSolved: Amazon spend gets judged apart from the rest of the media mix
No link between inventory, feed and campaigns
ACoS steers on a platform KPI, not on brand-wide profitability
amazon-ads.stevinAngle: Amazon Ads is indispensable if you sell on Amazon: Sponsored Products, Brands and Display drive purchase intent directly in the marketplace, exactly where people are already buying. For retail and CPG brands, that is not an option but a given. We use it where Amazon is a real sales channel and not a side effect. Where it pinches is that Amazon is its own world with its own KPI, ACoS, which says nothing about your brand-wide profitability. And the spend is rarely placed next to your inventory or your other media, while those three have everything to do with each other. Stevin runs as a layer on top of your stack and pulls the Amazon data in through the API, next to your feeds, inventory and media mix. A campaign that keeps running on a product that is nearly out, or spend that drifts away without return: that becomes a signal a person sees in time, instead of something ACoS hides.
amazon-ads.stackImpact: Choosing Amazon Ads means you want to connect your product feed, inventory and campaigns, because steered separately they work against each other. You need your inventory data and your broader media mix alongside it to weigh fairly. The risk is that Amazon becomes an island with its own success figure that nobody places next to the rest. In practice: make sure feed, inventory and spend come into one picture, otherwise you steer on ACoS and not on what your brand keeps, and Amazon stays separate from your real media decisions.
pitfalls: Steering on ACoS when it says nothing about your brand-wide profitability.
Decoupling inventory and campaigns, so you keep paying for a product that is nearly out.
Judging Amazon spend apart from the rest of your media mix.

amazon-dsp.shortDescription: Programmatic display and video within the Amazon ecosystem.
amazon-dsp.description: Amazon DSP is Amazon's programmatic platform, giving access to first-party retail data for display, video and audio, both on and off Amazon. Strong for retail and CPG brands that want to target on purchase intent.
amazon-dsp.useCase: Programmatic targeting based on Amazon purchase behavior, on and off Amazon.
amazon-dsp.howWeUseIt: Stevin uses Amazon DSP as part of a combined retail media strategy and connects the results to your MMM and attribution model.
problemsSolved: No access to Amazon purchase data for upper funnel campaigns
Retail media is not measured as a whole
amazon-dsp.stevinAngle: Amazon DSP opens up Amazon's purchase data for programmatic display, video and audio, including off Amazon itself. For retail and CPG brands, that is the appeal: targeting on real purchase behavior instead of a proxy. We use it as part of a retail media strategy where that purchase data makes a difference. Where teams get stuck is measurement at the top of the funnel. DSP reaches people before they search, but that contribution cannot be captured in a last click, and the results easily stay inside Amazon, separate from your other attribution. It becomes an upper-funnel spend whose effect you assume. That is where Stevin sits. As a layer on top of your stack, Stevin reads the DSP data through the API, next to your other channels, so that a move in traffic or conversion after a flight becomes a signal a person reviews, instead of a figure that stays in the Amazon dashboard.
amazon-dsp.stackImpact: Choosing Amazon DSP means you want to pull the results out of Amazon and place them next to your other channels, because at the top of the funnel a platform figure on its own says little. You need your other media mix and analytics alongside it to weigh the contribution. The danger is that DSP becomes an upper-funnel island separate from the rest of your attribution. The question is not whether you can use the purchase data, but whether someone sees the effect next to your other channels, otherwise you pay for reach you cannot prove.
pitfalls: Judging upper-funnel DSP reach on a last click that misses the effect.
Leaving results inside Amazon, separate from your broader attribution.
Assuming access to purchase data turns into incremental revenue on its own.

amperity.description: Amperity is a CDP that uses AI for identity resolution and building accurate customer profiles. The platform ties data from all sources to the right customer, even without deterministic identifiers.
amperity.useCase: AI-driven customer identification and profile enrichment across all data sources.
amperity.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI implements Amperity for organizations that struggle to tie customer data from multiple sources together and want to build accurate customer profiles.
problemsSolved: Customer data from different sources cannot be tied to the same customer
Duplicate customer profiles disrupt segmentation and reporting
amperity.stevinAngle: Amperity uses AI for identity resolution, and that is exactly where it sets itself apart: tying data from different sources to the same customer, even without hard identifiers. For organizations struggling with duplicate profiles and fragmented customer data, it solves a real problem that deterministic matching leaves behind. The flip side of probabilistic matching is that it is not infallible: the AI guesses well, but a guess stays a guess, and you have to be able to trust the matches before you steer on them. Where teams get stuck is the assumption that clean profiles automatically become good marketing. An accurate profile is a starting point, not an action. Stevin connects to Amperity, reads the resolved profiles and the segments, and turns them into signals with follow-up underneath, with a person seeing every change that carries weight first.
amperity.stackImpact: Choosing Amperity solves an identity problem that many CDPs sidestep, and that is the reason to pay the premium here. If you do not have that problem, a simpler CDP is enough. Count on a phase where you validate the matching quality before you build on it. The practical approach: do not trust the resolved profiles blindly, check the matches, and make sure there is a layer on top that turns the clean profiles into action instead of just storing them neatly.
pitfalls: Trusting probabilistic matches blindly without validating the quality.
Choosing Amperity without a real identity problem: you pay for resolution you do not need.
Confusing an accurate profile with a marketing action that follows from it on its own.
Assuming deduplicated profiles automatically deliver better segmentation without follow-up.

amplitude.shortDescription: Digital analytics platform for product and customer journey analysis.
amplitude.description: Amplitude is an enterprise product analytics platform with a strong focus on behavioral cohorts, predictive analysis, and cross-platform journeys. Widely used in B2B SaaS and consumer apps.
amplitude.useCase: Behavioral analytics, predictive cohorts, and journey optimization.
amplitude.howWeUseIt: Stevin integrates Amplitude with your CDP, CRM, and ad channels so behavioral cohorts are directly activatable in campaigns and lifecycle marketing.
problemsSolved: Behavioral cohorts are not activatable in advertising
Product data does not reach CRM and marketing
amplitude.stevinAngle: Amplitude is product analytics built specifically for SaaS and digital products, not for marketing. For brands looking at whether customers move through conversion funnels, build retention, and adopt features, this is the tool. For anyone who wants marketing attribution, GA4 or Mixpanel is a better fit. We see teams buy Amplitude because 'it is better than GA4' without realizing it is a product tool, not a marketing tool. The free tier is generous up to 10M events a month, so testing costs nothing.
amplitude.stackImpact: For your stack: treat Amplitude as the place where product data lives, not marketing data. Send events through the SDK directly from your app or website, with user_id tied to your auth system. Combine it with Segment or Rudderstack if you want to send events to multiple destinations. Avoid double tracking through GTM and the Amplitude SDK, that creates drift in the numbers.
pitfalls: Tracking events without a schema document, within 6 months you have 'button_clicked' in 50 different ways
Building charts without cohort segmentation, the average hides that power users pull everything
Connecting Amplitude to marketing attribution without realizing platform data on conversions does not sit there
Crossing the pricing tier without an alert, the Amplitude bill can climb unexpectedly when events explode

apple-music-for-artists.shortDescription: Streaming analytics, Shazam data, and playlist performance.
apple-music-for-artists.description: Apple Music gives access to detailed streaming data, including Shazam recognitions. A crucial channel to monitor alongside Spotify for a complete picture of your music performance.
apple-music-for-artists.useCase: Cross-platform streaming analysis and Shazam discovery tracking.
apple-music-for-artists.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI combines Apple Music data with Spotify and other platforms to give a total picture of your streaming performance per track, per region.
problemsSolved: Streaming data is spread across multiple platforms
No total overview of your music performance
Shazam spikes are not tied to marketing moments
apple-music-for-artists.stevinAngle: Apple Music for Artists is the source artists skip too often, and that is exactly why it is valuable: detailed streaming data plus Shazam recognitions, a discovery signal you get nowhere else quite like this. We monitor it alongside Spotify because a one-sided picture pulls your strategy off balance. Where it gets tight is that it is its own island. The numbers sit apart from Spotify and from your social, and a Shazam spike, which usually means people hear a track somewhere and want to know what it is, stays a loose value that no one ties to a moment. The platform does not draw that link. Stevin runs on top and combines Apple Music with Spotify and your other sources into a total picture per track and per region, and ties a Shazam spike to the marketing moment behind it, with a signal and a person reviewing anything that carries weight first.
apple-music-for-artists.stackImpact: Adding Apple Music means lining up two streaming sources side by side instead of leaning on one, otherwise you miss half your audience. Count on a connection that brings Apple Music and Spotify together, because each platform reports in its own corner. In practice: treat Shazam as a discovery signal, not noise, and make sure you can map it back onto your promotion. The question that remains is what you do with a spike you see in a loose dashboard but cannot tie to anything.
pitfalls: Steering on Spotify alone and missing half your listeners.
Leaving a Shazam spike as a loose value instead of a discovery signal.
Keeping streaming data separate per platform instead of bringing it together.
Assuming two dashboards side by side add up to a total picture.

appsflyer.shortDescription: Mobile measurement partner for app attribution and deep linking.
appsflyer.description: AppsFlyer is the global leader in mobile measurement. It measures app installs, in-app events, and multi-touch attribution for mobile campaigns, including SKAdNetwork for iOS and deep linking.
appsflyer.useCase: Mobile attribution, SKAdNetwork measurement, and deep linking for app campaigns.
appsflyer.howWeUseIt: Stevin integrates AppsFlyer with your media mix and MMM so mobile and web are viewed in one model, not as separate silos.
problemsSolved: App installs and web conversions are measured separately
iOS attribution through SKAN is incomplete
Deep linking is not tied to campaigns
appsflyer.stevinAngle: AppsFlyer is the standard in mobile measurement, and for good reason: it measures installs, in-app events, and multi-touch attribution in a way web tools simply cannot reach. For app-driven clients we recommend it over generic tracking that treats mobile as an afterthought. Honest about the pain: since iOS closed off the cookie, a lot of attribution leans on SKAdNetwork, and that is fundamentally coarser and slower than what marketers are used to. AppsFlyer makes the best of it, but it does not conjure certainty where Apple took it away. Where teams get stuck is that app data and web data stay two separate worlds, with double counts and gaps at the crossover. Stevin pulls the AppsFlyer data through the API into your broader media picture, puts web and app into one story, and flags when a campaign underperforms before it shows up in the monthly report. The person sees every adjustment first.
appsflyer.stackImpact: Choosing AppsFlyer means you take mobile measurement seriously, but also that you buy the limits of SKAdNetwork along with it: incomplete iOS data is not a setup error, it is built in. You need something that views app and web measurement in one model, otherwise you judge two silos apart from each other and count conversions twice or miss them. In practice: let AppsFlyer do the mobile measurement and put a layer on top that ties it to the rest of your media, so you steer across the whole journey rather than per channel.
pitfalls: Keeping app installs and web conversions measured apart: you double count or miss the crossover.
Treating SKAdNetwork data as complete while iOS has deliberately made the measurement coarser.
Setting up deep linking without tying it to the campaigns that drive the traffic.
Thinking a mobile measurement partner also makes your cross-channel decisions.

attention-insight.shortDescription: AI-generated attention heatmaps for ads and landing pages.
attention-insight.description: Attention Insight uses AI to predict where users look on a page or ad. No eye-tracking lab needed: upload your design and get a heatmap with attention distribution within seconds.
attention-insight.useCase: Quick validation of visual hierarchy in ads and landing pages.
attention-insight.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI uses Attention Insight to automatically check whether the CTA, the product, and the brand get the right attention in new creatives. Problems get flagged before the ad goes live.
problemsSolved: No quick way to check whether an ad is visually effective
CTAs and product images get overshadowed by distracting elements
Eye-tracking research is too slow and too expensive for iterative creative work
attention-insight.stevinAngle: Attention Insight does what used to need an eye-tracking lab, but in seconds: upload a design and you get an AI-predicted heatmap of where attention goes. For iterative creative work that is the real win, because you can check ten variants in the time a real study takes just to set up. One thing to stay honest about: it is a prediction based on patterns, not a measurement of real users. That makes it strong for catching clear misses early, a CTA that disappears, a product image that gets buried, and weaker if you treat it as hard proof. Stevin uses Attention Insight to automatically check whether the CTA, the product, and the brand get the right attention in a new creative. Problems get flagged before the ad goes live, and you see that check before media budget goes behind it.
attention-insight.stackImpact: Attention Insight gives you a predicted heatmap, fast and cheap, but it is a model trained on patterns, not a real user measurement, so treat it as a first filter and not as proof. It works on your designs, so the gain is in using it early and often while you iterate. On its own a heatmap is a snapshot with no validation afterward. In practice: use it to pull clear misses out of the visual hierarchy before an ad goes live and let real user data give the final confirmation, so you gain speed without confusing the prediction with reality.
pitfalls: Taking the predicted heatmap as a hard measurement instead of a first filter.
Only applying it to the final version, when the gain is in fast iteration.
Not laying real campaign data next to it to confirm or disprove the prediction.

attio.shortDescription: Modern, AI-native CRM you shape yourself.
attio.description: Attio is a modern CRM with a flexible data model: you build your own objects, lists, and relationships. Strong as a system of record, with an open API, webhooks, and a native MCP layer, but it leaves the smart follow-up to you.
attio.useCase: A clean, flexible CRM foundation for teams that want to bring their own automation on top.
attio.howWeUseIt: Stevin runs as a work layer over Attio. Through the API, webhooks, and the native MCP layer, Stevin reads contacts, pipeline, and activity and turns loose data into signals and concrete follow-up: a lead that goes quiet, a quote left sitting, a conversation asking for a next step. Attio holds the data, Stevin delivers the intelligence and the action on top.
problemsSolved: Attio is a strong database but weak at outbound automation
Follow-up and sequences take handwork
Call recordings and emails do not land on the right contact on their own
attio.stevinAngle: Attio sells itself as AI-native, but in practice the smart part is mostly autocomplete and enrichment. The follow-up it deliberately leaves to you. So we use Attio where it is genuinely strong: as a clean, flexible system of record. The difference for us is the native MCP layer. It lets Stevin read your pipeline and write back without the brittle field mappings you keep fighting with on older CRMs. Where teams get stuck is expecting Attio to chase deals. It does not. A lead that goes quiet, a quote left sitting, a conversation asking for a next step: Attio records it, but acts on nothing. That is exactly the layer Stevin adds on top, with a person reviewing every action that carries weight first.
attio.stackImpact: Choosing Attio means you build the automation on top yourself, or have it built. Count on a calling or email tool alongside it and a source for call recordings, because those do not sit in Attio itself. The open API and webhooks make the data flow clean, so the real question is not whether your data comes out, but what happens once a webhook fires. Without something reacting to it, nothing moves.
pitfalls: Building too many custom objects before you know your own process, cleaning up afterward is expensive.
Expecting AI-native to mean it follows up on its own.
Webhooks that fire without anything downstream listening.

faqs.question: Does Stevin replace Attio?
faqs.answer: No. Attio stays your CRM, Stevin is the AI layer on top that flags issues and follows up. We connect through the API, webhooks and the MCP layer.

axeptio.shortDescription: Consent management focused on design and conversion.
axeptio.description: Axeptio is a consent management platform that stands out with attractive design and high opt-in rates. It creates consent banners that match your brand identity.
axeptio.useCase: Consent management with optimized design for higher opt-in rates.
axeptio.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI implements Axeptio with a consent banner that matches your brand and connects it to Google Consent Mode for optimal data quality.
problemsSolved: Consent banner does not match the brand identity
Low opt-in rates from generic consent banners
axeptio.stevinAngle: Axeptio deliberately does something different from the rest: it makes the consent banner part of your brand instead of a gray legal pop-up, and that lifts the opt-in. We choose it for clients where the first impression counts and a standard banner just does not fit the site. The flip side is that design draws the attention and the technology behind it can suffer for it. A banner that looks good but does not pass the consent correctly to your tags still produces data loss, except nobody sees it right away. That is where the pitfall sits: looking good and working are not the same thing. Stevin runs on top of the consent status from Axeptio and your tag data, and flags when a choice does not come through or measurement drops out. That way the difference between a tidy opt-in and usable data stays visible, with a person checking the correction before a month of data goes crooked.
axeptio.stackImpact: Axeptio delivers the design and the opt-in, but you still need a tag manager and a correct Consent Mode connection to actually use the consent. The gain is in a banner that fits and converts, the risk is in a form that overshadows the technology. In practice: make the banner nice and in the same pass check whether the consent actually lands at your tags. Otherwise you run a handsome opt-in on data that still does not come through, and that only shows up when your numbers do not add up.
pitfalls: Making the banner nice but not testing the connection to your tags.
Confusing design with measurement that really works.
Assuming a high opt-in without checking whether consent comes through.
Adding tags that do not follow the banner's consent logic.

azerion.shortDescription: European digital entertainment and advertising platform.
azerion.description: Azerion is a European platform for digital advertising and gaming. It gives access to display, video and in-game ads across a broad network of entertainment and news sites.
azerion.useCase: Digital advertising through display, video and in-game formats at European scale.
azerion.howWeUseIt: Stevin uses Azerion for display and video campaigns and makes sure the results get integrated into your full media reporting.
problemsSolved: Display campaigns sit apart from performance channels
No centralized view across all media channels
azerion.stevinAngle: Azerion is a European alternative to the big display and video networks, with its own twist: gaming and in-game inventory you cannot buy as easily elsewhere. We use it with clients who want broad reach in a European context and do not want to run everything through the American players. Where it pinches is measurement. The inventory is diverse, from news sites to games, and that makes it hard to see what an impression actually delivered. Teams get stuck on reporting that sits apart from the rest of their channels, so it stays a guess whether that display euro contributes. That is where Stevin sits. As a layer on top of your stack, Stevin reads the campaign data through export or API and places it next to your performance figures, so that a deviation in reach or spend becomes a signal a person reviews, not a row in a separate dashboard.
azerion.stackImpact: Choosing Azerion means you need a measurement layer alongside it, because the platform gives you reach but not the link to conversion on its own. Count on your own tracking and analytics next to it to see what it does at the top of the funnel. The data comes in through export or API, so the real question is not whether you get figures out, but whether someone places them next to your other channels. Without that comparison, display stays a spend whose effect you assume rather than see.
pitfalls: Buying display reach without a place where it stands next to your performance channels.
Assuming in-game and news inventory measure the same way: the context differs sharply.
Leaving reporting in a separate dashboard, so nobody really judges the contribution.

bandsintown.shortDescription: Fan tracking, tour alerts, and concert demand analytics.
bandsintown.description: Bandsintown offers direct access to fan tracking data. How many fans follow you in which city? Where is the most demand for a show?
bandsintown.useCase: Fan demand analysis and tour marketing.
bandsintown.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI combines Bandsintown fan data with Spotify listeners per region and social media growth for data-driven tour planning.
problemsSolved: Fan demand data is not combined with streaming and social data
Tour marketing is not geo-targeted on current fan data
bandsintown.stevinAngle: Bandsintown gives you something rarely this direct: fans who actively follow you, per city. Not a derived estimate but a counter of people who want a heads-up when you play nearby. For tour decisions that is a stronger foundation than general streaming numbers, because it is intent, not listening behavior. The weakness is the isolation. That follower data sits apart from your Spotify listeners per region and apart from your social growth, even though it is the combination that shows where a show truly lands. Viewed separately, each number tells only half a story. Stevin combines the Bandsintown data with your streaming and social signals per region, so a city where all the lines converge comes forward as a candidate for a geo-targeted campaign or show. You see the recommendation first, the decision stays with you.
bandsintown.stackImpact: Bandsintown delivers fan tracking per city, but that number only becomes convincing next to your streaming listeners and social growth in the same region, so you need those sources. On its own it measures intent with no context: lots of trackers but few listeners in a city calls for an explanation. The real work is lining it up per region. In practice: use Bandsintown as one of your geo-signals and let a layer on top surface the cities where fans, streams, and social climb at once, so your tour and ad decisions rest on coherence instead of a single channel.
pitfalls: Taking trackers per city as truth without laying your streaming and social data alongside it.
Basing geo-targeting on a single source, so you miss the real picture.
Not translating fan demand into a concrete campaign or show at the right moment.

beatport.shortDescription: Chart positions, sales data, and genre rankings.
beatport.description: Beatport is the largest digital music store for electronic music. Chart positions and sales data are direct indicators of your commercial relevance in the scene.
beatport.useCase: Monitoring chart performance and sales trends per track and genre.
beatport.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI monitors your Beatport rankings and correlates spikes with your marketing activity and release strategy.
problemsSolved: No automatic overview of your chart positions over time
Sales data sits apart from your promotional efforts
beatport.stevinAngle: For electronic music, Beatport is where it counts commercially: chart positions, sales, and genre rankings are a direct gauge of your relevance in the scene, harder than streams alone. We monitor it because a strong placement here opens doors a Spotify number does not. Where it gets tight is that Beatport gives a snapshot with no memory and no context. You see your position today, but the trend over time and the link to your promotion you have to bring yourself, and sales sit apart from whatever you did to earn them. The platform does not lay that out for you. Stevin runs on top, keeps your rankings over time, and correlates spikes with your release strategy and marketing activity, so a rise or a fall becomes a signal with follow-up underneath, and a person reviewing anything that carries weight first.
beatport.stackImpact: Adding Beatport means you have a commercial signal that sits apart from your streaming and social data. Count on a way to capture the rankings over time, because the platform does not keep the trend for you and a loose snapshot says little. In practice: line your chart positions up against your release and promotion calendar, otherwise you know where you stand but not why. The question that remains is what caused a spike or a dip, because without that link you cannot repeat a strong placement.
pitfalls: Confusing a snapshot of your position with insight into the trend.
Keeping sales data separate from the promotion that produced it.
Not keeping a history, which leaves trends invisible.
Not being able to map a ranking spike back onto a release or campaign.

bigcommerce.shortDescription: Scalable ecommerce platform for growing webshops.
bigcommerce.description: BigCommerce offers a scalable ecommerce platform with built-in features and a broad API.
bigcommerce.useCase: Scalable ecommerce with strong API integrations.
bigcommerce.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI connects BigCommerce to your full marketing stack through API links and standard integrations.
problemsSolved: Ecommerce data never reaches the marketing tools
Integrations are not set up well
bigcommerce.stevinAngle: BigCommerce is a scalable ecommerce platform with a lot of built-in features and a strong API. In practice that is pleasant: less reliance on plugins than WordPress shops, and integrations that run solidly through the API. We use it for growing webshops that want to scale up without landing straight in Magento-level complexity. Where teams get stuck is not the technology but the setup: the standard integrations are there, but whether they actually connect to your marketing stack is another matter. Ecommerce data often never reaches the marketing tools unless someone wires the connection properly. Stevin adds a layer on top, reads order and product data through the API, and turns anything that looks off into concrete follow-up, a feed that has drifted or an order that is not coming through, with a person reviewing every action that carries weight first.
bigcommerce.stackImpact: Choosing BigCommerce means you get a solid API and built-in features, so you lean less on loose plugins than on other platforms. Do count on setting up the integrations: they exist, but they do not connect to your marketing stack on their own. The practical approach: use the API links where you can and check that the ecommerce data actually comes through. The question is not whether it scales, but whether the data ends up where you need it.
pitfalls: Assuming the standard integrations connect to your stack by themselves.
Leaving ecommerce data sitting in BigCommerce without it reaching the marketing tools.
Not using the API and falling back on copying data over by hand.

bigquery.shortDescription: Google's serverless data warehouse for analysis.
bigquery.description: BigQuery is Google's cloud data warehouse. It offers blazing-fast analysis over large datasets and integrates tightly with the Google ecosystem.
bigquery.useCase: Central data storage and analysis for marketing and business intelligence.
bigquery.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI uses BigQuery as the central data hub where marketing, sales, and website data come together. We build queries and models that help you make better decisions.
problemsSolved: Data is spread across too many tools
Analyses are too slow or too limited
No way to combine data from different sources
bigquery.stevinAngle: BigQuery is not an analytics tool, it is a data warehouse. It gets sold as 'for data analysts,' but the practical value for marketing sits in one thing: you can join GA4 data, CRM data, ad-spend data, and business data in queries you cannot run anywhere else. We connect GA4 to BigQuery as standard (free for most accounts, costs cents per query) and build the real attribution questions on top of that. Without BigQuery you work in separate silos; with it you work in a SQL layer.
bigquery.stackImpact: For your stack: GA4 export to BigQuery daily (free up to 1M events per day), exports from Stripe, HubSpot, or Salesforce through Fivetran or Airbyte, and visualization through Looker Studio or Metabase. Storage is cheap (cents per GB), queries only cost money on large scans. Do the math up front: complex joins on 100GB or more run toward 5 to 20 euros per query, so optimize with partitioning and clustering.
pitfalls: Running SELECT * on large tables, an accidental query can cost 50 euros or more
No partitioning on date fields, query costs explode on historical analyses
Letting Looker Studio query live BigQuery directly, dashboards get slow and costly, better through materialized views
Not giving service accounts scoped permissions, a compromised key can export your whole warehouse

bird.shortDescription: Cloud communication platform for email, SMS, and messaging.
bird.description: Bird (formerly MessageBird) is a cloud communication platform that combines email, SMS, WhatsApp, and voice. It offers API-driven communication and marketing automation for companies that want to communicate at scale.
bird.useCase: Omnichannel communication via email, SMS, and messaging at scale.
bird.howWeUseIt: Stevin integrates Bird into your marketing stack for automated communication across multiple channels, connected to your CRM and campaign data.
problemsSolved: Communication channels are fragmented across multiple tools
No scalable solution for omnichannel messaging
Messaging is not connected to marketing automation
bird.stevinAngle: Bird, formerly MessageBird, is API-first: email, SMS, WhatsApp, and voice that you tie together through an API and run at scale. That is exactly the strength and at the same time the trap. For teams with development capacity that genuinely want to build omnichannel, it is flexible. For a marketing team that expects a ready-made platform, it feels like a set of building blocks without a house around them. We use Bird where the communication has to run at volume and the connections are custom work. Where it pinches is that the channels stand apart until someone connects them. Stevin puts a layer over that, connects Bird to your CRM and campaign data, and makes sure an incoming signal leads to the right automated follow-up, with a person reviewing every action that carries weight first.
bird.stackImpact: Choosing Bird means you build the orchestration on top yourself, or have it built: it supplies the channels and the API, not the ready-made process. Count on development work to hang email, SMS, and WhatsApp off your CRM and automation. It covers multiple channels, so you do not need a separate tool per channel, but the cohesion is yours to organize. Without something that reacts to the incoming messages, they stay loose channels.
pitfalls: Choosing Bird without development capacity: the API building blocks sit idle without someone to connect them.
Running channels in isolation, so no coherent picture of the customer forms.
Expecting omnichannel to work out of the box instead of as a custom connection.

bloomreach.shortDescription: CDP and personalization platform for ecommerce.
bloomreach.description: Bloomreach combines a CDP with personalization and marketing automation. Strongly focused on ecommerce and personalized customer experiences.
bloomreach.useCase: Personalized ecommerce experiences based on customer data.
bloomreach.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI implements Bloomreach and connects it to your shop and marketing channels for data-driven personalization.
problemsSolved: The customer experience is not personalized
Customer data is not used for marketing
bloomreach.stevinAngle: Bloomreach is a CDP with personalization and marketing automation attached, and it is at its strongest in ecommerce. For webshops that want to turn customer data into targeted experiences it is a logical choice, because those three functions in one platform save connecting work.
