dragonfly-ai.stackImpact: Dragonfly gives you a uniform attention metric across digital and physical, which is rare, but it measures attention and not revenue. Count on a link with your sales and campaign data to give the heatmaps meaning, and on someone who weighs whether the attention also leads to a purchase, otherwise you optimize for standing out instead of for results. The analysis is cross-channel, so the gain is in connecting that one metric with what actually happens after the attention. Without that bridge it stays a pretty map with no outcome.
pitfalls: Confusing attention with effect: a heatmap says nothing about a purchase.
Optimizing for standing out instead of for results.
Not linking the saliency scores to your sales or campaign data.
Using the tool where the visual impact reaches no further than the screen.

drupal.description: Drupal is a powerful open-source CMS for complex websites with high demands on security, scalability, and customization.
drupal.useCase: Enterprise websites with complex content and user management.
drupal.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI handles correct tracking implementation and CRM connections on Drupal sites.
problemsSolved: Drupal integrations require technical expertise
Tracking is not implemented consistently
drupal.stevinAngle: Drupal is a powerful open-source CMS for complex sites with high demands on security, scale, and customization. That is the right place for it, and at the same time the warning: it requires technical expertise, and a Drupal without serious maintenance was the wrong choice. We run into it at larger organizations and government bodies where the complexity is genuinely needed. Where teams get stuck is the tracking implementation: because of the custom-build nature it is rarely consistent, and connections with the CRM require development work. Drupal records the content, but it does not watch what should happen with a submission or a conversion. Stevin adds a layer on top, reads the relevant events through a connection or webhook, and turns them into follow-up, with a person reviewing every action that carries weight first.
drupal.stackImpact: Choosing Drupal means you commit to custom work and maintenance: it is not a platform for a team without development capacity. Count on development work for consistent tracking and for the connections to your marketing stack and CRM. The strength sits in the flexibility and the governance, but you pay for that in setup time. The question is whether your complexity justifies the custom build, or whether a lighter CMS gets you to reliable data faster.
pitfalls: Choosing Drupal without development capacity: the custom build becomes a millstone.
Implementing tracking inconsistently because of the custom-build nature.
Not passing form and conversion data through to follow-up.

dv360.shortDescription: Programmatic advertising through Google Display & Video 360.
dv360.description: DV360 is Google's demand-side platform for programmatic advertising. It offers access to premium inventory and advanced targeting at scale.
dv360.useCase: Programmatic display and video advertising at scale.
dv360.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI deploys DV360 as part of larger media strategies. We make sure programmatic campaigns are properly connected to your tracking and that results are included in your overall reporting.
problemsSolved: Programmatic campaigns run apart from performance channels
No integrated overview of all media channels
dv360.stevinAngle: DV360 is Google's heavy programmatic platform: access to premium inventory and advanced targeting at scale, for display and video. It is powerful, but it is built for media teams and agencies, not for someone who just wants to run a campaign on the side. The trap is that programmatic at scale easily ends up in a silo: lots of impressions, lots of reach, but disconnected from what your performance channels actually bring in. We see advertisers stall on this: DV360 delivers volume, but there is no integrated picture where display and video sit next to search and social, so it stays unclear what the spend genuinely adds. Stevin runs as a layer on top, reads the campaign data through the API and puts it in your total reporting, with an eye on whether the tracking carries through correctly. A person sees the conclusion first, then comes a budget decision.
dv360.stackImpact: Choosing DV360 means you are running programmatic at agency level, and that requires a correct tracking setup and a place where the results come together with your other channels. Without that connection it becomes volume without context. The data is available through the API, so that is not the problem. The real question is whether display and video are measurable next to search and social, or whether they stay a separate silo. Without that integrated picture you steer on impressions instead of on contribution.
pitfalls: Letting programmatic run in a silo, apart from your performance channels.
Steering on impressions and reach because the contribution does not sit next to other channels.
Not checking the tracking setup, so conversions carry through wrong or not at all.
Assuming scale is the same as value without an integrated overview.

eventbrite.shortDescription: Event management, ticketing, and attendee data.
eventbrite.description: Eventbrite is the go-to platform for your own events, label nights, and small-scale shows. Attendee data and sales conversion are available right away.
eventbrite.useCase: Managing your own events and analyzing attendees.
eventbrite.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI syncs Eventbrite data and shows which promotion channels generate the most ticket sales.
problemsSolved: Event promotion is not measurable per channel
Attendee data is not reused for retargeting or community building
eventbrite.stevinAngle: Eventbrite is the obvious platform for your own events, label nights, and smaller shows: setup is quick, and you have attendee data plus sales conversion right at hand. For anyone organizing themselves that is enough to start, and there is nothing wrong with that. It gets tight the moment you want to know what your promotion actually earns. Eventbrite shows the sales, but not which channel brought the buyer, and the attendee data sits idle instead of flowing back to retargeting or community. So you pay for promotion without knowing what works and leave a valuable list unused. Stevin syncs your Eventbrite data and makes it visible which channel generates the most sales, and turns attendees into a base you can reach again. The actions that follow from it you see first, before anything goes out the door.
eventbrite.stackImpact: Eventbrite has a clean API, so getting the data out is not the problem. The platform measures the sale but not the source, so for channel attribution you need your tracking and UTMs alongside it. And the attendee list does nothing until you connect it to retargeting or your community tool, otherwise it is a dead export. In practice: let Eventbrite do the ticketing and let a layer on top assign the source and activate the attendees, so your promotion becomes measurable and your audience does not stay stuck in a spreadsheet after an event.
pitfalls: Not attributing sales to a channel, so you do not know which promotion worked.
Leaving the attendee list unused instead of deploying it for retargeting or community.
Forgetting tracking and UTMs, so the source of buyers cannot be traced afterward.

excel.shortDescription: Microsoft Excel for data analysis and reporting.
excel.description: Excel is still a widely used platform for data analysis and reporting, especially in enterprise environments running on Microsoft 365.
excel.useCase: Data analysis and reporting in Microsoft environments.
excel.howWeUseIt: Stevin delivers data exports and reports in Excel format and connects Excel to your marketing stack via Power Automate or Zapier where needed.
problemsSolved: Data from marketing tools is not available in Excel
Manual reports take too much time
excel.stevinAngle: For many organizations Excel is still the workhorse for data analysis and reporting, certainly where Microsoft 365 is the standard. The strength is familiarity and reach: almost everyone knows how to use it and the data lands in a form the whole team understands. The catch is that Excel is an endpoint, not a connection. Data from your marketing tools does not flow in on its own, and the reports people build by hand take time and go stale the moment the source changes. You are working with a photo of yesterday. We deliver exports and reports in Excel where that is the format that sticks, and connect it via Power Automate or Zapier where needed. Where teams get stuck is that an Excel report stays a snapshot. Stevin runs as a layer over your stack and makes sure the data that lands in Excel is current and that an anomaly gets noticed before someone sends around an outdated report.
excel.stackImpact: Choosing Excel as your reporting format means the team works in a familiar place, but data does not flow in on its own and goes stale fast. Count on a connection via Power Automate or Zapier if you do not want to keep exporting by hand. In practice Excel is a terminus, not a living source, so the question is who notices when a report no longer matches reality. Without a layer that refreshes the input and watches for anomalies, you steer decisions off a snapshot that may already be out of date.
pitfalls: Basing decisions on an Excel report that is an outdated snapshot.
Exporting by hand and building reports that take time and go stale fast.
Skipping a connection, so data from your tools never lands in Excel current.

facebook-graph.shortDescription: Facebook Page insights, post engagement, and community management.
facebook-graph.description: Facebook Pages remain an important channel for communities, events, and direct communication with fans. The Graph API offers access to page-level metrics and post performance.
facebook-graph.useCase: Monitoring page performance and tracking community engagement.
facebook-graph.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI syncs your Facebook Page data and combines it with Instagram and other channels for a cross-platform overview of your organic reach.
problemsSolved: Facebook data sits apart from your other social channels
Post engagement is not analyzed systematically
facebook-graph.stevinAngle: Facebook Pages get written off a lot, but for communities, events, and direct communication with a slightly older audience they still do work. The Graph API opens up the page level: post performance, engagement, the usual metrics. What the API does not do is bring your Facebook data into context with the rest. It stays an island, apart from your Instagram, apart from your other channels, even though it is often the same audience doing something in two places. Teams get stuck on that double picture: two tabs, two stories, no overview. Stevin reads the Facebook Page data through the Graph API and lines it up against your other sources, so a trend in engagement or a post that takes off surfaces as a signal instead of sitting in a loose dashboard. You set the follow-up, the person reviews it.
facebook-graph.stackImpact: Facebook Page data comes through the same Graph infrastructure as Instagram, so if you already have that set up this channel costs little on top. The bottleneck is not the connection but the coherence: Facebook and Instagram often share an audience, and if you read them separately your picture drifts apart. So you need something that lines the channels up side by side instead of two loose reports. Skip that, and you are paying attention to a channel you cannot tie to the rest anyway, and Facebook stays an island.
pitfalls: Reporting Facebook and Instagram separately, so the same audience is counted twice or inconsistently.
Writing the channel off and missing events and community signals from an older audience.
Collecting page data without anything that pulls trends out, so it becomes a dead dashboard.

fivetran.shortDescription: Managed ELT pipelines for enterprise data warehouses.
fivetran.description: Fivetran is a leading ELT platform that automatically syncs data from hundreds of sources into your data warehouse. A standard part of the modern data stack in enterprise organizations.
fivetran.useCase: Automated ELT from marketing, sales and product sources into the warehouse.
fivetran.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI uses Fivetran pipelines as the foundation for MMM and cross-channel attribution so data from every channel lands consistently in one warehouse.
problemsSolved: Custom ETL scripts break with every API change
Marketing data is not reliable in the warehouse
No consistent schema across channels
fivetran.stevinAngle: Fivetran is the workhorse of the modern data stack: managed ELT that automatically syncs hundreds of sources into your warehouse. The value is in what it removes, namely building and repairing connectors yourself that break with every API change. In enterprise environments it is the standard for good reason. Where teams get it wrong is treating Fivetran as the endpoint: it brings data in, but it models nothing and says nothing about what the data means. Schema drift and silent column changes can still wreck reporting if nobody watches the pipelines. Stevin uses Fivetran pipelines as the foundation and builds the measurement layer on top: the incoming channel data gets read, turned into signals and concrete follow-up, with a person reviewing every action that carries weight first.
fivetran.stackImpact: Choosing Fivetran means you outsource the flow of data into the warehouse and can clean up your own fragile ETL scripts. You get consistent, reliable data coming in, but you pay per volume processed, so broad syncs without cleanup add up fast. It delivers raw data, no models and no meaning, and it does not watch the pipelines for you. In practice: build the transformation and measurement layer on top of Fivetran and set up monitoring for schema changes, because it brings the data home, but what that data means is still something you have to put on top yourself.
pitfalls: Treating Fivetran as the endpoint: it delivers raw data, no models or meaning.
Not watching the pipelines, so schema drift quietly wrecks reporting.
Underestimating consumption costs through broad syncs without cleaning the data.
Assuming data in the warehouse is the same as usable marketing data.

folk.shortDescription: Lightweight relationship CRM for small teams.
folk.description: folk is a lightweight CRM focused on relationships and network: a clean rolodex with enrichment, email sequences, and contact sync. Strong for small teams and partnerships, less so for heavy sales pipelines.
folk.useCase: A relationship-focused CRM for founders and small teams.
folk.howWeUseIt: Stevin runs as an AI layer over folk. It reads contacts and interactions and turns them into signals and follow-up, so relationships do not go quiet and the right moment to reach out to someone again is not missed.
problemsSolved: Relationships go quiet without follow-up
No signal when you should reach out to someone again
folk.stevinAngle: folk is deliberately light, and that is its strength. A clean rolodex with enrichment, email sequences, and contact sync, made for founders and small teams who want to keep relationships warm without a clunky CRM machine. For networking and partnerships it works better than a heavy sales system you leave half empty. The limit is just as clear: the moment you need a real sales pipeline with many deals, stages, and reporting, folk runs out of room. It is a relationship tool, not a pipeline engine, and anyone who uses it for that quickly finds it too thin. Where teams get stuck is that relationships go quiet without anyone noticing, because folk records but does not remind you of the right moment to reach out again. Stevin runs as a layer over folk, reads contacts and interactions through the API, and turns a cooling relationship into a signal. The person decides on the follow-up.
folk.stackImpact: Choosing folk means you deliberately go for simplicity, and that is fine as long as your process is simple too. Grow your sales into real pipelines with forecasting and you outgrow folk and have to move, with a data migration you would rather have gotten ahead of, so choose it for relationships and not for heavy deals. It enriches contacts and sends sequences, but it does not guard momentum, for that you need something on top that watches for when a conversation has been quiet too long. The question that remains: who notices when a valuable relationship slips away.
pitfalls: Using folk for a heavy sales pipeline: it is a relationship tool, not a deal engine.
Letting relationships go quiet because nothing reminds you of the right moment.
Running sequences without anyone watching which relationship is cooling off.
Assuming recording a contact is the same as keeping the relationship warm.

foreplay.shortDescription: Ad inspiration library and competitor creative tracking.
foreplay.description: Foreplay is the swipe file for performance marketers. Save winning ads, organize them by theme or competitor, and share them with your creative team. Combined with TikTok and Meta ad monitoring, you always have a current picture of what works in the market.
foreplay.useCase: Competitor ad monitoring, creative inspiration, and brief backing.
foreplay.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI connects Foreplay's creative library to performance data. You see not only what competitors are doing, but which patterns actually deliver results. Briefs get backed with proven formats instead of assumptions.
problemsSolved: No structured overview of competitor creatives
Ad inspiration is ad hoc instead of systematic
Creative briefs lack examples of what works in the market
Ad screenshots get scattered across Slack, email, and folders
foreplay.stevinAngle: Foreplay solves a real problem: the swipe file that otherwise gets scattered across Slack, folders, and screenshots. Winning competitor ads in one place, organized by theme, with monitoring on Meta and TikTok on top. As a library it is strong. Where the thinking goes wrong is the assumption that collecting is the same as knowing what works. Foreplay shows what competitors are running, not whether it pays off, and an ad that runs long is not by definition an ad that converts. Teams get stuck there: inspiration becomes proof without anyone testing it. Stevin connects that library to your own performance. It reads via API which formats actually deliver results in your channels and lays that next to what you saved in Foreplay, so a brief rests on a proven pattern and not on a pretty screenshot. The person decides what goes to market.
foreplay.stackImpact: Foreplay replaces the loose folders and the chat screenshots, so your inspiration is finally organized and shareable. But it is a collection tool, not a measurement tool: it does not know your results and says nothing about whether a saved ad converts with your audience. Count on building the bridge to your own ad data yourself, alongside a tool that returns performance per creative, otherwise it stays a nice wall of examples nobody tests. The question is not whether you have enough references, but whether the reference you copy also works for your audience.
pitfalls: Mistaking a long-running competitor ad for a proven winner.
Collecting inspiration without linking it to your own results.
Copying a format because it looks good, not because it works for you.
Letting the library fill up until nobody remembers which example was saved and why.

freshsales.shortDescription: CRM from Freshworks with built-in AI scoring.
freshsales.description: Freshsales offers a modern CRM with built-in AI scoring, email tracking, and telephony. Part of the Freshworks ecosystem.
freshsales.useCase: A CRM with integrated communication tools and AI scoring.
freshsales.howWeUseIt: Stevin integrates Freshsales with your marketing stack and makes sure the AI scoring is fed with the right data from your campaigns.
problemsSolved: Lead scoring is not based on marketing data
The CRM and marketing tools are not synced
freshsales.stevinAngle: Freshsales packs in a lot: a modern CRM with telephony, email tracking, and built-in AI scoring, all within the Freshworks ecosystem. For teams that want communication and scoring in one place, that saves tying separate tools together. The trick is in that AI scoring, and that is also where the catch is. A score is only as good as the data going into it, and if that scoring runs on only what is in the CRM and not on your marketing data, you get a number that looks smarter than it is. Trusting a scoring model without the right input is a classic trap. Where teams get stuck is exactly that: lead scoring that is not fed with campaign data, and a CRM that does not run in sync with the marketing tools. Stevin connects to Freshsales through the API, feeds the scoring with the right signals from your campaigns, and turns a promising lead into a concrete next action. The person sees every action that carries weight first.
freshsales.stackImpact: Choosing Freshsales means you get a lot of functions in one system, but the AI scoring only has value if you feed it the right data. Count on the out-of-the-box scoring running on half a dataset, so the connection to your campaigns is not an extra but a condition. Without sync between the CRM and the marketing tools, your scoring runs behind the facts. In practice: let Freshsales carry the communication and scoring and make sure the data going in is complete.
pitfalls: Trusting AI scoring that runs only on CRM data and misses your campaigns.
Assuming an out-of-the-box score is the same as a well-founded one.
Not keeping the CRM and marketing tools in sync so the scoring runs behind.
Stacking built-in features without checking whether the data underneath is right.

google-ads.shortDescription: Advertising on Google Search, Display, Shopping and YouTube.
google-ads.description: Google Ads is the largest advertising platform in the world. From search ads to shopping and display, it gives you direct access to buying intent. But without solid tracking, landing pages and follow-up, it is also a platform where budget leaks away fast.
google-ads.useCase: Generate leads and customers through search intent, remarketing and shopping campaigns.
google-ads.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI connects Google Ads to your CRM, tracking and automation. We make sure conversions are measured correctly, that leads are picked up automatically, and that your campaigns are optimized on real customer value, not just clicks.
problemsSolved: Conversions are not measured correctly
Leads from Google Ads are not followed up fast enough
No insight into which campaigns genuinely produce customers
Budget leaks away through poor connection with the rest of the funnel
google-ads.stevinAngle: In 80 percent of the accounts we take over, Google Ads is not broken, it is read wrong. The dashboard shows conversions that Google did not cause: branded search that would have happened anyway, retargeting of warm traffic, comparison sites that had already secured the purchase. We run a geo test or holdout by default within the first month, to measure what actually comes in on top versus what would have converted without Google Ads anyway. The numbers from a test like that are structurally 20 to 40 percent off from what the Google dashboard reports itself.
google-ads.stackImpact: For your stack this means: tie Google Ads to an external baseline (CRM, P&L or a holdout segment), not just to Google's own conversion API. We send leads server-side straight to your CRM with the Click ID, so you can trace per lead which keyword, which campaign and which ad produced it. After that we measure customer value out to 12 months past the first click. Only then do you see which campaigns genuinely produce customers instead of clicks.
pitfalls: Running Performance Max without excluding branded keywords, it catches demand that was already there but still costs budget
Leaving conversion modeling on without understanding that you are then counting model estimates, not measured conversions
Smart Bidding on conversion volumes that are too low (under 30 a month), the algorithm has too little signal and starts guessing
No frequency cap on display, so a user gets served 40 times for one click

faqs.question: Does Stevin.AI also manage my Google Ads campaigns?
faqs.answer: Yes, we manage campaigns and make sure they are set up properly on the technical side, connected to your tracking and CRM, and optimised for real results.

faqs.question: Do you take a margin on my advertising budget?
faqs.answer: No. You pay your media budget straight to Google. We do not charge a margin or commission on your ad spend.

google-analytics-4.shortDescription: Website analytics and conversion tracking from Google.
google-analytics-4.description: Google Analytics 4 is the standard for website analytics. It gives insight into user behavior, traffic sources and conversions. But only if it is set up well, and at many companies that is not the case.
google-analytics-4.useCase: Measuring website traffic, conversions and user behavior.
google-analytics-4.howWeUseIt: Stevin sets up GA4 correctly: from enhanced measurement to custom events, conversion goals and connections to Google Ads. We make sure your data is reliable and that your reports line up with your commercial goals.
problemsSolved: GA4 is not configured well
Conversions are not measured correctly
No link between website data and campaign performance
Reports give no usable insight
google-analytics-4.stevinAngle: In most accounts GA4 is technically installed but fundamentally set up wrong. Default conversions usually do not count what you want to measure (for example 'Generate Lead' on a form submit, while your real conversion is a qualified lead in your CRM). Data sampling on large properties hides exactly the detail that is meaningful. We use GA4 as traffic-source reporting and behavioral analysis, not as the attribution source for budget decisions. For that last part we go to the CRM or an MMM.
google-analytics-4.stackImpact: Three technical things we fix as standard: server-side Google Tag Manager for tracking reliability (halving cookie loss of 20 to 40 percent), custom events that measure your funnel steps instead of Google's defaults, and a BigQuery connection so you can join GA4 data with CRM data. Only in BigQuery does GA4 become a real analysis tool instead of a dashboard.
pitfalls: Counting conversions on the pageview of the thank-you page when that page does not always load (SPAs, redirects)
Reading 'engaged sessions' as conversions: Google's definition is 10 seconds, which is not engagement
Cross-domain tracking not set up for your checkout on a different subdomain, splitting sessions
Leaving data retention on the default 2 months when you need 14 months for year-over-year comparisons

faqs.question: Can Stevin.AI improve my existing GA4?
faqs.answer: Yes. We audit your current setup, fix errors, and rebuild events and conversions so your data becomes reliable.

google-consent-mode.description: Google Consent Mode automatically adjusts the behavior of Google tags based on each visitor's consent status. It uses modeling to fill data gaps.
google-consent-mode.useCase: Consent-driven tracking with data modeling by Google.
google-consent-mode.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI implements Consent Mode v2 and makes sure all Google tags respond correctly to consent. This maximizes your data quality within the privacy rules.
problemsSolved: Google tags do not respect consent correctly
Data loss from consent without modeling
Consent Mode is not implemented or implemented wrongly
google-consent-mode.stevinAngle: Consent Mode is not a tool but a framework: it lets your Google tags behave according to the visitor's consent, and fills data gaps with modeling. Strong, but also exactly where the misunderstanding sits. We implement v2 because it is mandatory for Google advertising within Europe, not because it saves your measurement on its own. The modeling is an estimate, not real data, and on a wrong implementation tags do not respect consent at all or sit far too strict. Teams get stuck on the assumption that Consent Mode is on the moment they ticked a box somewhere. In practice the signal passthrough is often just slightly off. Stevin reads the consent status together with your tag data and gives a heads-up when tags ignore consent or measurement sinks, so a silent misconfiguration surfaces before you model on an error for weeks.
google-consent-mode.stackImpact: Consent Mode does not stand alone: it leans on your consent banner and your tag manager, and all three have to be right. If you pick a CMP, it has to pass the correct signals to Consent Mode, otherwise Google models on wrong assumptions and you build your advertising on an estimate that sits crooked. In practice: treat banner, tag manager and Consent Mode as a chain, not as three separate checkboxes, and verify that the signals hold up through the whole chain. The question that remains is not whether it is on, but whether the signals coming in actually match what the visitor chose.
pitfalls: Assuming Consent Mode works the moment it is ticked somewhere.
Confusing modeling with real measured data.
Connecting a CMP that passes the consent signals incorrectly.
Skipping v2 and letting your Google advertising decline.

google-merchant-center.shortDescription: Product data for Google Shopping, Free Listings, and Performance Max.
google-merchant-center.description: Google Merchant Center is the heart of your Google Shopping strategy. Product titles, descriptions, prices, and availability determine how and whether your products appear in Shopping results.
google-merchant-center.useCase: Google Shopping feed management, product data quality, and free listings optimization.
google-merchant-center.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI monitors your Merchant Center for disapprovals, data quality issues, and performance per product group. Feed problems get flagged right away before they affect your campaigns.
problemsSolved: Product disapprovals get discovered too late
Feed data quality is inconsistent
No view of which product groups deliver the most
google-merchant-center.stevinAngle: Google Merchant Center is the heart of your Shopping presence: titles, prices, availability, and descriptions decide whether your products appear at all. Well filled, it is the quiet engine under your shopping revenue. The problem is that it stays quiet at the wrong moments. A disapproval, a data quality issue, or a product dropping out of view, you often notice only once sales drop, because Merchant Center does not actively push those signals to you. Teams get stuck there: the feed seems fine until a whole product group goes silent. Stevin monitors your Merchant Center for disapprovals, data quality, and performance per product group and turns a problem into a signal before it hits your campaigns. Not yet another email in a full inbox, but a targeted alert with what is going on. The consultant sees what needs attention and decides what gets fixed.
google-merchant-center.stackImpact: Choosing Merchant Center is not a choice if you want to be on Google Shopping, it is the foundation. But it is a data container, not a watchdog: it does not warn proactively when something goes wrong, and the alerts that exist drown in your inbox. Count on a layer that actively flags disapprovals and quality problems and links them to which product groups deliver the most, so attention goes to the right place. The data is in there, the attention is missing. Without something keeping watch, you discover a feed problem only once your revenue tells you, and by then you are already days behind.
pitfalls: Only discovering a disapproval once sales are already dropping.
Relying on a data container that does not warn proactively.
Letting data quality slide until a whole product group falls out of view.
Having no view of which product groups actually earn the budget.

google-news-api.shortDescription: PR monitoring, press release tracking, and media coverage analysis.
google-news-api.description: Google News aggregates news articles and press releases. Essential for PR monitoring: know when you are in the news, what the sentiment is, and whether it grows your reach.
google-news-api.useCase: PR radar, media monitoring, and share-of-voice tracking.
google-news-api.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI monitors Google News for mentions and analyzes the sentiment. Positive media attention is put to use, negative coverage is flagged right away.
problemsSolved: Press releases and media mentions get missed
No insight into share of voice relative to competitors
PR impact is not tied to social media and streaming data
google-news-api.stevinAngle: The Google News API aggregates news and press releases, which makes it your PR radar: you know when you are in the news, in what tone, and whether it drives reach. It is a reliable source for media coverage without having to search by hand. What it is not is a judgment. The API delivers articles and mentions, but draws no link to the rest of your marketing and does not say what a piece is worth. That is where teams get stuck: a mention appears, no one sees it in time, and its impact on your social and streaming numbers stays a guess. Stevin monitors the news stream, weighs the sentiment, and lines a mention up against your other data. Positive attention becomes a proposal to act on, negative coverage a signal that surfaces fast. The person decides what happens with it.
google-news-api.stackImpact: A news API delivers articles, not priority, so you need something that weighs a mention and ties it to your own data to see whether the coverage leads anywhere. Sentiment from news text is coarse, so take it as an indication. On its own it is a feed you have to watch, and that rarely happens in time. In practice: let the API pull the mentions in and let a layer on top decide what is an attention spike and what is background noise, so positive coverage gets used and negative coverage does not only stand out days later.
pitfalls: Trying to watch the feed by hand until relevant mentions simply stand out too late.
Taking news sentiment as a hard number when it is coarse and context-poor.
Not tying media coverage to your social and streaming data, so the impact stays a guess.

google-search-console.shortDescription: Insight into your organic search performance in Google.
google-search-console.description: Google Search Console shows how your website performs in organic search results. From indexing to keywords and technical issues.
google-search-console.useCase: Monitoring organic search performance and technical SEO issues.
google-search-console.howWeUseIt: Stevin uses Search Console data to identify SEO opportunities and optimize landing pages for both organic and paid traffic.
problemsSolved: No view of organic search performance
Technical SEO issues go undetected
google-search-console.stevinAngle: Google Search Console is the direct line to how Google sees your site: indexing, keywords and technical issues, straight from the source. It is free and indispensable, and that is also where the limit sits. Search Console shows it, but does nothing, and it keeps the data only briefly, so a trend or a sinking page easily slips away before anyone looks. We use it where it is strong: as a factual source on your organic performance. Where teams get stuck is that the data stays in the tool. A page that suddenly gets fewer impressions, a keyword that sinks, an indexing problem: it is in there, but nobody looks every day. That is where Stevin sits. As a layer on top of your stack, Stevin reads Search Console through the API and keeps the history, so that a meaningful drop or a new technical problem becomes a signal a person reviews, instead of something you only discover once the traffic is already gone.
google-search-console.stackImpact: Choosing Search Console costs nothing, but the data lives only briefly and the tool does nothing with what it shows. Count on wanting to hold the history somewhere, otherwise you miss trends because the window is too narrow. The data comes in through the API, so the real question is not whether you can access it, but whether someone watches the movements that matter. Without something that keeps the history and watches for deviations, Search Console stays a dashboard you open when it is already too late, not a source that warns you.
pitfalls: Relying on the short retention period, so trends slip away before you see them.
Leaving the data in the tool while nobody looks at it daily.
Only noticing a sinking page or indexing problem once the traffic is already gone.

google-sheets.shortDescription: Spreadsheets for data storage, reporting, and workflows.
google-sheets.description: Google Sheets is more than a spreadsheet. It is a flexible data hub you can connect to almost any marketing tool. Ideal for reporting, data enrichment, and as a middle layer in automations.
google-sheets.useCase: Flexible data storage and reporting as part of marketing workflows.
google-sheets.howWeUseIt: Stevin uses Sheets as a link in automations: from lead lists to reporting exports and data enrichment via Zapier or Make.
problemsSolved: Data has to be moved between tools by hand
No central place for ad hoc reporting
google-sheets.stevinAngle: Google Sheets is much more than a spreadsheet. It is the flexible glue layer you connect to almost every marketing tool, ideal for lists, reporting exports, and enrichment. The strength is exactly that flexibility, you build something fast without heavy software. And that is where the risk sits too. A Sheet grows organically into a tab where nobody knows which formula depends on what, and data you type in by hand drifts away from your actual sources. We use it as a link in automations, not as a system of record. Where teams get stuck is that a Sheet becomes a quiet single point of failure: an import that stops or a cell that gets overwritten only shows up when a report comes out wrong. Stevin runs as a layer over your stack and uses Sheets as a waypoint, reads it through the API, and flags when data stops adding up or an expected update never lands, so a person steps in before it spreads.
google-sheets.stackImpact: Choosing Sheets as a link means you have something that ties almost everything together, but also something that can break quietly without anyone noticing. Treat it as a middle layer, not a source of truth, because manual entry drifts away from your real systems. The data is easy to read through the API, so the question is not whether you can get at it, but whether anyone notices when an import stalls or a cell gets overwritten. Without that check, a Sheet becomes a fragile heart of your workflow that nobody is watching.
pitfalls: Using a Sheet as a system of record, so data drifts away from your sources.
Letting formulas and links grow organically until nobody knows the dependencies anymore.
Catching a stopped import or an overwritten cell only when a report comes out wrong.

google-tag-manager.shortDescription: Tag management for handling tracking and pixels.
google-tag-manager.description: Google Tag Manager is the central point for all your tracking. Pixels, events, conversions: everything is managed through GTM. Set up well, it saves time and prevents errors. Set up badly, it causes data loss.
google-tag-manager.useCase: Central management of all tracking tags and marketing pixels.
google-tag-manager.howWeUseIt: Stevin sets up GTM according to best practices: clean containers, correct triggers, data layer implementation and server-side tagging where needed. We make sure all your tools receive reliable data.
problemsSolved: Tags fire incorrectly or twice
No overview in the GTM container
The data layer is not implemented or implemented badly
Server-side tagging is not set up
google-tag-manager.stevinAngle: GTM is not a marketing tool, it is tracking infrastructure. Most accounts treat it as 'the place where the marketer adds tags without a developer', which is technically true but leads to messy containers: 80 or more tags nobody can trace anymore, duplicate triggers, conflicting variables. We start every audit with a container clean: which tag is there and why, which still work, which pollute the signal. A clean container is a better ROI investment than a new campaign.
google-tag-manager.stackImpact: Server-side GTM is the standard in 2026, no longer optional. It solves three problems at once: data loss from browser restrictions (Safari ITP, ad blockers), latency on your site from fewer client-side scripts, and first-party data ownership instead of data that gets grabbed by 30 vendor pixels. We host server-side GTM on your own subdomain, not on Google's servers, so your data really sits in your stack.
pitfalls: Sticking with client-side GTM while your conversion match rate is already dropping below 60 percent
Using custom HTML tags for vendor pixels that do have a native template, more maintenance, no gain
Tying triggers to CSS classes the developer changes in a month, tracking quietly fails
Deploying a container without versioning or a preview-mode test, broken tracking goes live

google-trends.shortDescription: Measure Share of Search and track market trends in search behavior.
google-trends.description: Google Trends shows how search interest develops over time. Share of Search (your share of branded search volume versus competitors) is proven to be the best predictor of market share. No panel, no survey: pure search behavior from millions of users.
google-trends.useCase: Share of Search tracking, recognizing seasonal patterns, and monitoring brand health.
google-trends.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI automatically pulls Google Trends data for your brand and your competitors. Every week you see how your Share of Search evolves and whether your campaigns actually generate brand awareness, not just clicks.
problemsSolved: No view of whether campaigns actually raise brand awareness
Share of Search is not monitored structurally
Competitors gain ground without you noticing
Seasonal effects are not factored into media budget allocation
google-trends.stevinAngle: Google Trends is free and underrated. Share of Search, your brand's share of search volume against competitors, is one of the better predictors of market share, and it comes from real search behavior of millions of people, no panel or survey. That makes it stronger than many paid alternatives. The weakness is in the handling: the data is there, but nobody looks at it structurally, and loose searches produce no rhythm. Teams get stuck there: they measure clicks weekly but brand health never, and competitors gain ground before anyone notices. Stevin pulls Trends data automatically for your brand and your competitors and turns it into a weekly signal: your Share of Search is moving this way, your campaign is or is not generating brand awareness, a seasonal peak is coming up. The consultant sees the read before anyone acts on it.
google-trends.stackImpact: Google Trends costs nothing and gives you a brand signal you get this clean nowhere else, but on its own it does nothing: it is a website you have to visit. Count on a layer that pulls the data periodically, puts it next to your competitors, and turns it into a recurring signal, otherwise it disappears in the noise. The value is not in the graph, but in someone or something looking at it every week and warning you when the line goes the wrong way.
pitfalls: Measuring clicks weekly but brand health never.
Checking Share of Search occasionally instead of tracking it structurally.
Letting a competitor gain ground because nobody guards the line.
Missing seasonal patterns in your budget split because the data stays unseen.

faqs.question: What exactly is Share of Search?
faqs.answer: Share of Search is the percentage of branded search volume for your brand against the whole category. Research by Les Binet (IPA) shows it is the best predictor of market share, stronger than Share of Voice.

faqs.question: How often is Share of Search updated?
faqs.answer: Stevin.AI calculates your Share of Search weekly and compares it with previous periods so you see trends right away.

gwi.shortDescription: Consumer audience insights and audience segmentation based on panel data.
gwi.description: GWI (GlobalWebIndex) offers in-depth audience insights based on the largest online consumer panel in the world. From media behavior to brand perception, attitudes, and purchase intent: the data goes beyond demographics.
gwi.useCase: Audience analysis, media planning, and strategic positioning.
gwi.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI integrates GWI audience data into the strategic layer. Creative briefs and media allocation get backed with how your audience actually behaves, not how you think they behave.
problemsSolved: Audience knowledge is based on assumptions instead of panel data
Media planning does not match the audience's real media behavior
Creative briefs lack an audience foundation
gwi.stevinAngle: GWI goes beyond demographics: based on a large consumer panel, it shows how your audience really behaves, from media use to brand perception and purchase intent. For strategy and media planning, that is a firmer foundation than assumptions in a meeting room. The limit is in the nature of panel data: it is representative on the broad strokes, but it is a sample, not the full reality, and the narrower your audience, the thinner the base. Teams get stuck there: they treat a panel insight as a fixed fact about their specific customer. Stevin brings GWI data into the strategic layer and links it to your own campaign and customer data, so a creative brief or a media allocation rests on both the panel and what really happens in your channels. The consultant sees the foundation before a choice is made on it.
gwi.stackImpact: Choosing GWI means your audience knowledge rests on data instead of feel, but it is a general panel, not a measurement of your customers. Count on combining it with your own analytics and CRM, otherwise you plan media on an average that may not be your audience. The value is in bringing the broad panel picture together with your own data. Without that link you steer on a sample you never tested against your real results.
pitfalls: Treating a panel insight as a fixed fact about your specific customer.
Leaning on a narrow audience where the panel base is exactly thinnest.
Planning media on an average without laying it next to your own data.
Not linking the broad panel picture to your analytics and CRM.

heap.shortDescription: Auto-capture product analytics without tagging events in advance.
heap.description: Heap stands out with autocapture: every user interaction is recorded automatically, so you can still define funnels and events after the fact without a code deploy.
heap.useCase: Fast product analytics without extensive event tagging up front.
heap.howWeUseIt: Stevin uses Heap to get quick insight into user behavior and connects the events to your marketing stack and CRM for a complete journey.
problemsSolved: Event tagging up front is a bottleneck
Product data never reaches marketing
heap.stevinAngle: Heap has a genuinely nice trick: autocapture. You do not have to decide in advance which events you want to measure, the system records everything and you define your funnels afterward. That removes the prep work teams normally spend weeks stuck on. We see the other side too: recording everything is not the same as knowing what matters. You get a mountain of raw interactions and have to make sense of it yourself, and defining that retroactively quickly becomes a craft of its own. Where teams get stuck is exactly there: the data is sitting there, but nobody looks at it structurally and it never reaches the people who can act on it. Stevin reads Heap's events through the API, connects them to your CRM and campaigns, and turns a striking behavior pattern into a concrete signal. The person sees every action with weight first.
heap.stackImpact: Choosing Heap means you lower the bar to measure, but the bar to understand shifts to later. You still need something that translates the raw events into decisions, because Heap itself drives no follow-up. Count on a connection to your CRM so product behavior and customer data come together, otherwise your product data lives apart from where the selling happens. In practice: let Heap do what it is strong at, recording without fuss, and put a layer on top that attaches meaning and action to it.
pitfalls: Thinking autocapture replaces a measurement strategy: you still end up with a mountain of data without direction.
Redefining funnels after the fact until nobody knows which version is the truth.
Product data that stays stuck in Heap and never reaches the CRM or sales.
Assuming measuring everything is the same as knowing what counts.

hightouch.shortDescription: Reverse ETL: warehouse data into marketing and sales tools.
hightouch.description: Hightouch syncs data from your warehouse back into operational tools like advertising platforms, CRM and email. It turns your data warehouse into a composable CDP.
hightouch.useCase: Warehouse as the source of truth for segmentation and activation in marketing tools.
hightouch.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI uses Hightouch to activate audiences and lifecycle segments from the warehouse directly in Meta, Google, LinkedIn and CRM, with governance in one place.
problemsSolved: Audiences are maintained manually in every advertising platform
Segmentation is inconsistent across tools
A CDP is expensive or duplicate work next to the warehouse
hightouch.stevinAngle: Hightouch reverses the data flow: instead of pulling data into the warehouse, it pushes warehouse data back out to your operational tools like advertising platforms, CRM and email. That turns your warehouse into a composable CDP, and it is a smart move for teams who want to keep their governance in one place instead of in every tool separately. The gain is concrete: audiences you define once in the warehouse, you activate everywhere. Where teams get stuck is the assumption that reverse ETL does the thinking. Hightouch moves segments reliably, but the segments themselves and the logic behind them stay your work, and a wrongly defined segment gets neatly pushed to every channel. Stevin uses Hightouch to activate audiences and lifecycle segments from the warehouse in Meta, Google, LinkedIn and CRM, with governance in one place, and puts signals and follow-up underneath, with a person reviewing every action that carries weight first.
hightouch.stackImpact: Choosing Hightouch means your warehouse becomes the source of truth for segmentation and you do not need a separate CDP to activate audiences. That saves duplicate work and keeps logic in one place, but it requires your warehouse and segment definitions to be in order before it delivers anything. In practice: make sure the models are right before you activate, and build a check on what gets synced, because reverse ETL amplifies both good and bad segments, and a mistake synced to every channel is a mistake that multiplies.
pitfalls: Assuming reverse ETL takes over the segmentation logic instead of just moving it.
Activating faulty segment definitions, which then get pushed to every channel.
Using the warehouse as the source of truth while the models are not in order.
Seeing Hightouch as a full CDP without the governance and modeling that requires.

hotjar.shortDescription: Heatmaps and session recordings for user behavior.
hotjar.description: Hotjar gives visual insight into how visitors use your website through heatmaps, session recordings and feedback surveys. It complements quantitative analytics with qualitative insight.
hotjar.useCase: Understanding how visitors use your website for CRO.
hotjar.howWeUseIt: Stevin uses Hotjar to identify friction points on landing pages and forms. We translate the insights into concrete improvements in your conversion flow.
problemsSolved: Visitors drop off but you do not know why
Forms do not get completed
Landing pages convert below par
hotjar.stevinAngle: Hotjar is not an analytics tool, it is a diagnostic tool. You use it when you know conversions are dropping but do not know why. Heatmaps, session recordings and surveys tell you what a dashboard cannot: where people click on non-clickable elements, where they scroll past your most important CTA, where they stop on a form field. We deliberately run Hotjar periodically (two weeks per quarter) instead of permanently, otherwise your team drowns in 'interesting but not actionable' video footage. The free tier covers 35 sessions per day, enough for diagnostic rounds.
hotjar.stackImpact: Combine it with your analytics stack as a source of hypotheses, not as your primary measurement. When conversion drops on a specific page, first turn Hotjar on for that page, form a hypothesis, then build an A/B test to validate it. Integrate surveys with your CRM (through Zapier or native) so answers are tied to customer segments instead of floating around anonymously.
pitfalls: Leaving recordings always on, a privacy risk (PII in forms) and the team never reviews them
Reading a heatmap as quantitative data, 100 sessions is not a statistically valid sample
Showing surveys on every page, survey fatigue, the response rate collapses
Cookie consent not implemented correctly, Hotjar places cookies before consent, a GDPR violation

hubspot.shortDescription: All-in-one CRM with marketing, sales, and service hubs.
hubspot.description: HubSpot is one of the most widely used CRM platforms, with integrated tools for marketing, sales, and customer service. It offers a complete ecosystem for managing the whole customer journey.
hubspot.useCase: Central management of leads, deals, email marketing, and automation.
hubspot.howWeUseIt: Stevin connects HubSpot to your ad channels, website, and tracking. We set up lead scoring, workflows, and deal pipelines so marketing and sales work on the same data and leads are followed up automatically.
problemsSolved: Marketing and sales work with different data
Leads are not scored and distributed automatically
No insight into which marketing channels deliver real customers
Manual lead follow-up is too slow
hubspot.stevinAngle: HubSpot is a CRM with marketing tools bolted on, not the other way around. That means the value sits in the pipeline data and the automation, not in the emailing function or the landing page builder. We see teams buy HubSpot for one feature and switch the rest on 'because it is there anyway', then splinter their stack over HubSpot for some things and other tools for others. Stevin's line: either commit HubSpot to the whole customer journey or use it purely as a CRM and build the rest around your best tools.
hubspot.stackImpact: For a clean HubSpot: clean up properties (most accounts have 200+ custom properties, half of which are never used), document workflows, and define lifecycle stages strictly. Then the integrations: Stripe for revenue attribution, your ad channels for channel touchpoints, and your website CMS for content engagement. Only then do HubSpot reports become reliable enough to base decisions on.
pitfalls: Importing leads without a lifecycle stage, pipeline reports count suspects as prospects
Building workflows on an enrollment trigger without exit criteria, contacts get stuck in 8 workflows at once
Letting the MQL definition decay into 'anyone with an email', sales quality drops, marketing gets blamed
Using the HubSpot ads tool for budget control instead of Google/Meta native, you lose features and data granularity

faqs.question: Can Stevin.AI improve our existing HubSpot setup?
faqs.answer: Yes. We audit your current HubSpot setup and optimise workflows, lead scoring, integrations and reporting so you get more out of the CRM you already have.

infrabox.shortDescription: Project administration for infrastructure and civil engineering.
infrabox.description: InfraBox is software for infrastructure and civil engineering projects: project administration, cost control and progress on location.
infrabox.useCase: Administer and monitor infrastructure and civil engineering projects.
infrabox.howWeUseIt: Stevin connects to InfraBox and turns project data into signals: a phase running late, a cost item that deviates, a report that needs follow-up. For outdoor work, Stevin also ties weather data to the planning. Stevin does not replace InfraBox, it makes the information usable in time. Connect through the API or an export.
problemsSolved: Delay in a project phase surfaces too late
Cost deviations are not seen in time
Outdoor work is at risk from weather with no early warning
No central overview of what needs attention
infrabox.stevinAngle: InfraBox is made for infrastructure and civil engineering: project administration, cost control and progress on location. For road, ground and water works that is the right foundation, because it is built around the way those projects actually run. What the system does not do is account for the biggest unknown in this work: the weather. A phase running late, a cost item that deviates, a report from the site that needs follow-up, InfraBox records it but does not connect it to the planning or to outdoor conditions. We see teams lose time and money there. Stevin connects to it through the API or an export, reads the project data and turns it into signals, and for outdoor work it lays weather data next to the planning. Stevin does not replace InfraBox, it makes the information usable at the moment a crew can still shift, with the site manager seeing the action first.
infrabox.stackImpact: InfraBox covers the project side of infrastructure and civil engineering, but it does not account for weather, while outdoor work is exactly what makes or breaks the schedule. That link between planning and weather data is not in it and has to sit on top. The connection runs through the API or an export, so the project data comes out. The question is whether something flags a phase running late, a cost deviation or a weather risk in time. Without that monitoring, a crew only shifts when it is already too late, and a lost workday costs money straight away.
pitfalls: Only seeing a project phase running late once the whole planning has shifted.
Noticing cost deviations too late because they are not tied to the planning.
Letting outdoor work run with no weather warning, then a lost day costs money straight away.
No central overview of what needs attention, so report after report in the inbox.

instagram-graph-api.shortDescription: Organic Instagram metrics, comment monitoring, and engagement analysis.
instagram-graph-api.description: Instagram is the visual storefront for artists, brands, and creators. The Graph API gives access to reach, impressions, follower growth, and comment data at account and post level.
instagram-graph-api.useCase: Monitoring organic reach, filtering fan engagement, and sentiment analysis.
instagram-graph-api.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI pulls your Instagram metrics daily, filters high-intent comments out of the noise, and generates Advisor cards for engagement opportunities you would otherwise miss.
problemsSolved: Thousands of comments but no overview of what matters
Organic performance is not tied to ads strategy
No insight into follower growth trends per region
instagram-graph-api.stevinAngle: The Instagram Graph API gives you the numbers the app itself holds back: reach, impressions, follower growth, and every comment at post and account level. Solid and reliable, as long as you know it is raw data and not a judgment. That is exactly where the bottleneck sits. On an account with any volume, thousands of comments pour in, and most of them are noise. The one fan question that genuinely matters, a collaboration request, a complaint getting out of hand, disappears among the emoji. The API delivers everything, but filters nothing. Stevin runs as a work layer over the Graph API, pulls your metrics daily, and sifts the comments with intent from the rest. Whatever needs attention surfaces as a signal with a suggested reply, and you see it before anything goes out the door.
instagram-graph-api.stackImpact: Choosing the Graph API means setting up and maintaining a Meta app and the permissions that go with it, and Meta tightens the rules regularly. It gives you organic data, but it sits apart from your ads side, so for a complete picture you connect it to your advertising data. The comments arrive raw, with no filtering at all, so the value is in what happens on top. The real question is not whether you can get the metrics out, but whether something sifts the noise for you, because without that it stays a dashboard no one opens in time.
pitfalls: Underestimating permissions and app review, so the connection stalls on a Meta change.
Trying to read every comment by hand until it simply piles up untouched.
Looking at organic data apart from your ads data, so you miss half the story.

iterable.shortDescription: Cross-channel marketing automation for email, push, SMS, and in-app.
iterable.description: Iterable is an enterprise cross-channel marketing platform with a strong emphasis on personalization, journeys, and data flexibility. Suited to B2C brands that want to run individual journeys at scale.
iterable.useCase: Personalized cross-channel journeys for B2C at enterprise scale.
iterable.howWeUseIt: Stevin connects Iterable to your CDP, product data, and MMM so lifecycle investment can be weighed against paid channels and is not treated as a standalone cost.
problemsSolved: Lifecycle data is not connected to paid media decisions
Personalization snags on data fragmentation
iterable.stevinAngle: Iterable aims at B2C brands that want to run individual journeys at scale, with strong personalization and a flexible data model. In practice it is pleasant to work with as long as the data comes in well, and frustrating the moment it is fragmented, because then the personalization snags on the source and not on the platform. We use it for clients where lifecycle marketing is genuinely an engine, not for a team that sends the occasional campaign. Where teams get stuck is the tendency to treat lifecycle as a separate cost, apart from the paid channels. Stevin runs as a layer over Iterable, connects it to your CDP and product data, and makes visible how the lifecycle investment relates to your paid media, with the person seeing every action that carries weight first.
iterable.stackImpact: Choosing Iterable means the value stands or falls with your data source: the flexible data model is strong, but fragmented data cripples the personalization right away. Count on a CDP or a clean product-data layer underneath. It is not a CRM, so you keep your system of record alongside it. The question is not whether you can build individual journeys, but whether your lifecycle spend sits in the same trade-off as your paid media, instead of as a separate line item.
pitfalls: Using Iterable on fragmented data: the personalization strands on the source, not the platform.
Treating lifecycle as a separate cost without comparing it to your paid channels.
Building journeys faster than your data model can keep up.

iubenda.shortDescription: Privacy and consent solution for websites and apps.
iubenda.description: iubenda offers consent management, privacy policies and cookie policies in one platform. It is an accessible solution for SMBs that want to be compliant fast with GDPR and other privacy legislation.
iubenda.useCase: Privacy compliance and consent management for SMBs.
iubenda.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI implements iubenda as a consent solution and makes sure it works correctly with your tracking and Google Consent Mode.
problemsSolved: No privacy policy or cookie policy on the website
Consent management is not set up for GDPR compliance
iubenda.stevinAngle: iubenda is the pragmatic choice for SMBs: consent, privacy policy and cookie policy in an accessible package, so you are demonstrably in order fast without a lawyer or a big project. We use it for smaller clients who want to tick the compliance box and move on, not for organizations with heavy governance requirements. Where it pinches is exactly that simplicity: the moment you want more than a standard banner, or the connection to your tracking has to be right, you hit the limits of the package. Teams assume installed is the same as measuring correctly, and that often disappoints. iubenda handles the consent, not whether your tags pick up that consent. Stevin runs on top, reads the consent status with your tag data and flags when measurement drops out because of consent, so a silent error surfaces before you lose a month of data on it.
iubenda.stackImpact: iubenda covers the basics fast and cheap, but you still need a tag manager and a Consent Mode connection to get the measurement side right. For a simple site that is enough, for anything more complex you run into the ceilings. In practice: use iubenda for the policies and the standard banner, and separately check whether your most important conversion data comes in after consent. The question that remains is not whether you have a banner, but whether your tracking behind it actually measures what you need.
pitfalls: Assuming a placed banner equals correct measurement.
Wanting to stretch iubenda into a setup it cannot handle.
Skipping the Consent Mode connection because the policies are in order.
Only noticing at a reporting gap that tags ignore consent.

jcdecaux.description: JCDecaux is the world leader in out-of-home (OOH) and digital out-of-home (DOOH) advertising. From bus shelters and billboards to digital screens in stations and shopping centers.
jcdecaux.useCase: Brand awareness and reach through out-of-home and digital outdoor advertising.
jcdecaux.howWeUseIt: Stevin combines DOOH campaigns with online channels and measures the impact through footfall data and uplift studies, so you see how offline visibility contributes to online conversions.
problemsSolved: No view of how outdoor advertising affects online conversions
DOOH runs entirely separate from digital channels
jcdecaux.stevinAngle: JCDecaux is the world leader in outdoor advertising, from bus shelters and billboards to digital screens in stations and shopping centers. For visibility and brand awareness out on the street, little comes close. The honest limit is measurement: out-of-home works, but it leaves no click behind, so its contribution to online conversions is hard to prove. We see advertisers get stuck here: the screens are up, the reach is large, but it runs entirely separate from the digital channels and nobody can say what it set in motion online. The medium delivers visibility, not a trail you can follow. Stevin runs as a layer on top of your digital stack, combines DOOH campaigns with your online channels, and uses footfall and uplift signals to make the impact visible. A person reviews the conclusion before any budget moves between offline and online.
jcdecaux.stackImpact: Choosing JCDecaux gives you physical visibility you cannot buy online, but it leaves no click behind, so you need something that surfaces the impact a different way: footfall, uplift, and a connection to your online channels. Without that, outdoor advertising runs entirely separate from the rest. The real question is how the visibility on the street carries through to online conversions, because that link usually exists but is rarely measured. Without that picture, you judge a large budget purely on feel.
pitfalls: Leaving DOOH entirely separate from your digital channels, so you have no view of the online effect.
Not approaching the impact through footfall or uplift, given that no click is left behind.
Judging a large media budget on feel without any measurement.
Assuming no click means no effect, when the link usually does exist.

klaviyo.shortDescription: Email marketing and automation built specifically for e-commerce.
klaviyo.description: Klaviyo is the standard for e-commerce email marketing. Strong segmentation, automation, and native integrations with webshop platforms.
klaviyo.useCase: Advanced email marketing and automation for webshops.
klaviyo.howWeUseIt: Stevin connects Klaviyo to your webshop, ads, and tracking so your flows and segments are fed the right data and stay relevant.
problemsSolved: Email flows are not aligned with how customers actually behave
Segmentation is too broad or not driven by data
klaviyo.stevinAngle: Klaviyo was built for e-commerce, and you feel it in every feature. For D2C brands on Shopify or WooCommerce, Klaviyo is the default, not because it has the prettiest UI but because the product-data hooks work out of the box: viewed product, added to cart, started checkout, all of it triggerable without a developer. For B2B or services, Klaviyo is overkill and you miss flow features that HubSpot or ActiveCampaign do have. So watch the hype: Klaviyo does not solve every email problem, it solves e-commerce email well.
klaviyo.stackImpact: Three flows every Klaviyo account should have before it thinks about campaigns: a welcome series (3 to 5 emails over the week after signup), abandoned cart (1 email within the hour, 1 within 24 hours), and post-purchase (a review request after 14 days, a cross-sell after 30 days). In our data these flows deliver 30 to 40 percent of total email revenue, while you build them once and they run on their own. Campaigns, segmentation, and SMS come after that, not before.
pitfalls: Turning on the SMS channel without a TCPA-compliant opt-in flow. US fines run into five figures.
Using predictive analytics on accounts under 10,000 customers. The model has too little data, so the predictions are noise.
Building segments on 'Active in last 30 days' without defining what 'active' means. The segment fills up with junk fast.
Pushing email frequency past 3 per week without unsubscribe triage. List churn speeds up and deliverability drops.

kraan-bouwcomputing.shortDescription: Estimating and project software for construction.
kraan-bouwcomputing.description: Kraan Bouwcomputing delivers estimating, project and cost-price software for contractors and construction firms.
kraan-bouwcomputing.useCase: Build and monitor estimates and cost prices at the project level.
kraan-bouwcomputing.howWeUseIt: Stevin puts a work layer on top of Kraan and flags what needs attention around estimating and margin: an estimate with out-of-date prices, a project where costs are climbing. Stevin proposes the action, a person decides. Connect through the API or an export.
problemsSolved: Out-of-date prices in the estimate go unnoticed
Climbing costs on a project are seen too late
Estimate data sits apart from the execution
No early signals about margin risk
kraan-bouwcomputing.stevinAngle: Kraan Bouwcomputing specializes in the calculation work: estimating, cost price and project costs for contractors and construction firms. On that specialism it is strong, stronger than the calculation module of a broad ERP. The flip side of a dedicated estimating tool is that it mainly looks ahead, to the quote, and watches less of what happens to those numbers during execution. We see firms stall on this: an estimate still running on last season's prices, a project where the actual costs climb while the estimate stays put. Kraan calculates it correctly, but it does not lay the estimate next to the execution on its own. Stevin puts a layer on top, through the API or an export, and flags what creates margin risk with an action underneath. The estimator decides, Stevin keeps an eye on the distance between budgeted and actual.
kraan-bouwcomputing.stackImpact: Choosing Kraan gives you strong calculation work, but the estimate sits apart from what actually happens on site. That bridge between budget and execution is something you have to organize yourself. The connection runs through the API or an export, so the estimate data comes out. The question is whether something flags the out-of-date price or the climbing costs in time. Without that monitoring, you only discover margin risk at the after-the-fact costing, when the profit is already gone and correcting is no longer an option.
pitfalls: Estimating with last season's prices because nothing marks the out-of-date lines.
Only seeing climbing costs on a project once the estimate is already out of date.
Leaving the estimate apart from the execution, so budgeted and actual drift apart.
Only discovering margin risk at the after-the-fact costing, when the profit is already gone.

lightspeed-ecom.shortDescription: Ecommerce platform with strong POS integration.
lightspeed-ecom.description: Lightspeed eCom combines ecommerce with point-of-sale functionality. A good fit for retailers that want to integrate online and offline sales in one system.
lightspeed-ecom.useCase: Omnichannel retail with integrated online and offline sales.
lightspeed-ecom.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI connects Lightspeed eCom to your marketing tools and tracking so that both online and offline sales data are included in your campaign reporting.
problemsSolved: Online and offline sales data are not combined
Ecommerce tracking is not connected to marketing channels
lightspeed-ecom.stevinAngle: Lightspeed eCom is at its best with retailers that really have two legs: a webshop and a physical store. The POS integration is the reason to be here, because online and offline sales come together in one system. We recommend it where that omnichannel reality holds, and not to a pure online player who never uses the till side. Where it pinches is the assumption that one side of the sales picture is in view. The online numbers sit neatly in the marketing reporting, the in-store sales fall outside it, and that way you steer campaigns on half the story. Stevin connects Lightspeed through the API, merges online and offline data into one picture, and turns it into signals, for example a product that stands still online but sells in the store, with the consultant seeing the follow-up first.
lightspeed-ecom.stackImpact: Choosing Lightspeed pays off when till and webshop genuinely belong together and you use both sides seriously. If you have no physical sales, you pay for POS functionality that sits idle. It keeps online and offline sales in one system, so you do not need a separate till connection or a second place where stock drifts apart. The question that remains is whether your marketing reporting actually includes the store data, because otherwise you steer on the online part alone and miss where the campaign has offline effect.
pitfalls: Choosing Lightspeed without physical sales: the POS core sits idle while you pay for it.
Leaving in-store sales outside the marketing reporting, so you steer on half the revenue.
Not merging online and offline data, resulting in a double or incomplete picture.
Assuming omnichannel data ends up in your campaign tools automatically.

linkedin-ads.shortDescription: B2B advertising on LinkedIn for targeted lead generation.
linkedin-ads.description: LinkedIn Ads is the leading B2B advertising platform. The cost per click is higher, but the quality of leads is often better. That makes solid follow-up and tracking extra important.
linkedin-ads.useCase: B2B lead generation and account-based marketing through LinkedIn.
linkedin-ads.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI connects LinkedIn Ads to your CRM and makes sure leads from LinkedIn Lead Gen Forms are synced automatically. We measure through to the customer level so you know which campaigns genuinely produce revenue.
problemsSolved: High cost per lead with no insight into quality
Lead Gen Forms are not connected to the CRM
No view of the ROI of LinkedIn campaigns
linkedin-ads.stevinAngle: LinkedIn Ads has the highest cost per click in the market and the best targeting by job title or company size, both are true. What most accounts miss: LinkedIn's attribution window is 30 days and B2B cycles are 3 to 9 months. A lead that comes in six weeks after the first impression through Google gets zero credit from LinkedIn but was activated by it. We do not measure LinkedIn on conversions within 30 days, we measure on pipeline influence across the whole deal cycle.
linkedin-ads.stackImpact: For B2B this means: connect LinkedIn to your CRM at the company level (matched audiences, lead routing to BDRs, opportunity tagging). Only then do you see that a LinkedIn touchpoint is often not the 'last click' but the 'first touch' that made the whole deal possible. Combine it with Bombora or 6sense for intent data so you know when a target account is actively in-market.
pitfalls: Measuring ROAS over a 30-day window while your sales cycle is 6 months
Using Lead Gen Forms without an enrichment step, you get name and email but no role or company size
Sending Sponsored InMail to cold traffic, opt-out rates of 80 percent and up, hurts your long-term match rate
Targeting by job title without a seniority filter, junior staff in the funnel who never decide

linktree.shortDescription: Link-in-bio analytics, click tracking, and conversion data.
linktree.description: Linktree is the standard link-in-bio tool. Click data shows what your audience is most interested in: merch, tickets, new releases, or your website.
linktree.useCase: Click-through analysis and audience intent tracking.
linktree.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI analyzes your Linktree clicks and correlates them with your social media posts to determine which content drives the most traffic.
problemsSolved: No insight into which links are clicked most
Link performance is not tied to specific social posts
linktree.stevinAngle: Linktree is the standard link-in-bio, and the click data underneath is surprisingly honest: what your audience actually clicks on, merch, tickets, a new release, or your site, says more about intent than any vanity metric. It is a small window into what people genuinely want. The limit is that Linktree shows those clicks in isolation. You see that a link does well, but not which post or which moment drove the traffic, and without that link it stays a number with no cause. So you know something works but not why, which means you cannot repeat it. Stevin reads your Linktree clicks and lines them up against your social posts, so it becomes visible which content produced which traffic. Whatever forms a pattern surfaces as a signal with a proposal to build on, and you keep control.
linktree.stackImpact: Linktree gives you click data, but richer export and connections often sit behind the paid plan, so check whether your subscription delivers the data you want. The clicks sit apart from your social posts, so for the link you need your post data and good UTMs. On its own a click counter is an outcome with no cause. In practice: let Linktree catch the clicks and let a layer on top tie them to which post drove the traffic, so you not only see that a link works but also why, and can repeat it instead of guessing.
pitfalls: Looking at clicks without tying them to a specific post, so the cause stays unknown.
Assuming all the data is free when better export sits behind the paid plan.
Not using UTMs consistently, so the source of the traffic cannot be traced.

liveramp.shortDescription: Identity resolution and data collaboration for enterprise marketing.
liveramp.description: LiveRamp is the standard for identity resolution and data collaboration in retail, CPG and media. It matches offline and online identities on a deterministic basis and runs clean rooms for partner data.
liveramp.useCase: Identity resolution, audience onboarding and data clean rooms.
