liveramp.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI uses LiveRamp to match first-party data with advertising platforms, retail media networks and partner clean rooms, without raw PII leaving the organization.
problemsSolved: Offline customer data is not activatable in digital advertising
Retail media networks require identity onboarding
Sharing PII with partners carries compliance risk
liveramp.stevinAngle: LiveRamp is the de facto standard for identity resolution and data collaboration in retail, CPG and media. It matches offline and online identities on a deterministic basis and runs clean rooms for partner data, and that is work almost no one else does at this level. For anyone who wants to activate offline customer data in digital advertising or step into retail media networks, it is often not a choice but a requirement. The flip side is the weight: LiveRamp is enterprise infrastructure with the contracts and complexity to match, not something you add on the side. Where teams get stuck is the assumption that onboarding is the same as activation. The match delivers reach, but what you do with it stays a separate question. Stevin uses LiveRamp to match first-party data with advertising platforms and clean rooms without raw PII leaving the organization, and turns the activated audiences into signals with follow-up, with a person reviewing every action that carries weight first.
liveramp.stackImpact: Choosing LiveRamp means access to identity onboarding and clean rooms that make retail media and partner collaboration possible, with the governance that raw PII stays inside your organization. Against that stand enterprise complexity, contract work and a serious price. It is a foundation for data collaboration, not a plug-and-play tool you add on the side. In practice: make sure your first-party data is clean and matchable, because the value of LiveRamp starts with the quality of the identities you bring into it, and a messy source produces a messy match.
pitfalls: Confusing onboarding with activation: a match delivers reach, not a filled-in strategy.
Underestimating the enterprise complexity and contract burden for an organization that does not need it.
Supplying first-party data without cleaning it, resulting in a messy match.
Assuming clean rooms handle compliance entirely without your own governance around it.

looker-studio.shortDescription: Free dashboard tool from Google for data visualization.
looker-studio.description: Looker Studio (formerly Data Studio) is a free tool for building dashboards and reports. It connects data from dozens of sources into clear visualizations.
looker-studio.useCase: Central dashboards that combine data from multiple marketing tools.
looker-studio.howWeUseIt: Stevin builds Looker Studio dashboards that show you at a glance how your campaigns, website and leads perform. No noise, only relevant KPIs.
problemsSolved: Reporting takes too much time
Data from different tools is not combined
No clear overview of marketing performance
looker-studio.stevinAngle: Looker Studio (formerly Data Studio) is free and flexible, but that comes at a price: slow dashboards, limited transformation options, and hard to scale beyond a handful of data sources. For SMBs with basic reporting needs (GA4, Google Ads, GSC combined) it is fine. For multi-platform attribution or cross-tool dashboards you quickly hit limits and have to move toward Tableau, Looker (the paid version) or Metabase. We use it ourselves for client reporting; internally we work in BigQuery plus a custom UI.
looker-studio.stackImpact: For your stack: always connect through an intermediate layer (BigQuery views or an ETL tool like Fivetran), not directly on live APIs. Connecting straight to GA4 looks easy, but dashboards become slow and fragile to API changes. Build one template dashboard and duplicate it per client instead of 30 unique dashboards nobody maintains.
pitfalls: Not noticing sampled data in the GA4 connector, so figures in the dashboard do not match the GA4 UI
Using custom fields as calculations that should have lived in BigQuery, performance drops
Setting sharing permissions loosely (Anyone with link), so a competitor can view the dashboard
Building dashboards around a metric that later gets renamed in the source, refactoring is manual work

magento.description: Magento (Adobe Commerce) is a powerful e-commerce platform for larger webshops with complex requirements. Flexible but technically demanding.
magento.useCase: Enterprise e-commerce with complex product catalogs and integrations.
magento.howWeUseIt: Stevin makes sure your Magento webshop is properly connected to your marketing stack: from tracking and product feeds to CRM and automation.
problemsSolved: Magento integrations are technically complex
Marketing and shop data are not synced
magento.stevinAngle: Magento, now Adobe Commerce, is powerful for larger webshops with complex catalogs, and technically heavy enough that you need a developer alongside it. That is the honest side: the flexibility costs maintenance, and a Magento without serious technical management gets slow and brittle. We run into it at clients with a real catalog challenge, and there it earns its keep. Where teams get stuck is the connection to the marketing stack: product feeds, tracking, and CRM often lag behind what happens in the shop. Stevin puts a layer over that, reads order and product data through the API, and turns deviations into signals, a feed that is off, a conversion that is not coming through, with a person reviewing every intervention that carries weight first.
magento.stackImpact: Choosing Magento means you plan in technical maintenance: it is not a platform that keeps itself running, and the hosting and updates need attention. The integrations are complex, so count on work on your product feeds and tracking before the marketing data holds up. It gives a lot of control, but you pay for it in management. The question is whether your catalog and volume genuinely justify that complexity, or whether a lighter platform suits you better.
pitfalls: Choosing Magento without technical management: it gets slow and the integrations break.
Product feeds that lag behind the shop, so you advertise on stale data.
Leaving e-commerce tracking incomplete, so conversions do not come through.

mailchimp.shortDescription: Email marketing and basic automation for SMBs.
mailchimp.description: Mailchimp is one of the best-known email marketing platforms. Easy to use, with options for newsletters, automations, and landing pages.
mailchimp.useCase: Email newsletters and basic automation for SMBs.
mailchimp.howWeUseIt: Stevin connects Mailchimp to your CRM and lead sources so new leads land in the right list automatically and get the right follow-up flow.
problemsSolved: New leads are not added to email lists automatically
Email campaigns are not connected to CRM data
mailchimp.stevinAngle: In 2026 Mailchimp is a fine entry-level tool and a poor primary platform for growing companies. The line sits around 10,000 contacts or 50 euros a month: below that Mailchimp is cheap and simple, above it you pay for features you get for free elsewhere. We regularly migrate from Mailchimp to ActiveCampaign or Klaviyo when a client crosses that threshold, it takes a week of work and structurally saves hundreds a month plus opens up automation options Mailchimp does not offer.
mailchimp.stackImpact: For anyone who does stay on Mailchimp: use tags instead of lists (lists overlap, tags are flexible), switch on double opt-in by default despite it lowering your conversion rate (long-term deliverability matters more), and connect to your site through the native API instead of Zapier bridges (faster, more reliable, no rate limits). The API connection is free and most accounts do not use it.
pitfalls: Letting the audience counter climb without unsubscribing inactive contacts, you pay for an empty list
Duplicating templates over and over instead of one template plus content blocks, maintenance becomes brand-inconsistent
Building automations that sit in series instead of as trigger-based workflows, mistimed sends
No sending-domain authentication (DKIM/SPF/DMARC), emails land in spam despite good content

make.shortDescription: Visual automation tool for complex workflows.
make.description: Make (formerly Integromat) is a powerful automation tool with a visual interface. Suited to workflows more complex than Zapier, with more control over data flows.
make.useCase: Complex, visual marketing automations with advanced logic.
make.howWeUseIt: Stevin uses Make for complex automations where Zapier falls short: multi-step scenarios, conditional logic, and data transformations.
problemsSolved: Automations are too complex for Zapier
You want a visual view of your workflows
make.stevinAngle: Make, formerly Integromat, is the tool you reach for when Zapier gets too thin. The visual interface lets you build multi-step scenarios, conditional logic, and data transformations with a level of control that simpler automation tools do not give you. For anyone who wants to actually see and steer their workflow, that is the strength. That strength is also the weakness. Make gives you so many options that scenarios quickly sprawl into a tangle of modules nobody but the builder understands. A complex automation that depends on one person carrying it in their head is a risk we run into often. And Make does what you set it to, it does not think about whether a step still makes sense. Where teams get stuck is exactly there: brittle scenarios that break quietly without anyone noticing. Stevin uses Make as the executing layer for the plumbing, but puts the intelligence and the monitoring on top, with a person seeing every action that carries weight first.
make.stackImpact: Choosing Make means you bring in a lot of automation power, but also the responsibility to keep your scenarios maintainable. Count on documentation and someone who understands the logic, otherwise every change is a guess in a maze. It is an executor, not a thinker, so complex scenarios need monitoring that notices when something breaks quietly. In practice: let Make do the plumbing between your tools and put a layer on top that watches whether the flow still holds and adds intelligence where Make only switches.
pitfalls: Letting scenarios sprawl until only the builder still understands them.
Letting a complex automation depend on one person who holds the logic in their head.
Assuming an executing tool also notices when a step breaks quietly.
Building without documentation, so every later change becomes a guess.

marigold-engage.shortDescription: Enterprise email and cross-channel marketing platform.
marigold-engage.description: Marigold Engage (formerly Selligent Marketing Cloud) is an enterprise marketing platform for email, SMS, push, and cross-channel campaigns. It is strong in personalization and AI-driven recommendations.
marigold-engage.useCase: Cross-channel marketing automation with AI personalization for enterprise.
marigold-engage.howWeUseIt: Stevin integrates Marigold Engage with your CRM and marketing channels and optimizes cross-channel journeys and personalization.
problemsSolved: Cross-channel campaigns are not coordinated
Personalization is not used in email and messaging
marigold-engage.stevinAngle: Marigold Engage, formerly Selligent, is an enterprise cross-channel platform that is strong in personalization and AI recommendations across email, SMS, and push. In practice you are buying scale and depth here, and that has a price in setup and management. We use it for larger organizations that genuinely want to coordinate across channels, not for a team that wants to send a newsletter. Where it pinches is the dependence on good customer data: the personalization and recommendations are only as good as what goes in, and with fragmented data it gets hollow fast. Stevin puts a layer over that, connects Marigold to your CRM and sources, and watches whether the cross-channel flows hold up, with a person reviewing every campaign that carries weight first.
marigold-engage.stackImpact: Choosing Marigold Engage means you have to have your customer data in order before the personalization is worth anything. The platform coordinates channels, but it pulls the data from your systems, so the weakest link is usually your own data source. Count on setting up the connections to your CRM and lead sources, not on a ready-made flow. The gain is in coordination across channels, provided the data underneath is consistent.
pitfalls: Expecting AI recommendations on fragmented customer data: then you are personalizing on noise.
Running cross-channel without the channels drawing on the same customer data.
Underestimating the setup: an enterprise platform needs management, not switching on and forgetting.

marketo-engage.shortDescription: Enterprise B2B marketing automation within Adobe Experience Cloud.
marketo-engage.description: Marketo Engage (Adobe) is the enterprise standard for B2B marketing automation. Lead nurturing, scoring, account-based marketing, and complex workflows for large sales organizations.
marketo-engage.useCase: Enterprise B2B nurturing, lead scoring, and account-based marketing.
marketo-engage.howWeUseIt: Stevin connects Marketo to your CRM, advertising, and MMM so campaigns, scoring, and nurturing flows work in line, and marketing contribution is visible down to opportunity level.
problemsSolved: Marketo flows run separate from media channels
Lead scoring is not connected to advertising audiences
ABM programs lack a connected attribution model
marketo-engage.stevinAngle: Marketo Engage, part of Adobe, is the enterprise standard for B2B nurturing and lead scoring. In practice it is strong where long sales cycles and complex scoring are in play, and heavy to manage where you do not need that. We use it for organizations with a real sales organization and account-based programs, not for a team that only sends newsletters. Where teams get stuck is that the flows start running separate from the media channels and the lead scoring takes on a life of its own without anyone checking whether the rules still hold. Stevin runs as a layer over Marketo, connects it to your CRM and advertising, and watches whether scoring and nurturing flows still work in line, with the person seeing every intervention that carries weight first.
marketo-engage.stackImpact: Choosing Marketo means you need a Marketo administrator: the flows, scoring, and sync with your CRM need ongoing maintenance. It works best when you have a serious B2B sales process with opportunities to tie back to, otherwise it is overkill. Count on connection time toward advertising audiences, because without that your scoring stays trapped inside Marketo. The gain is visibility down to opportunity level, provided the connections hold.
pitfalls: Choosing Marketo for simple email: you pay for and manage a B2B machine you do not fill.
Letting lead scoring run without anyone keeping the rules tested against reality.
Letting nurturing flows run separate from the media channels and CRM.

matomo.description: Matomo is an open-source alternative to Google Analytics. It gives full control over your data and can be hosted on your own server, which makes it ideal for privacy-conscious organizations.
matomo.useCase: Website analytics with full control over data and privacy.
matomo.howWeUseIt: Stevin implements and configures Matomo as an alternative to or addition to GA4, including connections to your advertising platforms and CRM.
problemsSolved: A need for privacy-friendly analytics
A wish to host data on your own servers
matomo.stevinAngle: Matomo is the privacy-friendly alternative to Google Analytics: open-source, and you can run it on your own server, so your data really stays yours. For organizations that care about privacy or data ownership, that is the whole reason to choose it. We use it as an alternative to or addition to GA4 with clients who do not want their data at Google. Where it pinches is that Matomo, like any analytics package, mostly records. It shows what happens, but does not turn that into action or into a warning when something deviates. The insights stay in the dashboard. Stevin runs as a layer on top of your stack and reads Matomo through the API, next to your advertising platforms and CRM. A conversion path that suddenly stalls, traffic that drops on an important page: that becomes a signal a person reviews, so that the privacy choice does not become a separate silo but part of the whole.
matomo.stackImpact: Choosing Matomo often means hosting it yourself, and then you are responsible for the server, updates and reliability that you do not have to arrange with GA4. Count on that maintenance as the price for the control you get back. The data comes in through the API and stays on your own infrastructure, so the question is not whether you own your data, but whether someone places the insights next to your advertising and CRM data. Without that connection, your privacy choice becomes a tidy analytics package that sits apart from the rest of your stack.
pitfalls: Hosting it yourself and underestimating the maintenance that comes with your own server.
Keeping Matomo separate from your advertising and CRM data, so it becomes a silo.
Leaving insights in the dashboard without anything watching for deviations.

mediahuis.shortDescription: Advertising on Mediahuis brands in the Netherlands and Belgium.
mediahuis.description: Mediahuis is a large media group with brands like De Telegraaf, NRC and Limburger. It offers display, video and native advertising in high-quality news environments.
mediahuis.useCase: Reach on premium news brands in the Benelux through display, video and native.
mediahuis.howWeUseIt: Stevin uses Mediahuis for awareness campaigns on premium inventory and connects the results to your broader tracking and reporting.
problemsSolved: Premium media buying is not measurably linked to your funnel
No integrated view across all media channels
mediahuis.stevinAngle: Mediahuis is the route to premium news environments in the Benelux, with brands like De Telegraaf and NRC. We recommend it where the environment itself adds value: an ad next to serious journalism reads differently than a banner on some random site. For awareness and brand, that is strong. Where teams get stuck is the bridge to results. You buy visibility with a good audience, but whether that visibility later leads to an inquiry or a purchase, you do not see that in the buying platform itself. It stays a spend that sits apart from your funnel. Stevin runs as a layer on top of your stack and connects the Mediahuis campaign data to your own tracking. A spike in traffic after a placement, a landing page that suddenly gets busier: that becomes a signal that surfaces and that a person can weigh, instead of an assumption that awareness will surely help.
mediahuis.stackImpact: Buying premium media with Mediahuis calls for your own analytics alongside it, because the effect sits downstream and not in the buying platform itself. You do not need an extra channel, but you do need a way to track traffic and conversion in the days after a placement and tie it to the right placement. In practice: place the campaign data next to your site analytics and your media mix, otherwise you judge an awareness spend on impressions alone. Then your picture of what works drifts apart from what actually comes in, and the placement stays a spend judged on feel.
pitfalls: Judging premium placements on impressions because the link to conversion is missing.
Keeping awareness spend separate from your site analytics, leaving the effect invisible.
Assuming a good audience turns into results on its own without tracking it.

mediamarkt-retail-media.shortDescription: Retail media advertising on MediaMarkt channels.
mediamarkt-retail-media.description: MediaMarkt Retail Media lets brands grow their visibility on the MediaMarkt platform. Ideal for electronics and tech brands that want to reach shoppers at the moment of purchase.
mediamarkt-retail-media.useCase: Growing product visibility and conversion on MediaMarkt's digital channels.
mediamarkt-retail-media.howWeUseIt: Stevin manages MediaMarkt Retail Media campaigns and integrates the results into your broader media reporting for a complete picture.
problemsSolved: Retail media results are not compared with other channels
No centralized view across all media channels including retail media
mediamarkt-retail-media.stevinAngle: MediaMarkt Retail Media makes sense for electronics and tech brands: you advertise on the platform where the shopper is already looking at a TV or laptop, right before the purchase. That purchase moment is exactly the value. We use it where the product range fits MediaMarkt and the audience genuinely buys there. Where it pinches is the same pattern as with other retail media: its own environment with its own figures that rarely stand next to the rest of your channels. You know how a campaign did inside MediaMarkt, but not how it compares to your other spend. Stevin runs as a layer on top of your stack and pulls the campaign data in through export, so it stands next to your other channels. A campaign that eats spend without return or a product that suddenly runs hot: that becomes a signal a person sees in time, instead of something that only stands out at the month-end close.
mediamarkt-retail-media.stackImpact: Choosing MediaMarkt Retail Media means you want the results in your total media picture, otherwise the comparison with your other channels is missing. You need your media mix alongside it to see whether the euro does its work here. The risk is a loose retail report that nobody weighs against the rest. In practice: make sure the data from MediaMarkt lands in the same view as your other spend, because without that comparison you steer on a platform figure and not on what it earns across the business.
pitfalls: Keeping MediaMarkt figures separate, so you cannot weigh them against other channels.
Using it when the audience does not really buy there: the purchase moment is the whole value.
Seeing deviations only at the month-end close instead of when they arise.

memorable-ai.shortDescription: Predictive creative effectiveness based on deep learning.
memorable-ai.description: Memorable AI predicts the effectiveness of ads before they go live. The model is trained on millions of ads and predicts recall, engagement, and conversion potential based on visual and textual elements.
memorable-ai.useCase: Pre-launch effectiveness prediction and creative optimization.
memorable-ai.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI uses Memorable AI as an extra validation layer in the creative process. Alongside attention heatmaps (Neurons) you get an effectiveness score that predicts how the ad will perform on recall and action.
problemsSolved: No way to predict ad effectiveness before launch
Creative decisions only get validated after the fact
No objective comparison between creative variants
memorable-ai.stevinAngle: Memorable AI promises something appealing: predicting the effectiveness of an ad before it goes live. Trained on millions of ads, it gives a score on recall and action before you have spent budget. As an extra check before launch, that is valuable. Just keep in mind what it is: a prediction based on what worked on average, not a guarantee for your audience. The score is a guideline, not a verdict, and anyone who treats it as truth ends up disappointed. Teams get stuck there: the prediction replaces the testing instead of supplementing it. Stevin uses Memorable as one of several signals, not the only voice. It reads the pre-launch score via API and lays it next to your actual performance after launch, so the prediction keeps getting adjusted on what really happens in your channels. The consultant keeps the final decision.
memorable-ai.stackImpact: Memorable AI gives you a verdict before launch, but it does not close the loop: only after launch do you know whether the prediction held. Count on linking the score to your real results, alongside your ad and conversion data, otherwise it stays a loose opinion with no calibration. The value is not in the prediction alone, but in systematically comparing predicted and actual, round after round. Without that feedback the model never calibrates on your market and stays an average that may not be about your audience at all.
pitfalls: Treating a prediction as certainty instead of a guideline.
Never testing the pre-launch score against what the ad actually did afterward.
Letting the prediction replace the testing instead of supplementing it.
Leaning on a general model without calibrating it to your audience.

meta-ads.shortDescription: Advertising on Facebook and Instagram for reach and lead generation.
meta-ads.description: Meta Ads gives you access to Facebook and Instagram. Ideal for reach, retargeting and lead generation. The strength is in the targeting and the volume, but without solid tracking and follow-up you cannot see what it produces.
meta-ads.useCase: Lead generation, retargeting and brand awareness through social advertising.
meta-ads.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI connects Meta Ads to your CRM and automation. We implement the Conversions API for reliable data delivery and make sure leads from lead forms land directly in your CRM with the right follow-up.
problemsSolved: Leads from lead forms are not picked up automatically
Conversion data is unreliable due to cookie loss
No link between ads and actual revenue
meta-ads.stevinAngle: Since iOS 14, Meta Ads has had a measurement problem that most accounts hide behind the Conversions API and advanced modeling. The reality: 30 to 50 percent of the conversions shown in Ads Manager are modeled, not measured. We implement the server-side Conversions API by default, but we only believe the number after an independent uplift measurement. On accounts where that has been done, Meta often turns out to be stronger on upper-funnel awareness and weaker on direct conversion than the dashboard suggests.
meta-ads.stackImpact: The Conversions API is no longer optional, it is the foundation. On top of that you tie lead forms straight to your CRM so the 24-hour follow-up starts automatically (Meta leads not called within 5 minutes convert 8x lower). For your reporting: separate 'Meta-attributed conversions' from 'CRM-attributed customers' in your dashboards. The gap between the two is your real work.
pitfalls: Using lead forms without a real-time webhook to the CRM, leads cool off sharply within an hour
Optimizing conversions on the 'Lead' event instead of on a qualified-lead event from your CRM
Building lookalike audiences on a seed list of fewer than 1000 customers, the model has too little signal
Running ASC (Advantage+ Shopping Campaigns) without checking whether it cannibalizes existing buyers

metabase.shortDescription: Open-source BI tool for fast data analysis.
metabase.description: Metabase is an open-source business intelligence tool that makes it easy to ask questions of your data. You can build dashboards and explore data without knowing SQL.
metabase.useCase: Low-barrier data analysis and dashboards on your own database.
metabase.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI connects Metabase to your marketing database or data warehouse so your team can explore data and build reports on its own.
problemsSolved: Data analysis is only accessible to technical team members
No low-barrier tool to visualize data from your database
metabase.stevinAngle: Metabase does the BI world a favor by being approachable: open source, and your team asks questions of the data without any SQL involved. We connect it to the marketing database or warehouse for clients who want to look around quickly themselves without paying for a heavy enterprise tool. Where it gets tight is that the simplicity is also the ceiling: for heavy models and strict governance you hit the edges sooner than with the big players. And like any dashboard tool, Metabase is passive. It will show you an anomaly neatly, but it taps no one on the shoulder. That is where Stevin sits. Through the same database, Stevin reads the numbers along with you and raises a signal the moment a value drifts or hits a threshold, with concrete follow-up underneath and a person reviewing anything that carries weight first. Metabase opens the data, Stevin watches it.
metabase.stackImpact: Metabase runs on your own database or warehouse, so the data has to be correct and fresh there already: it is a window, not a pipeline. The win is that your team can look for itself without a technical barrier, the risk is that everyone spins up a dashboard and no one acts on it. In practice: connect it to a solid data layer and be strict about who owns follow-up. The question that remains is not whether your team can see the data, but whether anyone notices when the numbers are saying something.
pitfalls: Assuming an open database automatically means clean, fresh data.
Letting a pile of one-off dashboards appear that no one acts on.
Stretching Metabase to heavy models it was never built for.
Confusing being able to ask questions with following up: the tool does nothing itself.

metacom.shortDescription: ERP for metal, steel construction and installation firms.
metacom.description: Metacom is an industry ERP for the metal, steel construction and installation sector: from estimating and work preparation to production, hours and invoicing.
metacom.useCase: Manage the production and project administration of technical and steel construction firms.
metacom.howWeUseIt: Stevin puts a work layer on top of Metacom and turns production and project data into signals: a delivery that has not been confirmed, a production step that is running late, a margin under pressure. Stevin does not replace Metacom, it makes sure what is in there leads to action in time. Connect through the API or an export.
problemsSolved: Production and project information is scattered
Delays in production or delivery surface too late
Margin risk on an order is seen too late
Follow-up on open actions happens by hand
metacom.stevinAngle: Metacom is an industry ERP for metal, steel construction and installation, and it covers the whole chain: estimating, work preparation, production, hours and invoicing. For production firms that is exactly the breadth you want. The downside of that breadth is the same as with any full ERP: everything is in there, so nothing asks for attention on its own. We see work planners and project leads stall on this: a delivery that has not been confirmed and will hold up production later, a production step that runs late, a margin under pressure on an order without anyone noticing. Metacom records it neatly, but it does not ring the bell. Stevin puts a layer on top, through the API or an export, and turns production and project data into signals with a concrete action. Stevin does not replace Metacom, it makes sure a deviation surfaces in time instead of at the final reckoning.
metacom.stackImpact: Metacom covers production and project administration broadly, so functionally there is little you need to add. The gain is in the monitoring on top of the chain, not in an extra system. The connection runs through the API or an export. The real question is which moments you want to see early: an unconfirmed delivery that will stop the line, a step running late, margin pressure on an order. Without something scanning for that, you lean on the system's cycle and only see the problem once it is already in the planning or the margin.
pitfalls: Ignoring an unconfirmed delivery until the production line is waiting on it.
Only seeing a production step running late once the whole planning has shifted.
Missing margin pressure on an order because it disappears into the broader ERP figures.
Working through open actions by hand, so dependent on whoever remembers.

microsoft-advertising.shortDescription: Advertising on Bing and the Microsoft network.
microsoft-advertising.description: Microsoft Advertising (formerly Bing Ads) gives you access to the Microsoft search network. Often lower cost per click than Google, with an interesting audience for B2B and older demographics.
microsoft-advertising.useCase: Search advertising on Bing as a complement to Google Ads.
microsoft-advertising.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI manages Microsoft Advertising as part of your multichannel strategy. We make sure tracking and conversions are consistent across all search platforms.
problemsSolved: Inconsistent tracking between Google and Bing
An underused channel with potentially lower cost per lead
microsoft-advertising.stevinAngle: Microsoft Advertising is treated by most advertisers as a copy of Google Ads with a lower CPC. That is understandable, but it misses the point. In practice we see at clients that the user intent on the Microsoft network is noticeably different: a higher share of desktop sessions, an older audience, and a remarkably strong presence of business decision-makers through the integration with LinkedIn profile data for targeting. That makes the channel more effective for B2B clients than the volume figure suggests. What we find during implementations: conversion tracking in Microsoft Advertising is misconfigured more often than at Google, simply because it gets less attention. The result is false confidence in the Google data, while part of the cause-and-effect chain plays out on Bing. So we always start with a tracking audit before we scale campaigns, even if the account is already 'live'.
microsoft-advertising.stackImpact: Microsoft Advertising works cleanest when your measurement data is consistent with Google Ads. In practice that means: a shared tag manager implementation (Google Tag Manager or an equivalent), a CRM connection if you want to import offline conversions, and a unified reporting layer like Looker Studio or a data warehouse where both platforms land. Automatically importing Google Ads campaigns works as a starting point, but without adjustment it leads to suboptimal structures. Count on a separate connection for your conversion data and, if you use Microsoft Clarity, on a meaningful link with Advertising for behavioral data per campaign.
pitfalls: The 'import from Google Ads' feature does not overwrite your existing bid strategies by default, so you unknowingly run with incompatible settings if you later adjust by hand.
Universal Event Tracking (UET) and Google tags are not interchangeable: if you only install a Google tag, Microsoft Advertising records no conversions at all, without an error message.

LinkedIn targeting in Microsoft Advertising is available as a layer, but it raises the minimum CPCs and shrinks reach sharply. Without a volume check up front you burn budget on a segment that is too small.
Auto-bidding in Microsoft Advertising needs significantly more conversion data to stabilize than Google's Smart Bidding. At low volumes the system steers on noise instead of on signal.

microsoft-clarity.shortDescription: Free heatmaps and session recordings from Microsoft.
microsoft-clarity.description: Microsoft Clarity is a free alternative to heatmap tools. It offers session recordings, heatmaps and insight into user behavior without data limits.
microsoft-clarity.useCase: Free visual analysis of user behavior on your website.
microsoft-clarity.howWeUseIt: Stevin implements Clarity as an addition to your analytics stack for visual user insights, especially valuable for optimizing landing pages.
problemsSolved: No budget for paid heatmap tools
A need for visual insight into user behavior
microsoft-clarity.stevinAngle: Microsoft Clarity gives you free heatmaps and session recordings without data limits, and that is where the value sits: visual insight into behavior that you pay for elsewhere. We use it as an addition to the analytics stack, especially to understand and improve landing pages. Where it pinches is that Clarity lets you look, but summarizes or signals nothing. You see recordings and heatmaps, but you have to go through them yourself to find a pattern, and at volume that becomes a lot of manual work. A page where people drop off in droves can stay unnoticed simply because nobody has the time to watch every session. Stevin runs as a layer on top of your stack and uses the Clarity insights next to your conversion data and media spend, so that a page where behavior changes notably becomes a signal a person looks at. That way Clarity points to the spot and Stevin makes sure the right person looks at it in time.
microsoft-clarity.stackImpact: Choosing Clarity costs nothing and gives you rich visual data, but that data is only valuable if someone takes the time to go through recordings and heatmaps. Count on that manual work, because Clarity summarizes nothing for you. The insights stand on their own, so in practice you place them next to your conversion data and your spend, otherwise you know how people click but not what it costs you. Without that connection, Clarity stays a nice but loose bin of sessions that nobody watches in full.
pitfalls: Collecting heatmaps and recordings without the time to pull a pattern out of them.
Keeping Clarity separate from your conversion data, so behavior and cost never meet.
Missing a page with heavy drop-off because nobody watches every session.

microsoft-customer-insights.description: Microsoft Customer Insights is the CDP within the Dynamics 365 ecosystem. It brings together customer data from CRM, transactions and behavior and offers AI-driven insights and segmentation.
microsoft-customer-insights.useCase: Centralize and enrich customer data inside the Microsoft ecosystem.
microsoft-customer-insights.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI connects Microsoft Customer Insights to marketing channels and makes sure customer profiles get enriched with campaign data for better segmentation and personalization.
problemsSolved: Customer data inside Microsoft Dynamics is not unified
No AI-driven insights based on customer behavior
Segmentation is not based on complete customer data
microsoft-customer-insights.stevinAngle: Microsoft Customer Insights is the CDP within Dynamics 365, and the logic is right there: if you already live in the Microsoft house, it brings together CRM, transactions and behavior without you having to step outside. The AI-driven insights and segmentation hook neatly into the rest of Dynamics. Outside that ecosystem, much of that appeal disappears. Where teams get stuck: customer data inside Dynamics is often less unified than assumed, and the AI insights are only as good as the data underneath. A segment that looks smart but runs on half the data sends you in the wrong direction. Stevin connects Customer Insights to your marketing channels, reads the profiles and segments and enriches them with campaign data into signals with follow-up underneath, with a person reviewing every action that carries weight first.
microsoft-customer-insights.stackImpact: Choosing Customer Insights pays off mostly if you already run on Dynamics 365, because then the sources are already within reach and management stays in a familiar ecosystem. Outside Microsoft, the added value over a neutral CDP is limited and you pay for integration you do not use. It delivers AI insights, but those stand or fall with the unification underneath. In practice: make sure your Dynamics data is genuinely unified before you trust the AI segmentation, and connect the profiles to your channels, because insight inside the platform only changes anything once it reaches your campaigns.
pitfalls: Deploying Customer Insights without a Dynamics footprint, so the ecosystem advantage falls away.
Trusting AI insights while the underlying data is not genuinely unified.
Segmenting on half the data and steering campaigns the wrong way as a result.
Leaving profiles in the platform without connecting them to your marketing channels.

microsoft-dynamics-365-crm.shortDescription: Enterprise CRM integrated with the Microsoft ecosystem.
microsoft-dynamics-365-crm.description: Microsoft Dynamics 365 is an enterprise CRM that integrates closely with Outlook, Teams, and the rest of the Microsoft ecosystem.
microsoft-dynamics-365-crm.useCase: A CRM for organizations already working with Microsoft 365.
microsoft-dynamics-365-crm.howWeUseIt: Stevin connects Dynamics 365 to your marketing stack and makes sure lead data from campaigns lands in your CRM automatically and in the right format.
problemsSolved: Marketing data does not reach the CRM automatically
No integrated view of marketing and sales activity
microsoft-dynamics-365-crm.stevinAngle: Dynamics 365 makes sense if you are already fully in Microsoft. The tie to Outlook, Teams, and the rest of the ecosystem is exactly where it is strong, and for organizations already running there it saves a separate login world. We use it where Microsoft is the standard and another CRM would work against the current. The flip side is significant: Dynamics is an enterprise heavyweight, and that power comes with complexity. Setting it up takes specialists, it is expensive, and it can feel clunky for teams that want speed. For SMBs it is often more machine than needed. Where teams get stuck is that marketing data does not reach the CRM on its own and that marketing and sales have no shared view. Stevin connects to Dynamics through the API, makes sure lead data from campaigns comes in the right format, and turns an open action into a signal. The person reviews every intervention first.
microsoft-dynamics-365-crm.stackImpact: Choosing Dynamics means you bring in the Microsoft integration, but also the implementation load and the cost of an enterprise system. Count on specialists for the setup, because this is not a tool you stand up in an afternoon. Marketing data does not land in the right place automatically, so you have to build that connection to get a shared view between marketing and sales. In practice: worthwhile if you are already in Microsoft, otherwise weigh the heft carefully against what you actually need.
pitfalls: Choosing Dynamics for an SMB team that does not need the enterprise heft.
Underestimating the implementation: without specialists it stalls.
Assuming the Microsoft tie also pulls your marketing data in on its own.
Expecting marketing and sales on the same platform without the data actually coming together.

mixpanel.shortDescription: Product analytics for SaaS and digital products.
mixpanel.description: Mixpanel is a leading product analytics platform, widely used in B2B SaaS and consumer apps. It maps event-based user behavior, funnels, retention, and cohorts.
mixpanel.useCase: Product analytics, funnel analysis, and cohort retention in digital products.
mixpanel.howWeUseIt: Stevin connects Mixpanel to your ad channels, CRM, and CDP so product events carry through to marketing and sales, and activation moments also drive acquisition decisions.
problemsSolved: Product data stays inside the product team
No link between activation and acquisition channels
No cohort retention visible to marketing
mixpanel.stevinAngle: Mixpanel competes directly with Amplitude for product analytics. The difference is mostly in the pricing model and the developer experience. Mixpanel charges per Monthly Tracked User (MTU), Amplitude per event. For apps with many events per user Mixpanel is cheaper, for apps with many users and few events Amplitude is cheaper. We see teams pick based on what a colleague used somewhere else, not on their own event-to-user ratio. Do the math before you sign.
mixpanel.stackImpact: For your stack: send events through the SDK directly, with user.identify() at login to link anonymous and known users. Combine it with Segment or your own event bus if you also want to send the same events elsewhere (data warehouse, attribution tool). Funnel analysis works best when you name events consistently in the past tense ('signup_completed' not 'complete signup'). Mixpanel's built-in A/B testing is fine but not on the level of dedicated tools like Optimizely or GrowthBook.
pitfalls: Tracking anonymous and known without an identify call at the right moment, user journeys break in two
Creating events without properties, you cannot filter later by product tier or campaign
Letting MTU climb by counting bots or test accounts, the pricing tier jumps unexpectedly
Building cohort analysis on samples, Mixpanel samples by default on large queries, you have to switch that off explicitly

motion.shortDescription: Creative analytics for paid social: which ads work and why.
motion.description: Motion analyzes your ads at creative level and links visual elements to performance metrics. Which hook works best? Which color scheme converts? Motion makes it measurable.
motion.useCase: Creative-level performance analysis and data-driven creative iteration.
motion.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI integrates Motion's creative analytics into the Advisor. Instead of "ad set 3 performs better" you get "ads with a problem statement as the hook and warm color tones convert 34% better in this audience."
problemsSolved: Performance gets reported at ad set level, not creative level
No view of which visual elements drive conversion
Creative iteration is trial-and-error instead of data-driven
The link between creative concept and ROAS is invisible
motion.stevinAngle: Motion does something the ad platforms themselves do poorly: it reports at creative level instead of ad set level. Which hook holds attention, which color scheme converts, that makes it measurable, and for paid social that is exactly the layer that is missing. The limit is that Motion analyzes but does not act. It shows that ads opening with a problem statement do better, and there it stops. Someone still has to translate that lesson into the next round and make sure it does not evaporate between campaigns. Teams get stuck there: the insight is there, the follow-through is not. Stevin pulls Motion's creative analytics in via API and turns it into a concrete brief and a signal: this hook works in this audience, make more of it, this variant is leaking budget. The consultant sees every recommendation with impact before anything changes.
motion.stackImpact: Choosing Motion means you finally measure at creative level, but you need a layer on top that turns the finding into action and into a next brief. It reads your ad channels, so the data is there, only nothing moves on its own. Count on a link between Motion and your creative production, and on someone or something that holds the lesson between campaigns, otherwise the finding stays stuck in a dashboard nobody saves at the right moment. The insight is only valuable when something downstream reacts to it and carries it into the next round.
pitfalls: Collecting creative insights that nobody turns into a next brief.
Opening a dashboard after the campaign instead of during.
Letting the lesson from one round evaporate before the next starts.
Measuring at creative level but still steering at ad set level.

faqs.question: How is Motion different from the reports in Meta Ads Manager?
faqs.answer: Meta reports at the ad level. Motion goes deeper: it labels visual and text elements (hook type, colour, format) and correlates them with performance. That surfaces patterns you would never spot in Ads Manager.

mparticle.shortDescription: CDP for real-time customer data and integrations.
mparticle.description: mParticle is a CDP that collects, enriches, and distributes customer data in real time to your marketing and analytics tools.
mparticle.useCase: Real-time customer data integration across all channels.
mparticle.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI uses mParticle for organizations that need real-time data flows between their marketing and product tools.
problemsSolved: Data does not reach tools in real time
Customer profiles are not current across all channels
mparticle.stevinAngle: mParticle is a CDP built around real time: collecting, enriching, and immediately passing customer data on to your marketing and product tools. That real-time character is the real reason to choose it, and it comes into its own most with product teams that want to respond to behavior in the moment. If you do not need that speed, it is overkill. Where teams get stuck is the idea that real-time data is automatically real-time value. The streams move fast, but without something that picks the right signal out at the right moment, it flows right past you. Stevin reads the mParticle streams through the API, recognizes the pattern that matters (a profile that changes behavior, a segment that shifts), and puts follow-up underneath, with a person seeing every action that carries weight first.
mparticle.stackImpact: Choosing mParticle means choosing speed in your data streams, and there is a price tag on that which only pays off if you actually use that speed. It collects and distributes in real time, but it does not decide what an event means. Count on work to connect your tools to the streams correctly and to watch data quality at the source. The practical approach: put a layer on top that responds to the relevant events, because otherwise you have expensive real-time pipelines that pass data along without anything happening.
pitfalls: Choosing mParticle without a real real-time need: you pay for speed that sits idle.
Assuming real-time data is the same as real-time action.
Passing streams on to tools without something that picks the relevant events out.
Profiles that stay current but never set a decision in motion anywhere.

neurons.shortDescription: Predictive attention heatmaps and creative effectiveness scores.
neurons.description: Neurons uses AI models trained on neuroscience to predict where viewers look, what they remember, and what moves them. From static ads to video: you know before launch whether your creative grabs attention.
neurons.useCase: Pre-launch creative testing on attention, memory, and engagement.
neurons.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI connects Neurons to the creative process. Before an ad goes live, Stevin checks the visual hierarchy: does the CTA draw attention? Is the brand remembered? The result is an objective score that speeds up creative discussions.
problemsSolved: Creative choices only get validated afterward with campaign data
No objective measure for the visual effectiveness of ads
Expensive A/B tests that pre-testing could have prevented
Creative discussions drag on because there is no data
neurons.stevinAngle: Neurons uses AI trained on neuroscience to predict where viewers look, what they remember, and what moves them, before an ad is even live. The strength is that it shifts a creative discussion from opinions to a measurement: does the CTA draw attention, does the brand stick. It is a prediction, not a guarantee, and that is exactly where teams get it wrong. Treat the score as the final verdict and you skip the real conversation about the message, when the point is to speed that conversation up. And a high attention score says nothing about whether the right message landed. Stevin connects Neurons to the creative process and checks the visual hierarchy before an ad goes out, so problems surface early instead of only in the campaign data. The output is an objective starting point for the conversation, not a replacement for it, and a person decides.
neurons.stackImpact: Neurons gives you a predicted score on your creatives, but it is a model you feed with your designs, so the value depends on whether you use it early in the process and not just on the final version. It measures attention and memory, not whether the message is right, so your strategic judgment is still needed. On its own a score is a snapshot without context. In practice: use Neurons as a pre-launch check alongside your creative judgment and let a layer on top flag the problems, so expensive A/B tests after the fact become partly unnecessary instead of being the only way to validate.
pitfalls: Taking the predicted score as the final verdict and skipping the conversation about the message.
Only testing on the final version, when there is barely any room left to adjust.
Assuming high attention means the right message got through.

faqs.question: Does Neurons replace an A/B test?
faqs.answer: No, but it filters out the weak variants up front. You only test the ones that clear the attention threshold, which makes your testing budget go further.

faqs.question: Does this work for video too?
faqs.answer: Yes. Neurons analyses both static images and video frames for attention and engagement.

nielseniq.shortDescription: Market share, purchase behavior, and FMCG consumer intelligence.
nielseniq.description: NielsenIQ delivers market share data, purchase behavior, and retail trends based on point-of-sale data and panel research. The gold standard for FMCG and retail brands that want to know how they perform relative to the market.
nielseniq.useCase: Market share tracking, category analysis, and retail performance monitoring.
nielseniq.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI links NielsenIQ market data to your digital campaign performance. That way you see directly whether a rise in ad spend actually delivers market share: the ultimate validation of your marketing investment.
problemsSolved: No link between digital campaigns and market share
Campaign impact only gets measured on clicks, not on sales
Category trends get flagged too late
nielseniq.stevinAngle: For FMCG and retail, NielsenIQ is the measure that matters: market share and purchase behavior based on point-of-sale data and panels. It does not tell you whether your ad was clickable, but whether you actually sold relative to the category. That is exactly the kind of truth marketing often lacks. The downside is timing and granularity: the data comes with a delay and is aggregated, so you steer on the past and on large units, not on yesterday. Teams get stuck there: digital campaigns and market share stay two separate worlds. Stevin links NielsenIQ market data to your digital campaign performance, so you see whether a rise in spend translates into market share and not just into clicks. It flags when the two diverge, and the consultant judges what that means before any budget shifts.
nielseniq.stackImpact: NielsenIQ gives you the outcome that counts, sales and share, but it comes slow and coarse, so it is not a day-to-day steering wheel. Count on a layer that lays the market data next to your real-time campaign data, otherwise you look at two dashboards that never touch. The gain is in connecting the slow, hard signal with the fast, rough signal from your channels. Without that you know you advertised and you know your share moved, but never whether one caused the other.
pitfalls: Wanting to steer on delayed, aggregated data as if it were from yesterday.
Leaving digital campaigns and market share as two separate worlds.
Not laying the market data next to your real-time campaign data.
Measuring campaign impact only on clicks and ignoring the real sales.

northbeam.shortDescription: Multi-touch attribution and media mix analysis for e-commerce.
northbeam.description: Northbeam combines multi-touch attribution with machine learning to measure the real impact of every touchpoint in the customer journey. Built for e-commerce brands that want to look beyond last-click.
northbeam.useCase: Multi-touch attribution, creative-level performance, and channel uplift.
northbeam.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI uses Northbeam's granular attribution data to analyze creative-level performance. Not just "Meta works," but "this specific creative hook in this audience delivers the highest incremental value."
problemsSolved: Attribution data is too coarse to steer creative decisions
Multi-touch customer journeys do not get valued correctly
No link between creative performance and incremental revenue
northbeam.stevinAngle: Northbeam looks beyond last-click: with multi-touch attribution and machine learning it tries to weigh the contribution of every touchpoint in the customer journey, down to creative level. For e-commerce brands that understand the last tap is not the whole story, that gives a richer picture than the standard reporting. The caveat is that multi-touch models make assumptions about how value gets spread across touchpoints, and that split is a choice, not a measurement. Teams get stuck there: they treat the assigned value as fact and steer hard on it. Stevin uses Northbeam's granular attribution to read creative-level performance and links it to your broader cross-validation, so you do not just learn that a channel works, but which hook in which audience adds the most value. Every recommendation with budget impact goes past the consultant first.
northbeam.stackImpact: Northbeam gives you attribution fine enough to steer creative choices with, but it stays a model with its own way of splitting value across the touchpoints. Count on laying the results next to other measurements and not treating it as the only truth, however convincing the detail looks. The gain is in granularity plus control: the detail that backs a creative choice, weighed against a second source. Without that cross-check you optimize your creatives on a split the model chose, not on what demonstrably brought the revenue.
pitfalls: Treating the assigned value as fact while the split is a choice.
Steering hard on a model without laying it next to a second measurement.
Optimizing creatives on a split the model chose.
Confusing granularity with certainty: fine detail is not yet proof.

onetrust.shortDescription: Enterprise privacy and consent management platform.
onetrust.description: OneTrust is an enterprise privacy platform that offers consent management, data mapping and compliance automation.
onetrust.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI implements OneTrust and makes sure it is correctly integrated with your tracking and Google Consent Mode.
problemsSolved: Enterprise privacy compliance is complex
Consent management is not connected to tracking
onetrust.stevinAngle: OneTrust is the heavy artillery: consent, data mapping and compliance automation in one platform, built for organizations that genuinely have to prove something legally. We recommend it where the requirements are large and a light banner tool simply does not cut it. At the same time, that is also the trap. OneTrust is hefty, and on smaller setups you pay for depth nobody uses while the implementation soaks up all the attention. Where teams get stuck is the assumption that the platform talks to your tracking on its own. It does not, that connection has to be right, otherwise all the compliance is in order on paper while your data leaks. Stevin runs as a layer over the consent status from OneTrust and your tags, and raises a signal the moment measurement drops out or a tag ignores consent, so the gap becomes visible before it pollutes your reporting.
onetrust.stackImpact: Choosing OneTrust means an implementation project, not a plug-in. Count on a tag manager and a thought-through Consent Mode connection, plus someone who maintains and keeps the data mapping current. The platform handles the legal side broadly, but it says nothing about the quality of your measurement afterward, and those two get confused easily. In practice: let OneTrust do the compliance and separately make sure your most important conversion data still comes in and is correct after consent. Otherwise you have a sealed privacy file on top of measurement that quietly has gaps, and that only gets noticed late.
pitfalls: Choosing OneTrust for a setup that does not need it: you pay for depth that sits idle.
Expecting consent to talk to your tracking automatically.
Filling in the data mapping once and then letting it go stale.
Entering a long implementation without anyone watching the tag connection.

opusflow.shortDescription: Software for installation firms in sustainability and technical services.
opusflow.description: OpusFlow is business software for installation firms with a focus on sustainability such as solar panels, heat pumps and insulation: from quote and planning to installation and aftercare.
opusflow.useCase: Manage the sales and execution process for sustainable installations.
opusflow.howWeUseIt: Stevin puts a work layer on top of OpusFlow and recognizes signals in the process: a quote that was not followed up, an installation scheduled while materials are not in yet, a subsidy-sensitive job where supporting documents are missing. Stevin proposes the action, a person decides. Connect through the API or an export.
problemsSolved: Sustainability quotes are not followed up fast enough
Installation is scheduled without confirmed materials
Subsidy proof (photo, product details) is not collected in time
No early signals about open customer actions
opusflow.stevinAngle: OpusFlow is built for installation firms in sustainability, and that focus shows: from quote and planning to installation and aftercare for solar panels, heat pumps and insulation. It follows the process neatly. Where it pinches is that sustainability adds two demands the system itself does not watch: speed on the quote, because customers compare, and proof for subsidies, because otherwise it costs money later. We see teams stall on this: a quote that sits too long, an installation scheduled while the materials are not in yet, a subsidy-sensitive job missing the photo or the product details. OpusFlow holds the data, but it does not push. Stevin runs as a layer on top, through the API or an export, reads the process and proposes the action at the moment it counts. A person decides, Stevin watches the moment.
opusflow.stackImpact: OpusFlow covers the sales and execution process for sustainability broadly, so there is little you need to add alongside it. The gain is in two monitoring points that fall outside the system: how fast a quote is followed up, and whether the subsidy proof is complete before the job closes. The connection runs through the API or an export. The question is not whether the data comes out, but whether something is watching for a quote going stale or a missing supporting document. Without that, you notice too late, often only at the subsidy application.
pitfalls: Letting sustainability quotes sit while the customer is comparing elsewhere in the meantime.
Scheduling installation without confirmed materials, then the crew turns up for nothing.
Not collecting subsidy proof like a photo or product details in time, and losing the money later.
No signal on open customer actions, so follow-up runs on memory instead of on timing.

outbrain.shortDescription: Native advertising and content recommendations at scale.
outbrain.description: Outbrain is one of the largest native advertising platforms in the world. It shows your content as a recommendation on premium publishers and news sites, ideal for awareness and traffic.
outbrain.useCase: Content distribution and awareness through native recommendations on news sites.
outbrain.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI integrates Outbrain into your media strategy and makes sure native campaigns are included in your total attribution and reporting.
problemsSolved: Native advertising sits apart from your performance channels
No view of the impact of content on your funnel
outbrain.stevinAngle: Outbrain is one of the largest native platforms in the world and places your content as a recommendation beneath articles on premium publishers. For awareness and traffic that delivers a scale you will not easily get elsewhere. The honest story is that the scale also carries noise: native recommendations draw plenty of clicks, but not all from people with serious interest, and the contribution to your funnel is hard to pin down. We see advertisers stall on this: the traffic comes in, but it sits apart from the performance channels and there is no view of what that content eventually sets in motion. The platform delivers volume, not the interpretation. Stevin runs as a layer on top, reads the results through the API and puts the native campaign in your total attribution. A person sees the conclusion first, then comes a decision about budget.
outbrain.stackImpact: Choosing Outbrain gives you reach at scale, but that reach comes with noise and with traffic that sits apart from your real conversion channels. Count on a connection with your tracking and attribution, otherwise you are measuring clicks with no context. The data is available through the API. The real question is what all that traffic does in your funnel, because native easily draws clicks that lead nowhere. Without something that lays the quality of that traffic next to your other channels, you are paying for volume instead of for effect.
pitfalls: Steering on click volume while native draws a lot of noise and loose clicks.
Letting native sit apart from your performance channels, so no view of the funnel impact.
Assuming a lot of traffic is the same as valuable traffic.
Raising budget without laying the quality of the traffic next to other channels.

patreon.shortDescription: Patronage data, subscriber analytics, and community engagement.
patreon.description: Patreon gives artists and creators a direct revenue source from their most loyal fans. Subscriber trends and churn data are indicators of your community's health.
patreon.useCase: Owned revenue monitoring and superfan community tracking.
patreon.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI monitors your Patreon metrics and signals when subscriber growth speeds up or slows down, tied to your content and social media activity.
problemsSolved: Patreon sits apart from your broader marketing analytics
Churn is not flagged proactively
patreon.stevinAngle: Patreon gives artists and creators a direct revenue line from their most loyal fans, and the numbers underneath, subscriber growth and above all churn, say something more honest about your community than your reach. People who pay every month vote with their wallet, and that is a stronger signal than a follower. The weak point is that Patreon sits next to your marketing instead of inside it. Churn happens quietly: a supporter cancels, it appears in an overview you open too late, and by then the departure is already a fact. The link with your content and your social activity, exactly what explains growth or loss, the platform does not draw. Stevin monitors your Patreon metrics and signals when growth speeds up or sinks, tied to what you publish and post. A looming drop surfaces in time with a proposal, and you decide what happens with it.
patreon.stackImpact: Patreon delivers your subscriber and churn data, but it sits apart from what you publish and post, so you need your content and social data to explain growth or loss. On its own it is a member count: you see the number, not the cause. And churn is looking backward, unless you pick up the line early. In practice: line Patreon up against your publishing rhythm and social activity and let a layer on top flag a downward trend early, so you can step in before the cancellations are already in instead of counting them afterward.
pitfalls: Only seeing churn in the monthly overview, when the departure is already a fact.
Decoupling subscriber numbers from your content, so growth or loss stays unexplained.
Keeping Patreon outside your broader analytics, so the signals reach no one in time.

pinterest-ads.shortDescription: Visual advertising on Pinterest for inspiration and purchase.
pinterest-ads.description: Pinterest Ads targets users in the inspiration and planning phase. Ideal for e-commerce and brands with visual products. The intent is high, but tracking is essential to measure results.
pinterest-ads.useCase: Product discovery and conversions through visual advertising.
pinterest-ads.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI integrates Pinterest with your webshop, tracking and product feeds. We make sure your Pinterest Tag is implemented correctly and that conversions are measured reliably.
problemsSolved: Product feeds are not connected properly
Conversion tracking is not set up properly
No insight into which pins convert
pinterest-ads.stevinAngle: Pinterest positions itself as the platform for the inspiration phase, but in practice we see at clients that the Pinterest Tag fires far too broadly by default. Without explicit deduplication against Google Analytics or your CDP, Pinterest records conversions that have already been credited elsewhere. The result is false confidence in your ROAS figures. What we do consistently in projects: configure the Tag with strict event-match quality, connect the API for Conversions alongside the browser tag, and reconcile both signals in your reporting layer. Only then do you see the real picture. For e-commerce clients with an average order value above 60 euros, Pinterest is worth serious consideration as a discovery channel, but only if your product feed is synced daily and your conversion windows are in line with your other platforms. Without that foundation you are measuring noise.
pinterest-ads.stackImpact: Pinterest Ads only works well once you have a reliable product feed pipeline, ideally through a feed management tool like Channable or DataFeedWatch that pushes to the Pinterest Catalog daily. On top of that you need the Pinterest API for Conversions as a server-side addition to the browser tag, which requires a backend connection to your webshop or order management system. If you want to take Pinterest data seriously in your attribution, your data pipeline to your BI tool or data warehouse has to include Pinterest as an explicit source, otherwise the channel disappears into the leftover category.
pitfalls: Installing the Pinterest Tag without event deduplication against your server-side connection leads to double-counted conversions and a ROAS that comes out structurally too high.
Uploading a product feed once without automatic syncing causes out-of-date prices and sold-out products in your ads, which hits your click-to-purchase ratio directly.
Conversion windows on Pinterest default to 30 days for clicks and 30 days for views, which with short funnels produces attribution that does not match how you measure your other channels.
Optimizing campaigns on Pinterest's own conversion reporting without mirroring it against your webshop data leads to budget choices based on figures you cannot trace internally.

pipedrive.shortDescription: User-friendly CRM focused on sales pipelines.
pipedrive.description: Pipedrive is a CRM focused on managing sales pipelines visually. Simple, effective, and popular with SMBs.
pipedrive.useCase: Visual pipeline management for sales teams.
pipedrive.howWeUseIt: Stevin connects Pipedrive to your lead sources and automation so new leads are created as deals automatically and get the right follow-up.
problemsSolved: Leads have to be entered into Pipedrive by hand
No automatic follow-up after a new lead
pipedrive.stevinAngle: Pipedrive does one thing very well: making a sales pipeline visual and easy to grasp. Drag deals through stages, see at a glance where things stall, without needing a manual. For SMB teams that want to start fast, that is exactly why it is so popular. We see the flip side too: Pipedrive shows the pipeline, but it does not chase deals. The automation it ships with is basic, and the moment you want more than a few simple rules you hit the limits. Where teams get stuck is that leads have to be entered by hand and that after a new lead the follow-up gets left, because the system waits for someone to do something. Stevin connects to Pipedrive and your lead sources through the API, creates new leads as deals automatically, and turns a stalling deal into a signal with a concrete next action. The person reviews every action first.
pipedrive.stackImpact: Choosing Pipedrive means you get a clear pipeline, but you have to arrange the smart follow-up and the connection to your lead sources yourself. The built-in automation is thin, so count on something that pulls leads in and watches that follow-up actually happens, instead of a deal sitting quiet in a stage. Connect it to your forms and ad channels, otherwise retyping leads stays handwork and information leaks away along the way. The question that remains: who makes sure a new lead gets the right action within the hour instead of waiting until someone happens to look.
pitfalls: Retyping leads by hand because the connection to your lead sources is missing.
Assuming a visible pipeline is the same as followed-up deals.
Stretching the basic automation into a tangle of rules nobody can follow anymore.
Letting a new lead wait because the system sets nothing in motion on its own.

piwik-pro-consent-manager.shortDescription: Consent management integrated with Piwik PRO analytics.
piwik-pro-consent-manager.description: Piwik PRO Consent Manager is the consent module within the Piwik PRO platform. It offers consent management that works smoothly with Piwik PRO analytics and tag management.
piwik-pro-consent-manager.useCase: Consent management integrated with privacy-friendly analytics.
piwik-pro-consent-manager.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI implements Piwik PRO Consent Manager as part of a privacy-first analytics setup and connects it to Google Consent Mode.
problemsSolved: Consent management and analytics are not integrated
Need for a privacy-first consent solution
piwik-pro-consent-manager.stevinAngle: Piwik PRO's Consent Manager has a clear advantage: it sits in the same platform as the analytics and the tag management, so consent and measurement talk to each other naturally instead of through a brittle connection. We choose it where a client deliberately goes for a privacy-first stack and does not want to tie three separate tools together. The flip side is that it is strongest within the Piwik PRO ecosystem. If you also run Google tags outside it, the connection to Consent Mode still has to be right, and in an otherwise closed setup that easily gets shortchanged. That is where the pitfall sits. Stevin runs on top of the consent and analytics data from Piwik PRO and flags when measurement drops out or a tag outside the ecosystem ignores consent, so a gap becomes visible before it quietly pollutes your numbers, with a person checking the fix.
piwik-pro-consent-manager.stackImpact: The big gain is that consent, tags and analytics live in one house, so within Piwik PRO you need few separate connections. But the moment you run Google advertising or external tags alongside, Consent Mode comes into it after all and has to connect smoothly. In practice: keep your measurement inside the ecosystem as much as possible and set up the external connections deliberately, not as an afterthought. The question that remains is what happens to the tags that live outside Piwik PRO, because that is where the built-in advantage no longer applies.
pitfalls: Assuming the built-in advantage also applies to tags outside Piwik PRO.
Treating Google Consent Mode as an afterthought in an otherwise closed setup.
Connecting external advertising tags without testing whether consent comes through.
Discovering a gap in the external measurement only in the numbers.

postgresql.description: PostgreSQL is a powerful open-source database used widely for data storage and as a base for marketing data integrations.
postgresql.useCase: Data storage and integration base for marketing data.
postgresql.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI uses PostgreSQL as a data layer for custom integrations and as a source for dashboards and reporting.
problemsSolved: A need for a reliable data layer for integrations
Custom data models needed for specific reporting
postgresql.stevinAngle: PostgreSQL is not a marketing product but a reliable open-source database, and it is exactly that plainness that makes it usable as a data layer under integrations and reporting. No license costs, broadly supported, and it does exactly what you ask without surprises. We use PostgreSQL as a foundation for custom integrations and as a source for dashboards. Where it goes wrong is expecting a database to be more than a database: PostgreSQL stores and serves data, but it does not build models, signal anything, or maintain itself. Without structure and without someone watching the schemas, it grows into a junk layer. Stevin uses the PostgreSQL layer as a source, reads the tables directly, and turns the relevant data into signals with follow-up underneath, with the consultant reviewing every action that carries weight first.
postgresql.stackImpact: Choosing PostgreSQL as a data layer means full control and no license costs, but also that you are responsible yourself for schema, maintenance, backups, and security. It is a foundation, not a platform: reporting, integrations, and models you build on top of it yourself. Count on someone who actively manages the data layer instead of letting it grow. The practical approach: keep the schema clean and documented, because a database that grows organically without discipline becomes a millstone faster than a reliable source.
pitfalls: Confusing a database with a platform: PostgreSQL stores, it does not model or signal.
Letting schemas grow organically without discipline, until the data layer becomes unmanageable.
Underestimating maintenance and backups because the tool feels free.
Leaving data sitting in tables without anything that pulls signals and action out of it.

power-bi.shortDescription: Microsoft's business intelligence and dashboard platform.
power-bi.description: Power BI is Microsoft's BI platform. Powerful for data visualization and reporting, especially in organizations already working with the Microsoft ecosystem.
power-bi.useCase: Business intelligence dashboards in Microsoft environments.
power-bi.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI builds Power BI dashboards that combine your marketing, sales and customer data into clear reports.
problemsSolved: Marketing data is not available in Power BI
Reports are manual and time-consuming
power-bi.stevinAngle: Power BI is strong and cheap if you already live in the Microsoft house: you build rich dashboards in it and the license often already sits in your subscription. We build client reports in it where the organization already runs on Microsoft and data from several sources has to come together. Where it pinches is that Power BI shows what happened, but never acts on its own. A dashboard is a mirror: a campaign sinking, a cost line running off the rails, it sits there neatly, but someone has to notice it and do something. In practice nobody looks every day. That is where Stevin steps in. Through the same dataset, Stevin reads the numbers along and raises a signal the moment a value deviates or hits a threshold, with the follow-up underneath and a person reviewing every action that carries weight first. Power BI shows, Stevin watches.
power-bi.stackImpact: Choosing Power BI means you first have to get the data into it: count on a connector or an intermediate layer that supplies your marketing, sales and customer data, because out of the box it mostly talks to Microsoft sources. It visualizes excellently, but it changes nothing about the freshness or accuracy of what you load in. In practice: invest in the data flow into Power BI, not just in the charts. A nice dashboard on slow or incomplete data gives a false sense of oversight.
pitfalls: Building a dashboard nobody looks at daily, so deviations sit unaddressed.
Underestimating the data flow and putting nice charts on incomplete data.
Choosing Power BI outside the Microsoft ecosystem and running into connector work.
Confusing visualizing with following up: the dashboard does nothing on its own.

prestashop.description: PrestaShop is an open-source e-commerce platform with a large community and many modules.
prestashop.howWeUseIt: Stevin connects PrestaShop to your marketing tools and takes care of correct tracking and product feed integrations.
