problemsSolved: PrestaShop is not connected well to marketing channels
Product feeds are not automated
prestashop.stevinAngle: PrestaShop is open-source and affordable, with a large community and many modules. That is the appealing side and at the same time the warning: the quality of the modules varies widely, and a PrestaShop stands or falls with whoever maintains it. We run into it at price-conscious clients who want control, and there it works, as long as you do not underestimate how much management comes with it. Where teams get stuck is the connection to marketing: the tracking is not complete on its own and product feeds are often manual work. Stevin puts a layer over that, reads order and product data through the API, and turns deviations into signals, a feed that no longer holds, a conversion that is not coming through, with a person seeing every intervention that carries weight first.
prestashop.stackImpact: Choosing PrestaShop means you come out cheaper on licenses, but you pay it back in maintenance and module management: count on technical time to keep it running and secure. The connection to your marketing tools is not a given, so product feeds and tracking need setup. In practice: choose reliable modules and automate the feed, otherwise it stays manual work. The question is whether the control over the platform is worth the maintenance that comes with it.
pitfalls: Stacking unreliable modules until management becomes unsustainable.
Maintaining product feeds by hand, so they lag behind your stock.
Not setting up tracking completely, leaving you with half the conversion data.

producthero.shortDescription: AI-driven product feed optimization and label strategy for Google Shopping.
producthero.description: Producthero automatically segments your products into hero, sidekick, and villain categories based on performance. This makes targeted budget allocation possible in Google Shopping and Performance Max campaigns.
producthero.useCase: Product segmentation and shopping budget optimization.
producthero.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI integrates Producthero's product segmentation into the Advisor engine. Budget gets shifted automatically from underperformers to hero products, backed with cross-channel performance data.
problemsSolved: No difference in budget allocation between top and underperforming products
Shopping budget gets split equally across all products
Performance Max lacks the nuance to differentiate products
producthero.stevinAngle: Producthero does one sharp, narrow job well: it automatically sorts your assortment by performance, hero to villain, so budget goes to the products that deserve it. For Shopping and Performance Max, where budget otherwise gets smeared equally over everything, that is a real lever. The caveat is that the sorting rests on Producthero's own logic and on the data it sees, while a product can be strategically important for reasons outside its view. Teams get stuck there: the label strategy steers the budget, but nobody weighs the exceptions. Stevin brings Producthero's segmentation into the Advisor and enriches it with cross-channel performance, so budget shifts on a broader picture than a single channel. A hero in Shopping can perform differently elsewhere, and the consultant sees that nuance before the budget moves with it.
producthero.stackImpact: Choosing Producthero means your shopping budget finally shifts in a targeted way instead of split equally, but it judges on the data and the logic it sees itself. Count on a layer that lays the segmentation next to your cross-channel performance, otherwise you shift budget on a one-sided picture. The value is in product labels that account for how a product performs across all your channels, not just in Shopping. Without that broader view you may demote a product that is actually doing the work elsewhere.
pitfalls: Letting the label strategy steer the budget without weighing the exceptions.
Demoting a product on Shopping data alone while it performs elsewhere.
Relying on a sorting that sees only part of your channels.
Losing strategically important products because they score as villain in a silo.

puzzel.shortDescription: Cloud contact center platform with reporting and analytics.
puzzel.description: Puzzel is a cloud-based contact center solution with extensive reporting and analytics capabilities. It offers insight into customer interactions across multiple channels.
puzzel.useCase: Reporting and analysis of customer interactions in the contact center.
puzzel.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI connects Puzzel data to your marketing reports so you can measure the impact of campaigns on customer interactions and service channels.
problemsSolved: Contact center data sits apart from marketing reports
No insight into the relationship between campaigns and customer interactions
puzzel.stevinAngle: Puzzel is not a marketing tool but a contact center platform, and that is immediately the interesting part: it sits on customer interactions that most marketing stacks never see, with its own reporting on top. We connect Puzzel data to marketing reports where the question is whether a campaign produces more calls or tickets, and whether that is good or bad news. Where it pinches is that Puzzel reports within its own walls: it shows what happens in the contact center, but it draws no line of its own to your campaigns or the rest of your data. That bridge is missing. Stevin runs on top and reads the interaction data together with your channel data, so a spike in calls after a campaign becomes a signal instead of a loose chart, with follow-up underneath and a person reviewing every action that carries weight first.
puzzel.stackImpact: Choosing Puzzel means you have a rich source of customer interactions that by default sits apart from your marketing. Count on a connection or an intermediate layer to get that data alongside your campaign insight, because Puzzel does not come to your reporting on its own. In practice: treat the contact center as a measurement source, not as an island. The question that remains is who draws the line between what a campaign does and what comes in afterward in calls, because on their own both tell you half the story.
pitfalls: Leaving contact center data apart from marketing, so the connection stays invisible.
Assuming Puzzel draws the bridge to your campaigns on its own.
Not linking a spike in calls to the campaign that caused it.
Confusing Puzzel's own reporting with a complete picture.

qlik-sense.shortDescription: Enterprise BI platform with associative data analysis.
qlik-sense.description: Qlik Sense is an enterprise business intelligence platform built on an associative data model. It offers powerful visualizations and self-service analytics for complex datasets.
qlik-sense.useCase: Advanced business intelligence and data visualization at enterprise scale.
qlik-sense.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI feeds marketing data into Qlik Sense for organizations that already run on the platform, so campaign and customer data become part of their BI environment.
problemsSolved: Marketing data is not available inside the BI environment
No way to freely explore marketing data
Reporting does not line up with company-wide BI
qlik-sense.stevinAngle: Qlik Sense stands out for its associative model: you can move freely through the data and find connections you never planned to look for, which is more than most tools that lock you onto a fixed path. So we feed marketing data into Qlik Sense at organizations that already use it as company-wide BI and actually put that exploration to work. Where it gets tight is that this is enterprise tooling: heavy, with a learning curve, and marketing data usually arrives late and does not slot in on its own. And like any BI environment, Qlik waits for someone to look. It shows the anomaly, it does not flag it. Stevin runs on top, reads the same data, and signals when something turns, with follow-up underneath and a person reviewing anything that carries weight first. Qlik is for exploring, Stevin is for acting in time.
qlik-sense.stackImpact: Choosing Qlik Sense usually means the choice was already made at company level, and marketing data has to fall in line behind it. Count on a data layer underneath, and on real work to get your channels cleanly into the associative model, because that does not happen by itself. It explores beautifully, but it changes nothing about how fresh your sources are. In practice: make sure your marketing data is delivered as seriously as the rest of the BI. The question that remains is who responds to what the exploration brings to light.
pitfalls: Treating marketing data as a latecomer that never quite fits the BI.
Underestimating the learning curve and leaving the exploration power unused.
Assuming a BI environment flags anomalies on its own.
Confusing exploring with following up: Qlik does nothing of its own accord.

quantcast.shortDescription: AI-driven audience intelligence and programmatic advertising.
quantcast.description: Quantcast combines audience intelligence with programmatic advertising. The platform uses AI to find and reach audiences without depending on third-party cookies.
quantcast.useCase: Cookieless audience targeting and programmatic advertising at scale.
quantcast.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI deploys Quantcast for cookieless targeting and makes sure campaign data is connected to your broader marketing reporting.
problemsSolved: Targeting becomes less effective as third-party cookies decline
No insight into audience overlap between channels
quantcast.stevinAngle: Quantcast combines audience intelligence with programmatic and has a clear point now that third-party cookies are falling away: it builds audiences in ways that lean less on those cookies. For cookieless targeting that is relevant. The honest note is that audience models make a promise about the audience that you cannot see yourself, and that overlap between channels stays invisible as long as everything sits apart. We see advertisers stall on this: the targeting works, but the campaign data is not in the broader reporting and no one knows whether the same people are already being reached through other channels. The platform delivers reach, not the overview. Stevin runs as a layer on top, connects the campaign data to your reporting through the API and flags overlap between channels. A person sees the conclusion first, then comes a shift in budget.
quantcast.stackImpact: Choosing Quantcast makes sense if you want targeting to lean less on cookies, but you get an audience model you do not inspect yourself. Count on a connection with your broader reporting, otherwise the reach floats free of the rest. The data is available through the API. The real question is whether you are not already paying for the same people through other channels, because audience overlap is exactly what you do not see when the campaign runs in a silo. Without that overview you steer on reach instead of on added value.
pitfalls: Trusting an audience model you cannot inspect yourself.
Leaving campaign data in a silo, so overlap with other channels stays invisible.
Paying for the same audience twice because no one lays the channels side by side.
Steering on reach instead of on what the channel genuinely adds.

readpeak.shortDescription: Native advertising platform for premium publishers.
readpeak.description: Readpeak is a native advertising platform that places your content on premium news sites. Ideal for thought leadership, content promotion and brand awareness with a relevant audience.
readpeak.useCase: Native advertising and content distribution on premium news sites.
readpeak.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI uses Readpeak as part of content and awareness strategies and connects results to your tracking for a complete picture.
problemsSolved: Content does not reach the right audience
No insight into how native ads contribute to conversions
readpeak.stevinAngle: Readpeak places your content as a native ad on premium news sites, and for thought leadership or content promotion that is a tidy way into a serious audience. It puts your story in places where it fits. The weakness of native is well known: it reaches people early in the funnel, and the contribution to an eventual conversion is hard to pin down. We see advertisers stall on this: the content runs, the impressions come in, but it is unclear whether the right audience is being reached and how that visibility carries through to leads or sales. The platform delivers placement, not the proof of effect. Stevin runs as a layer on top, connects the results to your tracking through the API and puts the native campaign in the context of your whole funnel. A person judges whether it produces anything before more budget goes to it.
readpeak.stackImpact: Choosing Readpeak gives you access to premium news environments, but native sits at the top of the funnel and that makes the effect indirect. Count on a connection with your tracking, otherwise it stays impressions with no story behind them. The data is available through the API. The hard question is whether the right audience is being reached and whether that visibility comes back later as a lead or customer. Without something that places it in your funnel, you judge on reach while not knowing whether it sets anything in motion.
pitfalls: Reaching the wrong audience without noticing because only impressions count.
Judging native apart from the funnel, so blind to the carry-through to leads.
Steering on reach while the effect at the top of the funnel is indirect.
Raising budget without proof that the content sets anything in motion.

realeyes.shortDescription: Emotion and attention measurement for video ads via webcam AI.
realeyes.description: RealEyes uses webcam-based AI to measure how viewers respond to video content. Attention, emotion, and engagement are mapped second by second. Ideal for optimizing video ads before you spend media budget.
realeyes.useCase: Video ad pre-testing on emotion and attention.
realeyes.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI brings RealEyes data into the creative feedback process. For each video ad you see where viewers drop off, which moments trigger emotion, and whether the message comes across.
problemsSolved: No view of how viewers respond emotionally to your video ads
High production costs for video without knowing in advance what works
Drop-off points in video only get discovered after launch
realeyes.stevinAngle: RealEyes uses webcam AI to measure how viewers respond to video second by second: where the attention is, which moments trigger emotion, where they drop off. For video ads that is more valuable than for a still image, because with video the problem is often in the flow, the mid-clip drop-off you cannot see in a heatmap. It does need real viewers and therefore time, so it is not an instant check like a predictive heatmap. That is the trade-off right there: you get richer data, but use it where video production is expensive enough to be worth the effort, not for every single post. Stevin brings the RealEyes data into the creative feedback process, so for each video ad you see where viewers drop off and whether the message lands. Drop-off points and weak moments surface as concrete fixes before you spend media budget, and the choice of what to change stays with the person.
realeyes.stackImpact: RealEyes measures with real viewers via webcam, which means you need time and a test panel, unlike a predictive tool that is done in seconds. That makes it not a check for every post, but for video with enough budget behind it to be worth the effort. The data is rich but sits apart from your production process, so you need something that brings the findings back to the creative team. In practice: use RealEyes for your more expensive video ads before you spend media budget and let a layer on top surface the drop-off moments as concrete fixes, so the measurement actually lands in the work.
pitfalls: Using RealEyes for every single post, when the turnaround only makes it worthwhile for more expensive video.
Not feeding the findings back to the creative team, so the measurement stays stuck in a report.
Only discovering drop-off points after launch because the pre-test gets skipped.

reddit-ads.description: Reddit Ads gives access to subreddits with strong community and niche context. Suited to brands that want to reach specific interest groups with relevant messages.
reddit-ads.useCase: Targeting at the interest and community level for B2B and niche B2C.
reddit-ads.howWeUseIt: Stevin connects Reddit Ads to your tracking, CRM and MMM so you measure not just clicks but actual leads and incremental value.
problemsSolved: Niche audiences are not reachable through mainstream platforms
Reddit spend sits apart from the rest of your attribution
reddit-ads.stevinAngle: Reddit Ads lets you target at the community and interest level, in subreddits with a sharp context you miss on mainstream platforms. For B2B and niche B2C, that is the strength: you reach a group that has gathered around a topic. We use it where that niche is genuinely valuable and broader reach falls short. Where teams get stuck is that the spend quickly comes loose from the rest of your attribution, and that you keep steering on clicks while you want to see leads and real value. Reddit traffic feels different than it measures. That is where Stevin sits. As a layer on top of your stack, Stevin reads the campaign data through the API, next to your tracking and CRM, so that a lead coming from a subreddit can be followed through the funnel. A campaign that delivers clicks but no leads, or a niche that suddenly converts: that becomes a signal a person reviews, not a loose click figure.
reddit-ads.stackImpact: Choosing Reddit means you want to carry the clicks through to leads and CRM, because at the click level niche traffic says little. You need your tracking and CRM alongside it to see whether that specific community actually delivers anything. The risk is that Reddit spend stays in its own corner, separate from your other attribution. The question is not whether you reach the niche, but whether it translates into leads you can follow. Without that connection you judge an interesting channel on clicks that tell you nothing about the return.
pitfalls: Steering on clicks when you want leads and real value from a niche.
Keeping Reddit spend separate from your CRM, so you cannot follow the contribution.
Assuming a sharp community converts on its own without measuring it.

redpoint-global.shortDescription: CDP with built-in data management and campaign orchestration.
redpoint-global.description: Redpoint Global offers a CDP with integrated data management and campaign orchestration. The platform combines customer data unification with the ability to orchestrate campaigns across every channel from one place.
redpoint-global.useCase: Unify customer data and orchestrate campaigns directly from a single platform.
redpoint-global.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI implements Redpoint Global for organizations that want to combine customer data unification and campaign orchestration in one solution.
problemsSolved: Customer data and campaign execution live in separate systems
No centralized orchestration of cross-channel campaigns
redpoint-global.stevinAngle: Redpoint Global combines customer data unification with campaign orchestration in one platform, and bringing those two together is the real promise: not data in the CDP first and then campaigns in a separate tool, but both from one place. For organizations tired of pumping data back and forth between separate systems, that is appealing. The downside of all-in-one is that none of the parts is necessarily the best, and the platform asks a lot before it delivers. Where teams get stuck is the assumption that unification plus orchestration in one tool automatically runs smoothly across channels. The setup decides whether it lives up to the brochure. Stevin connects to Redpoint through the API, reads the unified data and the campaign logic and turns the patterns into signals with follow-up underneath, with a person reviewing every action that carries weight first.
redpoint-global.stackImpact: Choosing Redpoint means unification and orchestration together in one platform, which saves you separate integrations but also ties you to one vendor for both sides of the process. Plan for a serious setup project, because the strength is entirely in how you configure it. In practice: be sharp about whether a combined platform really fits better than a separate CDP and orchestration tool, because all-in-one often means sharpest at nothing, and the gain is in how you make the orchestration respond to real signals.
pitfalls: Assuming unification plus orchestration in one tool runs smoothly across channels on its own.
Underestimating the setup project because the features sit in one platform.
Choosing all-in-one when a focused CDP and orchestration tool would fit better.
Orchestrating campaigns without the triggers connecting to real data signals.

resident-advisor.shortDescription: Event listings, artist rankings, and scene relevance.
resident-advisor.description: Resident Advisor is the authority in the electronic music scene. Rankings, event reviews, and your RA profile are indicators of your position in the market.
resident-advisor.useCase: Monitoring scene relevance and tracking event performance.
resident-advisor.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI monitors your RA profile and correlates event data with your online performance.
problemsSolved: RA rankings and reviews are not monitored systematically
Event performance is not tied to online growth
resident-advisor.stevinAngle: In the electronic scene, Resident Advisor is an authority, not because it claims to be but because the scene itself looks at it: rankings, event reviews, your RA profile. It says something about your position in the market in a way that sits apart from your streaming numbers. What RA does not do is put that in motion. Your ranking shifts, a review appears, your profile changes, and it sits there until someone happens to look. Systematic monitoring rarely happens, and no one draws the link between your RA position and your online growth. Stevin keeps an eye on your RA profile and ties event data to your online performance, so a shift in your position or a review that matters surfaces as a signal instead of passing unseen. You set whatever needs follow-up, Stevin makes sure you see it in time.
resident-advisor.stackImpact: RA has no broad public API, so the connection leans on scraping or manual work and the data does not come in real time. It measures your scene position, not your revenue, so you need your online performance alongside it to read a shift. On its own, your RA profile is a status indicator no one keeps up with structurally. So the question is not whether your ranking and reviews exist, but whether you notice when they move, because that is the moment something in your position changes. Treat RA as one of your reputation signals, not a standalone scoreboard.
pitfalls: Counting on real-time data when the scrape connection is delayed and brittle.
Not monitoring your RA profile structurally, so a shift passes unnoticed.
Decoupling scene position from your online growth, so you do not know whether it carries through.

rtb-house.description: RTB House is a retargeting platform that uses deep learning to show personalized ads. The platform is strong in dynamic product ads and runs entirely on its own AI models.
rtb-house.useCase: Advanced retargeting for e-commerce and lead generation with AI optimization.
rtb-house.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI integrates RTB House into your media plan and makes sure retargeting results are included in your total attribution model and reporting.
problemsSolved: Retargeting performance is not compared with other channels
No insight into how much extra value AI retargeting actually adds
rtb-house.stevinAngle: RTB House runs entirely on its own deep-learning models for retargeting with dynamic product ads, and on that specialism it often performs well. The honest story is that the hood is shut: you get strong results reported, but little grip on how, and on how much of it is genuinely extra. With retargeting that is a familiar trap, because it easily claims conversions that were coming anyway. We see advertisers stall on this: the performance is not compared with other channels, and the claimed value is rarely tested against what would have happened without those ads. The platform optimizes in its own black box. Stevin runs as a layer on top, reads the results through the API and puts them in your total picture, so you see where the channel overlaps with the rest. A person judges, Stevin keeps it honest.
rtb-house.stackImpact: Choosing RTB House means trusting a model you do not set yourself, so most of the steering is in how you judge the channel next to your other sources. Count on a connection with your tracking and reporting, otherwise the claimed value floats free. The data is available through the API. The hard question is whether those conversions were genuinely extra or double-count with your other retargeting and with search. Without something that lays that side by side, you sail blind on a dashboard that always brings good news.
pitfalls: Not laying the results next to other channels, so no idea about double-counting.
Trusting the black box without testing what was genuinely extra.
Taking retargeting revenue at face value while part of it was happening anyway.
Steering on a dashboard that structurally brings good news without context.

salesflare.shortDescription: A CRM that updates itself from your email and calendar.
salesflare.description: Salesflare is a CRM that minimizes data entry: it pulls contacts and companies automatically from your email and calendar and keeps the timeline up to date. Strong for small B2B teams that want to log little by hand.
salesflare.useCase: A low-admin CRM for small B2B sales teams.
salesflare.howWeUseIt: Stevin runs as an AI layer over Salesflare. Where Salesflare automates the entry, Stevin delivers the intelligence: signals about what is going wrong and concrete follow-up after every contact.
problemsSolved: A lot of time lost to data entry
Automatic entry but no smart follow-up
salesflare.stevinAngle: Salesflare solves a real annoyance: keeping a CRM up to date by hand. It pulls contacts and companies automatically from your email and calendar and keeps the timeline itself, so small B2B teams do not lose half the day to entry. For anyone who wants to type little, that is a relief. Where the limit sits: automatic entry is not the same as smart follow-up. Salesflare makes sure your data is right, but it does not think about what should happen next. The timeline fills up, and then it goes quiet. Where teams get stuck is exactly that difference: they expect a CRM that updates itself to also suggest the right action, and it does not. Stevin runs as a layer over Salesflare, reads contacts and pipeline through the API, and delivers the intelligence underneath: a signal when a deal cools off, a draft after a touchpoint. The person sees every action that carries weight first.
salesflare.stackImpact: Choosing Salesflare means you automate the entry away, but the follow-up is still an open question. The time you save on typing you lose again if nobody does anything with the clean data, so count on a layer that attaches action to it. For large, complex sales organizations it is too light, it is made for small B2B teams and you feel that the moment you want more stages or reporting. Keep in mind too that the automatic enrichment leans on what is in your email and calendar, so a messy inbox in means messy data out. In practice: let Salesflare carry the admin and put intelligence on top that decides what should happen.
pitfalls: Expecting automatic entry to also mean automatic follow-up.
Mistaking a clean timeline for a working sales process.
Using Salesflare for a large, complex organization it is too light for.
Saving time on entry and losing it again because nobody acts on the data.

salesforce.shortDescription: Enterprise CRM platform for sales, marketing, and service.
salesforce.description: Salesforce is the largest CRM platform in the world. Powerful and extensive, but complex. The value sits in the right configuration and connections.
salesforce.useCase: Enterprise CRM for complex sales and marketing processes.
salesforce.howWeUseIt: Stevin connects Salesforce to your marketing channels and makes sure lead data, campaign attribution, and follow-up flow smoothly. We build the bridge between marketing and sales.
problemsSolved: Salesforce is not well connected to marketing channels
Lead attribution is incomplete or unreliable
Sales has no insight into the marketing interactions of leads
salesforce.stevinAngle: Salesforce is not a tool you switch on, it is a platform you configure. The difference: 6 weeks of implementation versus 6 months, 50,000 versus 500,000 in total cost over year one. We regularly see accounts that are 18 months into a Salesforce implementation without the sales data getting any better, usually because scope creep never stopped. Stevin's position: if you do not have a dedicated RevOps person who knows Salesforce, choose HubSpot. Salesforce wins on customization, loses on time-to-value for SMBs.
salesforce.stackImpact: For the stack this means: invest in Salesforce administration as a role, not a side job. Setting up the standard objects well (Lead, Contact, Account, Opportunity) matters more than building 30 custom objects. Marketing data comes in through Marketing Cloud Account Engagement (formerly Pardot) or through a custom integration, both are work. Connect with your ad channels through UTM parameters that map to Lead Source, not through vague 'multi-touch attribution' tools.
pitfalls: Not syncing custom fields on Lead to Contact at conversion, historical data disappears
Lead routing through Process Builder and Workflows and Apex at once, nobody understands what triggers anymore
Validation rules so strict that the sales team creates all leads through 'override', the data becomes unreliable
Basing reports on formula fields that recalculate nightly, discrepancies between dashboards

salesforce-commerce-cloud.shortDescription: Enterprise ecommerce platform within the Salesforce ecosystem.
salesforce-commerce-cloud.description: Salesforce Commerce Cloud is an enterprise ecommerce platform that integrates tightly with the rest of the Salesforce ecosystem. It offers B2C and B2B commerce functionality at scale.
salesforce-commerce-cloud.useCase: Enterprise ecommerce integrated with Salesforce CRM and marketing.
salesforce-commerce-cloud.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI connects Salesforce Commerce Cloud to your tracking and marketing channels and uses the Salesforce integration for complete commerce reporting.
problemsSolved: Commerce data is not connected to marketing channels
No integrated picture of ecommerce and CRM data
salesforce-commerce-cloud.stevinAngle: Salesforce Commerce Cloud is built for the top of the market and you can tell: scale, B2C and B2B in one, and a direct line to the rest of Salesforce. We use it where a client already sits deep in that ecosystem, because that is when the integration really pays off. Outside that ecosystem you pay for weight you do not use. Where teams get stuck is the assumption that the Salesforce connection gives a complete picture by itself. Commerce events, marketing channels, and CRM get scattered across clouds and no one watches the whole. Stevin reads those streams through the API, turns loose transactions and campaign data into signals (a product that suddenly converts less, a channel that is cooling off), and puts concrete follow-up underneath, with the consultant seeing every action that carries weight first.
salesforce-commerce-cloud.stackImpact: Choosing Commerce Cloud means, in practice, choosing the whole Salesforce house. Apart from Sales Cloud and Marketing Cloud you lose the reason to be here. Count on implementation work to measure tracking and product feeds through correctly, because that does not happen well on its own, and keep in mind that a wrongly placed tag only shows up in your reporting weeks later. The data comes in clean, so the question is not whether commerce and CRM are connected, but whether someone acts the moment the numbers shift.
pitfalls: Choosing Commerce Cloud without the rest of Salesforce: you pay for integration you do not use.
Assuming the connection delivers a complete commerce-plus-CRM picture by itself.
Underestimating tracking implementation, so marketing channels receive mismeasured data.
No person or layer that responds when a product or channel sinks in the numbers.

salesforce-data-cloud.shortDescription: CDP from Salesforce for unifying customer data.
salesforce-data-cloud.description: Salesforce Data Cloud (formerly Salesforce CDP) centralizes customer data from all Salesforce products and external sources into one platform. It offers unified customer profiles and segmentation within the Salesforce ecosystem.
salesforce-data-cloud.useCase: Centralizing and activating customer data within the Salesforce ecosystem.
salesforce-data-cloud.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI connects Salesforce Data Cloud to marketing channels and external data sources so customer profiles are enriched and immediately usable for campaigns and personalization.
problemsSolved: Customer data inside Salesforce is spread across multiple clouds
No centralized customer profile for marketing and sales
Segmentation is not based on complete customer data
salesforce-data-cloud.stevinAngle: Salesforce Data Cloud, the former Salesforce CDP, brings customer data from all Salesforce clouds and external sources together into one profile. For organizations that have their customer picture scattered across Sales, Service, and Marketing Cloud, that is the place where it finally comes together. The gain is biggest if you already sit broadly in Salesforce, because then the sources are already there. Outside that, you pay to unify data that you get together more easily elsewhere. Where it pinches: a centralized profile is not yet a used profile. Segmentation on complete data sounds good, but without someone turning the profiles into campaigns and follow-up, it stays a nice overview. Stevin connects Salesforce Data Cloud to your marketing channels, reads the enriched profiles, and turns them into signals with follow-up underneath, and the consultant sees every action that carries weight first.
salesforce-data-cloud.stackImpact: Choosing Salesforce Data Cloud pays off if your customer data is already spread across multiple Salesforce clouds and you want to keep management within that ecosystem. Outside that ecosystem the added value over a warehouse approach is limited and you mostly pay for the Salesforce name. It unifies profiles, but the activation to channels you have to set up explicitly. The practical approach: connect it to your real marketing channels and make sure segmentation also leads to action, because an enriched profile that no one uses changes nothing about your campaigns.
pitfalls: Using Data Cloud without a broad Salesforce footprint, so the unification adds little.
Confusing a centralized profile with a profile that actually gets used.
Having segmentation on complete data without it leading to campaigns and follow-up.
Underestimating activation to marketing channels because the data already sits inside Salesforce.

salesforce-marketing-cloud.shortDescription: Enterprise marketing automation platform from Salesforce.
salesforce-marketing-cloud.description: Salesforce Marketing Cloud is the enterprise marketing automation platform within the Salesforce ecosystem. It offers email, SMS, social, advertising, and journey orchestration at scale.
salesforce-marketing-cloud.useCase: Enterprise marketing automation and customer journey orchestration.
salesforce-marketing-cloud.howWeUseIt: Stevin implements and optimizes Salesforce Marketing Cloud and makes sure journeys, data extensions, and connections to other channels are set up correctly.
problemsSolved: Marketing Cloud is not connected well to Salesforce CRM
Journeys and automations are not optimized
Data extensions are not set up correctly for segmentation
salesforce-marketing-cloud.stevinAngle: Salesforce Marketing Cloud is an enterprise platform, and that is the honest warning up front: it can do a lot, but you pay for it in complexity. Journey Builder, data extensions, AMPscript, it is powerful in the right hands and a millstone if you underestimate it. We use it for organizations already deep in Salesforce and where the scale justifies it, not as a first automation tool. Where teams get stuck is the assumption that the link with Salesforce CRM is set up well by default. It rarely is: data extensions and sync logic need constant maintenance. Stevin runs as a layer on top and watches whether journeys still do what they should and whether the data between the CRM and Marketing Cloud is not drifting apart, with the person seeing every intervention that carries weight first.
salesforce-marketing-cloud.stackImpact: Choosing Marketing Cloud is a commitment: you need someone to maintain the data extensions and journeys, otherwise it bogs down. It works best when Salesforce CRM is already your system of record, because without that you are paying for a heavyweight you barely use. Count on setup time and on governance, not on a platform that runs out of the box. The real question is whether your organization can carry the complexity.
pitfalls: Choosing Marketing Cloud without Salesforce CRM underneath: you pay for integration you do not use.
Assuming the CRM sync is fine without anyone watching the data extensions.
Building journeys nobody can maintain once the person who set them up leaves.

sap-commerce-cloud.description: SAP Commerce Cloud (formerly Hybris) is an enterprise ecommerce platform for large organizations with complex product catalogs, multiple sales channels, and international operations.
sap-commerce-cloud.useCase: Enterprise ecommerce for complex, international organizations.
sap-commerce-cloud.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI connects SAP Commerce Cloud to your marketing stack and makes sure ecommerce tracking, product feeds, and campaign data are measured through correctly.
problemsSolved: Ecommerce data does not reach the marketing tools from SAP
Tracking implementation in SAP Commerce is technically complex
sap-commerce-cloud.stevinAngle: SAP Commerce Cloud, the old Hybris, is heavy machinery for heavy organizations: complex catalogs, multiple channels, international operations. It does that well, but it asks a lot. We run into it at clients who are already in it and cannot just walk away, and there the gain is not changing the platform but getting the measurement layer around it in order. Because that is where it goes wrong: tracking in SAP Commerce is technically hard, and ecommerce data often reaches the marketing tools half or not at all. Teams stay stuck in implementation detail while no one sees what the numbers actually say. Stevin runs as a layer above SAP Commerce, reads the transaction and feed data through the available interfaces, and turns it into usable signals with follow-up underneath, and the person decides before anything that carries weight happens.
sap-commerce-cloud.stackImpact: Choosing SAP Commerce is a multiyear decision with the implementation budget and lead time that come with it. Count on specialist work to measure product feeds and tracking reliably through to your marketing stack, because by default that is not built in well and every change touches a chain of systems. You get a robust commerce foundation, but the marketing side you have to build on top of it explicitly. The practical approach: invest first in a clean measurement layer between SAP and your channels, otherwise campaigns keep running on data you cannot build on.
pitfalls: Underestimating tracking complexity in SAP Commerce, so marketing data comes in unreliable.
Product feeds that come through partly or not at all, leaving campaigns on incomplete data.
Staying stuck in implementation detail without anyone reading the outcome.
Assuming an enterprise commerce platform automatically includes a marketing measurement layer.

segment.shortDescription: Customer Data Platform for centralizing customer data.
segment.description: Segment collects customer data from all your sources and sends it to the right destinations. It is the infrastructure layer under your marketing stack.
segment.useCase: Centralizing customer data for consistent tracking and personalization.
segment.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI implements Segment as the data infrastructure layer that feeds all your tools with consistent, reliable data.
problemsSolved: Customer data is spread across dozens of tools
Tracking is inconsistent between platforms
No single source of truth for customer data
segment.stevinAngle: Segment is a Customer Data Platform that, at its core, solves one problem: it keeps you from having to track the same event 15 times for 15 tools. One SDK call, Segment routes it to GA4, Mixpanel, Klaviyo, Facebook CAPI, and so on. For growing companies this is an instant win. For an SMB with 3 tools it is overkill, direct integrations are cheaper and simpler there. Since Twilio bought Segment the pricing structure has gotten stricter, so do the math up front and watch the MTU limits.
segment.stackImpact: For your stack: Segment does not replace an analytics tool, it is a routing layer in front of it. Send events to Segment, Segment fans out to destinations. The key discipline: a tracking plan in a shared document, a naming convention for events, and versioned schemas so an SDK update does not quietly break data. Combine it with Protocols (Segment's own schema validation) once your team grows past 5 developers.
pitfalls: Sending the same event from both client and server, it double-counts in destinations and attribution becomes unreliable
Adding destinations without budget monitoring, costs climb with multi-platform fan-out
Not maintaining a tracking plan, events grow organically into a chaotic mess
Turning on the Personas feature before data quality is in order, segments are noise

semrush.shortDescription: SEO and marketing analytics tool for keyword research and competitor analysis.
semrush.description: Semrush offers extensive SEO tools, keyword research, competitor analysis and content optimization. It is an essential platform for data-driven marketing decisions.
semrush.useCase: Keyword research, competitor analysis and SEO monitoring.
semrush.howWeUseIt: Stevin uses Semrush for strategic keyword research and competitor analysis that form the basis for your paid and organic strategy.
problemsSolved: No view of keyword opportunities
Competitors are not mapped out
semrush.stevinAngle: Semrush is the broad SEO and market analysis tool: keyword research, competitor analysis and content insights in one package. The strength is the breadth, you find almost everything about search traffic and what competitors are doing. We use it where it belongs: as the basis for strategic keyword and competitor research that gives your paid and organic effort direction. Where teams get stuck is that all that data is a snapshot you have to keep checking yourself. A competitor that suddenly bids on your terms, a keyword where your position sinks: it is in Semrush, but only if someone actively looks at it. It quickly becomes a tool you open when you have time. That is where Stevin sits. As a layer on top of your stack, Stevin reads the Semrush data through the API and tracks the development, so that a meaningful shift in positions or competition becomes a signal a person reviews, instead of a report that stays untouched.
semrush.stackImpact: Choosing Semrush gives you a lot of data, but it is a research source you have to actively consult, not something that warns you. Count on the value arising only once someone keeps tracking the movements. The data comes in through the API, so the real question is not whether you have insight, but whether someone picks up the shifts that matter. Without a layer that tracks the development and watches for deviations, Semrush stays a rich report you open now and then, while the movements you should have seen have already passed.
pitfalls: Using Semrush as a loose research tool you only open when there is time.
Missing competitor movements because nobody tracks the data structurally.
Only seeing a sinking position once organic traffic has already dropped.

server-side-tagging.shortDescription: Server-side tracking for more reliable data.
server-side-tagging.description: Server-side tagging moves tracking from the browser to a server. This makes data more reliable, reduces the impact of ad blockers and gives more control over which data is shared.
server-side-tagging.useCase: More reliable tracking and more control over data flows.
server-side-tagging.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI implements server-side tagging via Google Tag Manager Server-Side. We make sure your most important conversion data gets measured reliably, even with ad blockers and privacy restrictions.
problemsSolved: Data loss from ad blockers and browser restrictions
Unreliable conversion data
Too little control over which data goes to third parties
server-side-tagging.stevinAngle: Server-side tagging pulls measurement out of the browser and puts it on a server you manage yourself. That makes your data more reliable, less sensitive to ad blockers, and it gives control over what goes to third parties. We use it where your most important conversion data really matters and the browser is letting you down. It is no magic bullet: a server-side setup is more work to stand up and maintain, and an error sits deeper hidden than with a tag in the browser. Where teams get stuck is the idea that the data now adds up on its own. The flow gets more reliable, but someone still has to look at it. Stevin runs on top of that server-side flow and flags when a conversion event drops out or deviates, so a silent break in measurement stands out before you steer a whole campaign on it, with a person confirming the cause.
server-side-tagging.stackImpact: Server-side tagging requires its own container and hosting, so count on infrastructure you manage and pay for, not a free script. The gain is more reliable data and more grip on what you share, the price is complexity and maintenance. In practice: use it for your core conversions, not for everything at once, otherwise you build an expensive layer for events that barely need it. The real question is who notices when the server-side measurement stalls, because in the browser you see it faster.
pitfalls: Wanting to measure everything server-side instead of your core conversions first.
Assuming the data adds up on its own once it runs on the server.
Underestimating the hosting and the maintenance.
Discovering a silent break in the server flow only in the report.

shazam.shortDescription: Discovery data, Shazam spikes, and the geo-location of recognitions.
shazam.description: Shazam is the thermometer of music discovery. A spike in Shazams after a festival or radio play is a direct signal that your track resonates with a new audience.
shazam.useCase: Tracking music discovery moments and geo-targeting based on Shazam data.
shazam.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI detects Shazam spikes and ties them to events, performances, or viral moments. The Advisor recommends running ads in regions where Shazam activity is high.
problemsSolved: Shazam spikes are not used for targeted promotion
No insight into where your music is being discovered
shazam.stevinAngle: Shazam is not a marketing platform, it is a thermometer. Someone hears your track somewhere, grabs their phone, and wants to know what it is. That action is a more honest signal than a like, because there is real curiosity behind it. That makes Shazam valuable in a way most analytics miss: it shows you where your music is being discovered, not where you are already known. The problem is that the data stays put. A spike in a city after a radio play or a performance is an open door for targeted promotion, but without something acting on it nothing happens. Stevin reads the Shazam data, ties a spike to an event or a moment, and turns it into a recommendation: switch ads on in the region where recognitions are climbing. We run nothing unseen, you see every proposal first.
shazam.stackImpact: Shazam as a signal source only works if you can also activate the geo-data somewhere, so count on an ad platform alongside it where you can target per region. The data says where you are being discovered, not why, so you need your event and release calendar alongside it to read a spike. Viewed in isolation it is an interesting observation with no follow-through. In practice: let Shazam point to the place and let another system run the promotion, so a recognition spike does not stay a graph but becomes a reason to put budget down with intent.
pitfalls: Admiring a Shazam spike without a channel ready to target the region right away.
Not tying the spikes to your event or release calendar, so you do not know what caused them.
Reacting to noise: mistaking a small fluctuation for a real discovery moment.

shopify.description: Shopify is the most popular e-commerce platform for SMBs. User-friendly, scalable, and with extensive integration options.
shopify.useCase: Webshops connected to marketing and analytics.
shopify.howWeUseIt: Stevin connects your Shopify webshop to ads, tracking, email, and analytics. We make sure conversions are measured correctly, product feeds stay up to date, and customer data flows to your CRM.
problemsSolved: E-commerce tracking is not set up well
Product feeds are not synced with ad channels
Customer data does not reach the CRM
shopify.stevinAngle: For 80 percent of D2C brands in 2026, Shopify is the right platform. The remaining 20 percent sit in two groups: enterprise (choose Shopify Plus or another CMS), or niche (very specific checkout flows that Shopify does not support). We see teams that started on WooCommerce and migrate to Shopify because they no longer have time for WordPress maintenance. The other way around, we rarely see. The most important choices in a Shopify setup: themes ('Online Store 2.0' templates with sections), apps (as few as possible, every app slows your site down), and checkout customization (only really possible on Shopify Plus).
shopify.stackImpact: For your stack: Shopify integrates out of the box with most marketing tools (Klaviyo, Meta, Google), but watch out for apps that add their own scripts, that is how a Shopify site goes from 1.5s load time to 5s. Reviews, fulfillment, abandoned cart emails, all through a curated set of apps instead of 30 that overlap each other. For analytics: Shopify Analytics is fine as a baseline, but for real attribution connect to GA4 plus BigQuery plus Klaviyo.
pitfalls: Installing apps and never uninstalling them. Scripts keep loading even when you no longer use them.
Editing a theme without version control. The next theme update overwrites your work.
Using the standard checkout for B2B with separate VAT rules. It leads to wrong invoicing.
Not switching off Shopify Payments in markets where Mollie or Adyen converts better.

shopware.shortDescription: German e-commerce platform popular in Europe.
shopware.description: Shopware is a European e-commerce platform growing in popularity. Flexible, open-source, and strong in the European market.
shopware.useCase: E-commerce for the European market with local compliance.
shopware.howWeUseIt: Stevin integrates Shopware with your marketing and analytics stack for complete e-commerce tracking and campaign optimization.
problemsSolved: Shopware data is not connected to ad platforms
E-commerce tracking is incomplete
shopware.stevinAngle: Shopware is a European e-commerce platform that is growing, is open-source, and fits well for anyone who wants to stay within the EU on data and compliance. In practice it is flexible and solid, and a bit lighter to manage than Magento, though you still need technical support to run it cleanly. We use it for clients who weigh the European side heavily and want a serious shop. Where teams get stuck is the same trap as with any e-commerce platform: the connection to ad platforms and analytics lags behind and the tracking is incomplete. Stevin puts a layer over that, reads order and product data through the API, and flags what deviates, a feed that no longer holds or a conversion that is not coming through, with a person reviewing every action that carries weight first.
shopware.stackImpact: Choosing Shopware means you have a European, open platform, but you still need technical setup for tracking and feeds. Count on work to connect the shop to your ad platforms and analytics, because out of the box that data does not come in clean. It is a bit lighter than Magento, but no no-code solution. The gain is in the EU position and the openness, provided you set up the connections to your marketing stack well.
pitfalls: Assuming open-source means you need no technical management.
Not connecting Shopware data to your ad platforms, so campaigns run on half the data.
Leaving e-commerce tracking incomplete and only noticing the gaps at reporting time.

showheroes.shortDescription: Video advertising and content solutions for publishers and advertisers.
showheroes.description: ShowHeroes is a video advertising platform that gives advertisers access to video inventory on premium publishers. It combines video content creation with programmatic distribution.
showheroes.useCase: Video advertising on premium publishers through programmatic and direct.
showheroes.howWeUseIt: Stevin uses ShowHeroes for video campaigns and makes sure viewability and conversion data get included in your full media reporting.
problemsSolved: Video campaigns are not linked to your performance channels
No view of how video advertising affects your funnel
showheroes.stevinAngle: ShowHeroes gives you video inventory on premium publishers, with content creation and programmatic distribution in one. For brands that want video reach in serious environments, that is handy: you do not have to source everything from YouTube. We use it where video plays a role at the top of the funnel and the environment matters. Where teams get stuck is viewability and contribution. Video feels like a strong format, but whether an impression was actually seen and whether it later delivers anything easily disappears into a separate video dashboard. It stays a feeling that it works. That is where Stevin sits. As a layer on top of your stack, Stevin reads the campaign data through export and places viewability and traffic next to your other channels, so that a notable move after a video flight becomes a signal a person reviews. ShowHeroes delivers the reach, Stevin makes visible whether it leads anywhere.
showheroes.stackImpact: Choosing ShowHeroes means you want to be able to place viewability and effect next to your other channels, because video easily gets judged on feel. You need your own analytics alongside it to recognize movement after a flight. The question is not whether you get video impressions, but whether someone looks at what they set off in your funnel. Without that connection you pay for visibility whose effect you assume, and video stays a format that feels good without you proving it.
pitfalls: Buying video impressions without placing viewability and effect next to your other channels.
Assuming a strong format contributes on its own without tracking it.
Leaving results in a separate video dashboard that nobody places next to the rest.

similarweb.shortDescription: Digital market share, traffic analysis, and competitive benchmarks.
similarweb.description: SimilarWeb estimates website traffic, traffic sources, and market share for any website in the world. Ideal for benchmarking your digital position against competitors without needing access to their data.
similarweb.useCase: Digital market analysis, competitor traffic benchmarks, and channel mix comparison.
similarweb.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI pulls SimilarWeb data in to benchmark your digital market position. You see not only your own traffic, but also how competitors grow and through which channels.
problemsSolved: No view of competitors' website traffic
Market share only gets measured offline or via panels
No idea which channels competitors are using
similarweb.stevinAngle: SimilarWeb gives you something you can never see yourself: an estimate of the traffic and channel mix of any competitor, without access to their data. For benchmarking your digital position, that is a rare window. Just keep in the back of your mind that these are estimates, projected from models, and that the figures get rougher on smaller domains. As a direction it holds, as precise truth it does not, and anyone who takes the numbers too literally draws skewed conclusions. Teams get stuck there: a benchmark becomes a fact. Stevin pulls SimilarWeb data in and turns it into a signal that runs over time: a competitor that is growing, a channel they are shifting toward, a change in their mix. Not the snapshot, but the movement is what counts, and the consultant sees the read before any budget shifts on it.
similarweb.stackImpact: Choosing SimilarWeb means you can set your position against competitors without their cooperation, but you buy estimates, not measured truth. Count on reading the figures as a trend and not as an absolute outcome, and on laying them next to your own analytics to give context and absorb the noise on small domains. The gain is in tracking the direction over time, not in a loose percentage from a single reading. Without that you over-interpret an estimate as if it were your own, measured data.
pitfalls: Treating an estimate as measured truth.
Trusting figures on small domains that are roughest exactly there.
Grabbing a snapshot instead of the movement over time.
Not laying the data next to your own analytics, so reading it without context.

simon-data.shortDescription: CDP built on your own data warehouse.
simon-data.description: Simon Data is a CDP that works directly on your existing data warehouse. It combines the power of a CDP with the flexibility of your own data infrastructure.
simon-data.useCase: CDP functionality on your own data warehouse.
simon-data.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI implements Simon Data for organizations that want to build their CDP on their own data infrastructure.
problemsSolved: A need for a CDP without duplicating data
The existing data warehouse is not used for marketing
simon-data.stevinAngle: Simon Data is a CDP that runs on your existing data warehouse instead of building a copy, and that is exactly where the appeal sits. You keep your data in one place and get CDP functionality on top of it, without the duplication that classic CDPs bring. For teams that already take their warehouse seriously, that is a sensible route. Where it pinches: the value stands or falls with the quality of that warehouse. If your data foundation is messy, Simon Data inherits that mess one for one. And a CDP on your warehouse does not activate anything by itself, it makes segments available. Stevin connects to that warehouse layer, reads the segments and behavioral data, and turns them into signals with follow-up underneath, with the consultant reviewing every change that carries weight first.
simon-data.stackImpact: Choosing Simon Data means your warehouse stays the source, not a second copy next to your existing infrastructure. That saves duplication and keeps governance in one place, but it makes the quality of your warehouse immediately critical for everything you activate. Count on data work up front: clean models in, usable segments out, and someone who maintains that. The practical approach: invest in your warehouse before you expect the CDP layer to deliver, because Simon Data does not improve your data, it works with it exactly as it is at that moment.
pitfalls: Putting a CDP on your warehouse while the data foundation is messy.
Expecting Simon Data to solve data problems instead of inheriting them.
Having segments available without anything turning them into action.
Claiming the governance benefit without actually modeling in one place.

simple-simon.shortDescription: Work order and service app for engineers and technicians.
simple-simon.description: Simple Simon is a digital work order and service app that lets engineers record jobs, hours, materials and photos on the move. Popular with installation, maintenance and service firms.
simple-simon.useCase: Handle work orders, service jobs and engineer recording digitally.
simple-simon.howWeUseIt: Stevin reads the work orders and service jobs from Simple Simon and turns them into signals: a job with no follow-up, a customer who has not had an update yet, a review that can be asked for at the right moment. Stevin does not replace the app, it makes sure the loose orders lead to action in time. Connect through the API or an export.
problemsSolved: Finished work orders do not lead to follow-up or invoicing
Customers do not get an update in time
Reviews are not asked for at the right moment
No overview of open service actions
simple-simon.stevinAngle: Simple Simon does exactly what the name promises: engineers quickly record their job, hours, materials and photos in a work order while on the move. It is low-friction, and that is why it actually gets used on site, where heavier systems get left alone. But that simplicity stops the moment the order is done. We see service firms stall after completion: a work order that is finished but never invoiced, a customer who gets no update, a happy customer who is never asked for a review when that was exactly the moment. Simple Simon captures the work in the field, but does nothing afterward. Stevin reads the finished orders through the API or an export and turns them into signals with a next step underneath: invoice, update the customer, ask for a review. The owner sees the action before it goes out, Stevin makes sure the order does not stay sitting.
simple-simon.stackImpact: Choosing Simple Simon gives you fast input in the field, but the whole follow-up side is something you have to arrange yourself, because it is deliberately not in the app. Count on an invoicing system alongside it and something that turns finished orders into actions. The connection runs through the API or an export, so the orders come out. The question is what happens the moment an order is finished. Without something reacting to that, finished orders pile up and you miss both the invoicing and the right moment for a review.
pitfalls: Not turning finished work orders into invoicing, so revenue is delayed.
Not giving the customer an update after the job, when a short message makes the difference.
Letting the review moment pass because no one has a signal on it.
No overview of open service actions, so everything runs on the planner's inbox.

slack.shortDescription: Team communication with strong integration options.
slack.description: Slack is more than chat, it is a hub for notifications and integrations. From lead alerts to campaign updates, Slack keeps your team posted in real time.
slack.useCase: Real-time notifications and communication about leads and campaigns.
slack.howWeUseIt: Stevin connects Slack to your CRM and lead processes so your sales team gets an immediate alert on a new lead or an important action.
problemsSolved: Sales is not informed about new leads fast enough
Campaign updates do not reach the team in time
slack.stevinAngle: Slack has long been more than chat: it is where notifications and integrations come together and where a team stays posted in real time. For lead alerts and campaign updates it is a natural hub, because everyone is already in there. So that is exactly how we use it, as the place where signals land and people act on them. The trap sits in that same strength. Slack makes it easy to throw everything in, and before you know it an important lead alert drowns in dozens of noise messages nobody reads anymore. An alert everyone ignores is the same as no alert. Slack sends the message, but it does not decide what is worth sending. Where teams get stuck is that sales hears about a new lead too late, or drowns in updates instead. Stevin connects to Slack and your CRM through the API, sends only the signal that matters to the right channel, and attaches a concrete action to it. The person decides on the follow-up.
slack.stackImpact: Choosing Slack as a notification hub means you get a central place where your team already sits, but you need discipline about what you throw in. Expect unfiltered alerts to pollute the channel until nobody looks at it anymore, so the value is in selection, not volume. Slack itself does not decide what matters, that judgment has to happen somewhere else. In practice: connect Slack to your CRM and lead processes and put a layer in front that only forwards the signals that deserve action.
pitfalls: Throwing everything into Slack, so important lead alerts drown in the noise.
Assuming a sent message is also a read message.
Expecting Slack itself to decide which alert matters.
Setting up notifications without attaching a concrete action to them.

snapchat-ads.shortDescription: Advertising on Snapchat for younger audiences and AR formats.
snapchat-ads.description: Snapchat Ads gives access to a younger audience through Stories, Spotlight and AR Lenses. Strong for brands with visually strong creative and consumer-facing offerings.
snapchat-ads.useCase: Reach and conversion with younger audiences through vertical video and AR.
snapchat-ads.howWeUseIt: Stevin implements the Snap Pixel and Conversions API and connects Snapchat to your tracking, CRM and MMM so you measure real incremental contribution.
problemsSolved: Conversion data is unreliable without a server-side connection
Snapchat's contribution is missing in the broader media mix
snapchat-ads.stevinAngle: Snapchat Ads brings you to a younger audience with Stories, Spotlight and AR Lenses, formats where visually strong brands make the difference. For consumer-facing offerings with good creative, that is the value: an audience you reach less easily on other platforms. We use it where that younger audience genuinely fits and the creative is in order. Where it pinches is measurement. Without a server-side connection through the Conversions API, the conversion data is unreliable, and without that, Snapchat's contribution gets lost in your broader mix. You see clicks, but not what they deliver. Stevin runs as a layer on top of your stack and, once the Snap Pixel and CAPI are in place, reads the campaign data through the API next to your tracking and CRM. A lead that comes from Snapchat but does not get followed up, or spend that drifts away without return: that becomes a signal a person reviews, not a figure that without server-side measurement was already off.
snapchat-ads.stackImpact: Choosing Snapchat means the Snap Pixel and the Conversions API have to be set up seriously, otherwise you measure on sand. Count on a server-side connection as the first piece of work, because without it everything you report afterward is unreliable. The data comes in through the API, but the real condition is that the measurement is right before you place the contribution next to your other channels. Without that foundation, Snapchat stays a channel with nice clicks and an unknown return, and your picture drifts apart from what actually comes in.
pitfalls: Running Snapchat without server-side CAPI: the conversion data is then unreliable.
Deploying it without the creative in order, when the format leans entirely on that.
Reporting clicks without anyone checking whether a lead comes out that gets followed up.

snowflake.shortDescription: Cloud data platform for storage and analysis.
snowflake.description: Snowflake is a cloud data platform that combines data storage, processing, and analysis. Popular with companies that want to centralize their data infrastructure.
snowflake.useCase: Cloud data warehouse for centralized data analysis.
snowflake.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI connects Snowflake to your marketing stack and builds data models that combine marketing, sales, and customer data for deeper insight.
problemsSolved: Marketing data is not centralized
No way to do advanced cross-channel analysis
snowflake.stevinAngle: Snowflake is not a marketing tool, it is the cloud data platform where more and more marketing data eventually lands. Storage, processing, and analysis in one place, and it scales without you having to think about infrastructure. For organizations that want to centralize their data foundation it is a strong choice. The trap is that Snowflake on its own does nothing for marketing: it is a tub of compute underneath. Marketing, sales, and customer data come in, but without models and without someone pulling the insight out, it stays storage. We connect Snowflake to the marketing stack and build the data models that combine channels. Stevin reads those models through the connection and turns the cross-channel patterns into signals with concrete follow-up, with a person seeing every action that carries weight first.
snowflake.stackImpact: Choosing Snowflake is choosing a central data layer, not a ready-made marketing solution. You need modeling to get value out of it, and a tool or layer that activates the insight in your channels. The costs run with your usage, so sloppy queries and unchecked compute get expensive fast. The practical approach: see Snowflake as a foundation and build the marketing logic on top of it explicitly, because centralizing the data is step one, doing something with it is step two and that does not happen on its own.
pitfalls: Seeing Snowflake as a marketing tool while it is a data layer without models.
Centralizing data without the models that pull cross-channel insight out of it.
Underestimating usage costs, so sloppy queries drive up the bill.
Leaving insight sitting in the warehouse without anything that activates it.

songkick.shortDescription: Concert tracking, tour management, and fan demand data.
songkick.description: Songkick is one of the largest platforms for concert discovery. Fan demand data shows in which cities your audience is growing fastest.
songkick.useCase: Tour planning support and concert marketing.
songkick.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI ties Songkick data to your streaming and social media trends per region, so your tour planning is backed by data.
problemsSolved: Tour planning is based on gut feel instead of data
Fan demand per city is not visible
songkick.stevinAngle: Songkick is one of the largest places where fans discover concerts, and the demand data underneath is gold for tour planning: which cities your audience is growing fastest in, where the hunger for a show is. That is information many artists guess at on instinct while it is sitting there, measurable. The shortfall is not in the data but in what happens with it. Songkick shows demand per city, but leaves the link with your streaming and social growth to you, and in practice that link rarely gets drawn. So you plan a tour on gut feel instead of on signals. Stevin reads the Songkick data and puts demand per region next to your listeners and your social trends, so a city climbing on multiple fronts surfaces as a candidate for a show. You see the proposal first, then you decide.
songkick.stackImpact: Songkick gives you demand per city, but that number only becomes useful next to your streaming listeners and social growth per region, so you need those sources to get a valid picture. On its own it is a demand signal with no context: lots of followers in a city says little if your listener numbers do not match. The link per region is the real work. In practice: treat Songkick as one of several geo-signals and let a layer on top pull out the cities where everything climbs at once, so tour decisions rest on coherence and not on a loose number.
pitfalls: Taking demand from one source as truth without your streaming and social data per region alongside it.
Planning a tour on gut feel when the geo-signals are there for the taking.
Picking a city on followers alone when listening behavior tells a different story.

soundcloud.shortDescription: Plays, reposts, comments, and community engagement on SoundCloud.
soundcloud.description: SoundCloud is the platform for underground releases, bootlegs, and DJ sets. The community is more active and more vocal than on Spotify. This is where you discover your core fans.
soundcloud.useCase: Monitoring underground traction, set engagement, and community sentiment.
soundcloud.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI tracks your SoundCloud performance and detects when a track unexpectedly picks up traction. The Advisor flags it so you can reinforce that momentum with ads or social posts.
problemsSolved: SoundCloud engagement is not factored into your marketing strategy
You miss viral momentum on bootlegs or sets
No link between SoundCloud traction and Spotify streams
soundcloud.stevinAngle: SoundCloud is where the scene actually lives: bootlegs, DJ sets, and a community that reacts more actively and more directly than on Spotify. For finding your core fans and early traction there is no better place. We monitor it because a track often moves here before it moves anywhere else. Where it gets tight is that this movement easily goes unnoticed. Plays, reposts, and comments pile up, but SoundCloud itself does not tell you when something unexpectedly takes off, and without that flag you miss the moment to throw ads or a post behind it. The platform shows the traction, it does not warn you about it. That is where Stevin sits on top. Through your SoundCloud data, Stevin notices when a track suddenly moves and gives the Advisor a signal to reinforce that momentum, with a person reviewing anything that carries weight first before any budget goes on it.
soundcloud.stackImpact: Choosing SoundCloud as a channel means you have an early-signal source that sits apart from your Spotify numbers and your ads. Count on a connection that pulls the traction in, because it does not come to your strategy on its own and the spikes are fleeting. In practice: treat SoundCloud as the place where momentum starts and your other channels as the place where you reinforce it. The question that remains is who notices a track moving at the moment it happens, because a day late and the momentum is gone.
pitfalls: Missing viral momentum on a bootleg or set because no one sees it in time.
Keeping SoundCloud engagement outside your marketing strategy.
Not tying the traction here to your Spotify streams and ads.
Assuming the platform warns you itself when something takes off.

sparktoro.shortDescription: Audience research: discover what your audience reads, follows, and watches.
sparktoro.description: SparkToro analyzes the online behavior of your audience: which websites they visit, who they follow on social, which podcasts they listen to, which hashtags they use. Ideal for finding unexpected media placements and influencers.
sparktoro.useCase: Audience discovery, influencer identification, and media planning.
sparktoro.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI uses SparkToro to map your audience's media behavior. The result: unexpected channels and influencers where your competitor is not advertising but your audience is active.
problemsSolved: Media budget gets spent on the obvious channels
Influencer selection is based on follower count, not audience overlap
No view of which niche media your audience consumes
sparktoro.stevinAngle: SparkToro answers a question the big platforms do not ask: where your audience actually hangs out. Which sites they visit, who they follow, which podcasts they listen to. That turns up media placements and names you would never have hit through the usual targeting. The caveat is that it discovers, it does not prove: an overlap with an influencer or a site is a clue, not a guarantee that a campaign there pays off. Teams get stuck there: an interesting find becomes a media budget without anyone testing whether it works. Stevin uses SparkToro to map your audience's media behavior and then links those channels to your own performance, so an unexpected placement gets tested small before it gets budget. The consultant sees which discoveries are worth scaling.
sparktoro.stackImpact: Choosing SparkToro means you can leave the obvious channels and reach your audience where the competitor is not, but it is a research tool, not a measurement tool. Count on linking every find to a test and to your own results, otherwise you put budget on an assumption about where your audience is. The value is in discovering plus testing, not in discovering alone. Without that second step you buy an interesting hypothesis instead of a working channel.
pitfalls: Mistaking an interesting overlap for a proven channel.
Putting media budget on a find without testing it small first.
Picking an influencer on overlap without checking whether a campaign pays off.
Discovering without the second step, testing it against your own results.

spotify-for-artists.shortDescription: Streaming data, listener demographics, and playlist tracking.
spotify-for-artists.description: Spotify is the largest music streaming platform in the world. Insight into your streams, listeners, saves, and playlist placements is essential to steer your release strategy and understand your fanbase.
spotify-for-artists.useCase: Monitoring streaming performance, listener growth, and playlist impact.
spotify-for-artists.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI pulls in your Spotify data and correlates it with your social media activity and ads. That way you see which TikTok video or Instagram post actually drives streams.
problemsSolved: No insight into which marketing actions drive streams
Streaming data sits apart from your social media performance
You do not know which regions your growth is coming from
spotify-for-artists.stevinAngle: Spotify for Artists gives you a surprising amount: streams, listeners, saves, playlist placements, and where your growth is coming from. For steering a release strategy it is the single most important source of measurement there is. So we use it as the foundation, not an afterthought. Where it gets tight is that everything stays inside Spotify. You see the streams spike, but not which TikTok video or ad caused that spike, because the dashboard never draws that link. An artist stares at a nice graph without knowing which action drove it. That is where Stevin sits on top. Through the Spotify data, Stevin reads along and lines the numbers up against your social activity and ads, so a spike can be traced back to the post or campaign that set it off, with a signal to reinforce momentum and a person reviewing anything that carries weight first.
spotify-for-artists.stackImpact: Choosing Spotify for Artists as your main source means lining it up against your social and ad data, because on its own it tells you the what but not the why. Count on a connection that brings the streaming numbers next to your marketing activity. In practice: treat Spotify as the outcome and your social and ads as the cause, and make sure you see both side by side. The question that remains is not whether your streams grow, but which action set off that growth, because otherwise you cannot repeat it.
pitfalls: Admiring a stream spike without knowing which action caused it.
Keeping streaming data separate from your social and ad performance.
Assuming growth keeps going on its own without knowing its source.
