Tracking playlist placements but never tying them to your promotion.

spotler.shortDescription: Dutch email marketing and marketing automation platform.
spotler.description: Spotler is a Dutch platform for email marketing and marketing automation, focused on the Benelux market.
spotler.useCase: Email marketing and automation for the Benelux.
spotler.howWeUseIt: Stevin integrates Spotler with your CRM and lead sources for automated follow-up and nurturing.
problemsSolved: Email marketing is not connected to the CRM
You want a Dutch platform
spotler.stevinAngle: Spotler is a Dutch platform for email marketing and automation with its eye on the Benelux. For an SMB that wants a reliable, local system for newsletters and nurturing without the complexity of the big international suites, it is a logical choice. Support speaks your language and knows the market. The limit is depth. Spotler handles email and basic automation solidly, but the moment you want more than a clean newsletter and a welcome series, you notice that the segmentation and advanced flows are thinner than the pricier alternatives. It is solid, not outright powerful. Where teams get stuck is that email marketing sits apart from the CRM, so follow-up happens on an island. Stevin connects to Spotler through the API, brings in your CRM and lead sources, and makes sure the right trigger comes from your own data instead of a manual list. A person sees every campaign that carries weight first.
spotler.stackImpact: Choosing Spotler means you bring in a local email platform that does its job solidly, but you run into limits with more complex segmentation and flows. Expect it not to hang off your CRM by default, so you have to make that connection to keep follow-up off an island. For anyone who only sends newsletters it is plenty, for deep nurturing you weigh it against heavier tools. In practice: let Spotler do the sending and connect it to your real data so the right people get something at the right moment.
pitfalls: Keeping email marketing apart from the CRM, so follow-up happens on an island.
Pulling triggers from a manual list that nobody maintains.
Assuming solid email also means deep segmentation and complex flows.
Choosing on local support and only later noticing the advanced features are thinner than you need.

spyfu.shortDescription: Competitor PPC intelligence: ad spend, keywords, and ad history.
spyfu.description: SpyFu reveals how much competitors spend on Google Ads, which keywords they bid on, and what their ads look like. Essential for finding opportunities and avoiding waste in your PPC strategy.
spyfu.useCase: Competitor ad spend analysis, finding keyword gaps, and PPC strategy optimization.
spyfu.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI uses SpyFu to identify PPC blind spots. Which keywords are we missing? Where does the competitor spend more? Where are they pulling back? These signals get translated automatically into Advisor recommendations.
problemsSolved: No view of competitors' PPC strategy
Keyword gaps are not identified systematically
Budget gets wasted on keywords where the competitor already dominates
spyfu.stevinAngle: SpyFu shows what normally stays hidden: which keywords your competitor bids on, what their ads look like, and, roughly, what they spend. For finding keyword gaps and avoiding a bidding war you would lose anyway, that is useful ammunition. The caveat is that the spend figures are an estimate, not their invoice, and that a gap in their coverage is not automatically an opportunity for you. Teams get stuck there: they take the numbers literally or chase every keyword the competitor misses, including the worthless ones. Stevin reads SpyFu data and translates it into concrete signals in your Advisor: this keyword is sitting unused while it fits, here the competitor spends more, here they are actually pulling back. It proposes the move, a person decides whether it fits your strategy and budget.
spyfu.stackImpact: SpyFu gives you a view of other people's PPC strategy, but it is a reconnaissance tool, not a steering wheel: it does not tell you what to do, only what they do. Count on a layer that lays the findings next to your own campaign performance, otherwise you copy a competitor who may be running at a loss. The spend is estimated, so treat it as direction. The real value comes when the gaps and overlaps get weighed against what works in your account, not as a loose list of keywords.
pitfalls: Mistaking a competitor's estimated spend for their actual invoice.
Copying a competitor who may be running at a loss themselves.
Chasing every keyword the competitor misses, including the worthless ones.
Not weighing the findings against what works in your own account.

statista.shortDescription: Market data, statistics, and industry reports for strategic backing.
statista.description: Statista aggregates statistics, market research, and industry reports from thousands of sources. From market size to consumer preferences: it is the fastest route to hard numbers for your strategy.
statista.useCase: Market research, backing business cases, and strategic presentations.
statista.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI pulls relevant market data from Statista to add strategic context to campaign analyses. Not just "your CPA dropped," but "your CPA dropped while the market grew 12%."
problemsSolved: Strategic decisions lack market context
Market research costs hours of searching and compiling
C-level presentations lack hard market figures
statista.stevinAngle: Statista is the fastest route to a hard number: market size, consumer preferences, industry figures, aggregated from thousands of sources. For a business case or a board presentation, it saves hours of searching and compiling. Just be sharp on the origin: it is an aggregator, so a number comes from an underlying source with its own method and year, and not every figure is equally fresh or equally comparable. Teams get stuck there: a nice number becomes a fixed fact without anyone checking the source. Stevin pulls relevant market data from Statista to give campaign analyses context, so a result gets meaning: not just that your cost per inquiry dropped, but that it dropped while the market grew. The consultant judges whether the figure fits and is current before it lands in a story.
statista.stackImpact: Statista quickly gives you the market context strategic decisions lack, but it is a collector of other people's figures, not a primary source. Count on checking the origin, the method, and the year before a number appears in a C-level presentation, because not every figure is equally fresh or comparable. The value is in laying a reliable market number next to your own performance, not in blindly taking the first figure that fits. Without that check you back a conclusion with a source you never saw yourself.
pitfalls: Taking a nice figure without checking the underlying source and the year.
Putting outdated or non-comparable numbers side by side as if they were equal.
Treating an aggregator as a primary source.
Grabbing the first figure that fits your story instead of the right one.

strapi.description: Strapi is an open-source headless CMS with a user-friendly admin and a strong API. Self-hosted and fully customizable.
strapi.useCase: Self-hosted headless CMS with full control.
strapi.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI connects Strapi to your marketing tools and makes sure tracking and data integrations work in a headless architecture.
problemsSolved: The headless CMS is not connected to marketing
Tracking implementation is complex
strapi.stevinAngle: Strapi is an open-source headless CMS that you host yourself and can fully customize, with a pleasant admin and a strong API. The appealing side is control: you own it, you shape it to your hand. The flip side is that you also carry the maintenance, hosting, and security yourself. We use it for clients with development capacity who really want to keep their stack in their own hands. Where teams get stuck is the same headless trap: the tracking implementation is complex and the content sits apart from the marketing data until someone connects them. Stevin adds a layer on top, reads the relevant events through the API, and keeps content and behavior connected, with a person reviewing every action that carries weight first.
strapi.stackImpact: Choosing Strapi means you trade control for responsibility: you host and maintain it yourself, including security and updates. Count on development work for the front end, the tracking, and the connections to your marketing stack. It is a content API, not a marketing tool, so you keep analytics and CRM alongside it and connect them. The gain sits in ownership and adaptability, as long as you have the capacity to keep it running and measured.
pitfalls: Self-hosting without accounting for maintenance, updates, and security.
Underestimating tracking implementation in a self-built headless setup.
Leaving content and marketing data separate until no one can oversee the connection anymore.

supermetrics.shortDescription: Data integration for marketing reporting and analytics.
supermetrics.description: Supermetrics pulls data from marketing platforms and sends it to your reporting tools. It acts as a bridge between your advertising channels and dashboards in Looker Studio, Google Sheets or data warehouses.
supermetrics.useCase: Centralize marketing data in your reporting and analysis tools.
supermetrics.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI uses Supermetrics to automatically load data from advertising platforms into Looker Studio, Google Sheets or BigQuery for integrated reporting.
problemsSolved: Marketing data has to be exported manually
Dashboards are not connected to every channel
No automated data flows into reporting tools
supermetrics.stevinAngle: Supermetrics does exactly one thing and does it reliably: pull data from your advertising channels and drop it neatly into Looker Studio, Sheets or a warehouse. It is the bridge, not the destination. We use it where manual exporting eats time and data from several channels has to come into one place. Where teams get stuck is the expectation that Supermetrics also does something with that data. That is not its role. It delivers clean, fresh numbers into your reporting tool, and there it stops: whether someone looks at it and acts is not something it handles. That is where Stevin steps in. Through the same centralized data, Stevin reads along and flags when a value deviates or hits a threshold, with concrete follow-up underneath and a person reviewing every action that carries weight first. Supermetrics brings the data, Stevin watches it.
supermetrics.stackImpact: Supermetrics is a transport layer, so you need something on both sides: the sources it reads and a dashboard or warehouse where it lands. It does not change the data, it only moves it reliably, and if a connector breaks the flow stalls without it warning you. In practice: the real question is not whether the numbers reach your tool, but who notices they tell you something and who picks it up when the supply falters. Without something that reacts to the incoming data, you have fresh data in a dashboard nobody opens in time.
pitfalls: Expecting Supermetrics to do something with the data itself: it only transports.
Letting data land in a dashboard nobody looks at daily.
Neglecting the reporting side because the data flow works.
Only noticing a broken connector when the numbers stall.

syntess-atrium.shortDescription: ERP for installation, maintenance and technical services firms.
syntess-atrium.description: Syntess Atrium is business software for the installation and technical trades: service planning, work orders, materials, maintenance contracts and invoicing in one system.
syntess-atrium.useCase: Manage service requests, engineer scheduling and work orders for installation and maintenance.
syntess-atrium.howWeUseIt: Stevin puts a work layer on top of Syntess. It reads service requests, work orders and planning and flags what needs attention: a recurring maintenance job coming up, a work order with no follow-up, an engineer who cannot start on time. It proposes the action, a person approves it. Stevin does not replace Syntess, it makes the information usable at the right moment. Connect through the API or an export.
problemsSolved: Recurring maintenance is scheduled too late
Work orders are left sitting with no follow-up
Materials or planning do not line up at the start of a job
No early signals about open service actions
syntess-atrium.stevinAngle: Syntess Atrium is a serious industry ERP for installation and technical services: service planning, work orders, materials, maintenance contracts and invoicing in one system. It is broad and it keeps track of a lot, but that very breadth means it never tells you what is urgent. Everything is in there, so nothing stands out. We see service firms stall on this: a recurring maintenance job coming up that never gets scheduled, a work order that is finished but stays hanging, an engineer who cannot start on time because the materials are not in yet. Syntess knows all of it, but waits for someone to go looking. Stevin runs as a layer on top. Through the API or an export it reads service requests, work orders and planning and turns them into signals with a proposed action. The planner approves it, Stevin remembers the moment.
syntess-atrium.stackImpact: With Syntess you already have most of it under one roof, so there is little you need to add alongside it. The gain is not in another system but in what sits on top of the data. The connection runs through the API or an export, and the real question is which moments you watch: upcoming maintenance, open work orders, materials that block the start of a job. Without something keeping an eye on that, the information waits until someone happens to open the right screen. In practice that is where most of the time goes.
pitfalls: Relying on the breadth of the system, so recurring maintenance gets scheduled too late.
Letting finished work orders hang because there is no signal on the follow-up.
Only checking materials at the start of the job, when the engineer is already on the way.
No alert on open service actions, so everything runs on someone watching the screen.

tableau.shortDescription: Enterprise data visualization and analytics platform.
tableau.description: Tableau is one of the most advanced data visualization tools. Ideal for complex analyses and interactive dashboards.
tableau.useCase: Advanced data visualization and interactive dashboards.
tableau.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI connects marketing data to Tableau for organizations that already work with this platform and need advanced visualizations.
problemsSolved: Marketing data is not available in Tableau
Need for advanced visualizations
tableau.stevinAngle: Tableau is one of the sharpest visualization tools out there: for complex analyses and interactive dashboards, little touches it. We connect marketing data to Tableau mostly at organizations that already have it in house and genuinely use that depth. Where it pinches is the price and learning curve against what many teams actually get out of it: a large share uses a fraction of the power and would have been fine with something simpler. And like every dashboard, Tableau is passive. It shows a trend beautifully, but it does not tap anyone on the shoulder when a campaign turns. That is where Stevin sits on top. Through the same data source, Stevin reads the numbers along and flags when something deviates, with concrete follow-up underneath and a person reviewing every action that carries weight first. Tableau is to explore, Stevin to react in time.
tableau.stackImpact: Tableau only pays off if you use the depth and supply the data well. Count on a data layer or warehouse underneath and someone who builds and maintains the visualizations, because self-service sounds easier than it is. It changes nothing about the quality of your sources, it only shows them sharper. In practice: choose Tableau when the analysis is genuinely complex, otherwise you pay for power that sits idle. The question that remains is who reacts to what the dashboards show, because looking is not following up.
pitfalls: Choosing Tableau for analyses that something simpler could have handled: you pay for unused depth.
Assuming self-service means everyone builds dashboards without help.
Putting nice visualizations on weak or slow source data.
Confusing exploring with following up: Tableau does nothing on its own.

talpa-media.shortDescription: Advertising on Talpa brands such as SBS and Radio 538.
talpa-media.description: Talpa Media offers advertising across TV, radio and digital channels through brands like SBS6, Radio 538 and Jinek. It combines traditional media with digital targeting.
talpa-media.useCase: Cross-media advertising across Talpa's TV, radio and digital channels.
talpa-media.howWeUseIt: Stevin integrates Talpa Media campaigns into your media plan and connects results to your digital tracking for a complete picture of your media investment.
problemsSolved: TV and radio campaigns are not linked to digital results
No view of how traditional media contributes to online conversions
talpa-media.stevinAngle: Talpa puts TV and radio within reach, with SBS6 and Radio 538 as familiar names. That is exactly where it is strong and tricky at once: traditional reach that touches a large audience, but that does not measure like a click. We use it with clients where mass reach matters and not every euro has to drive direct conversion. Where teams get stuck is the link to digital. A TV spot runs, the traffic on the site moves, but whether the two have anything to do with each other stays guesswork as long as both worlds sit apart. That is where Stevin sits. As a layer on top of your stack, Stevin places the broadcast moments next to your digital data, so that a notable move in traffic or searches around a spot becomes a signal a person reviews. Talpa does the reach, Stevin makes visible whether it sets anything in motion.
talpa-media.stackImpact: Choosing Talpa means you want to be able to place TV and radio moments next to your digital data, otherwise they stay two split worlds. You need your own analytics and ideally your broadcast schedule to recognize movement around a spot. The question that remains is not whether you reach an audience, but whether you see what that reach sets off in your digital channels. Without that bridge you judge traditional media on feel and your digital channels on figures, and the two never speak to each other.
pitfalls: Spending TV and radio budget without placing broadcast moments next to your digital data.
Crediting movement in traffic around a spot to the spot without checking it.
Keeping traditional and digital media in separate reports that never come together.

tealium.description: Tealium offers enterprise tag management and a CDP. It centralizes data collection and distribution for large organizations.
tealium.useCase: Enterprise data collection and distribution through a CDP.
tealium.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI implements Tealium for organizations that need an enterprise-grade solution for data collection and distribution.
problemsSolved: Enterprise data collection is complex and inconsistent
A need for a scalable CDP solution
tealium.stevinAngle: Tealium is enterprise tag management with a CDP attached, and it is solid at what it was built for: centralizing data collection and distribution for large organizations. Companies with many sites, tags, and sources benefit from it, because the chaos of loose tags becomes manageable. The price is complexity. Setting Tealium up well is specialist work, and many teams underestimate what it costs to keep it clean. Where it goes wrong is when data collection is centralized but no one does anything with what comes out: the data flows around neatly without a single signal or action following from it. Stevin connects to the Tealium data layer, reads the collected streams, and turns them into concrete signals with follow-up underneath, and the consultant sees every change that carries weight before it is carried out.
tealium.stackImpact: Choosing Tealium is choosing an enterprise foundation under your data collection, with the setup and maintenance work that does not stop after go-live. It replaces a tangle of loose tags, but you need the right people to keep it clean, and without those people it gets polluted anyway. The CDP side delivers distribution, not action on its own. The practical approach: arrange something that responds to the distributed data, otherwise you have a tidy pipeline that pumps data around without it ever leading to a decision.
pitfalls: Setting up Tealium without the specialist knowledge to keep it clean.
Centralizing data collection without anyone turning the outcome into action.
Seeing the CDP side as activation while it mostly delivers distribution.
Underestimating maintenance, so the tag setup gets polluted anyway.

teamleader.shortDescription: Belgian CRM for SMBs with project management and invoicing.
teamleader.description: Teamleader combines CRM, project management, and invoicing in one platform. Popular with SMBs in the Benelux.
teamleader.useCase: All-in-one business management for small and mid-sized companies.
teamleader.howWeUseIt: Stevin connects Teamleader to your marketing tools so leads are created automatically and follow-up starts right away.
problemsSolved: Leads are retyped by hand from other tools
No connection between marketing and the CRM
teamleader.stevinAngle: Teamleader does something practical for Benelux SMBs: CRM, projects, and invoicing in one platform, so you do not have to tie three separate systems together. For small and mid-sized companies that want their whole operation in one place, that saves hassle and separate subscriptions. Where the limit sits: an all-in-one that does everything a little rarely does anything outright strong. The CRM side is solid but not deep, and anyone running heavy sales or complex projects notices the parts are shallow. Where teams get stuck is that leads from other tools get retyped by hand and that marketing and the CRM do not talk. Stevin connects to Teamleader through the API, creates leads automatically so follow-up starts right away, and turns a quote or invoice left sitting into a signal. The person sees every action that carries weight first.
teamleader.stackImpact: Choosing Teamleader means you capture three functions in one system, but you give up depth compared to specialized tools. For a simple SMB process that is a fine trade and it saves you separate subscriptions, for heavy sales or complex projects it gets tight and you miss the features of a dedicated tool. It is not connected to your marketing channels on its own, so you have to lay that bridge to avoid retyping and to make sure a lead drops straight into follow-up. In practice: let Teamleader carry the broad foundation and put a layer on top that automates lead processing and follow-up.
pitfalls: Expecting an all-in-one to be equally strong in every part.
Retyping leads by hand because marketing and Teamleader are not connected.
Stretching Teamleader into heavy sales or complex projects it is too shallow for.
Assuming everything in one place is the same as everything well arranged.

the-trade-desk.shortDescription: Independent DSP for programmatic display, video, audio and CTV.
the-trade-desk.description: The Trade Desk is one of the largest independent demand-side platforms in the world. Enterprise advertisers use it for programmatic buying across display, video, audio, native and connected TV, outside the walled gardens of Google and Meta.
the-trade-desk.useCase: Programmatic media buying at scale, including CTV, audio and cross-device targeting.
the-trade-desk.howWeUseIt: Stevin connects The Trade Desk to your tracking, CDP and MMM so you measure not just impressions and clicks, but the incremental contribution per channel and per market.
problemsSolved: Programmatic spend sits in a silo outside the walled gardens
No uplift measurement on CTV and the open web
Cross-device attribution is missing
the-trade-desk.stevinAngle: The Trade Desk is the large independent programmatic player outside the gardens of Google and Meta, with reach across display, video, audio, native and connected TV. For anyone who wants to run programmatic seriously and in their own hands, that is the strength: scale without depending on a walled garden. We use it with clients who have enough volume to steer that themselves. Where teams get stuck is measurement. You reach people on CTV and the open web, but cross-device attribution and the real contribution per channel are notoriously hard, and the spend quickly ends up in its own silo. It becomes a lot of data without anyone weighing the contribution. That is where Stevin sits. As a layer on top of your stack, Stevin reads the campaign data through the API, next to your tracking and your other channels, so that a deviation in spend or reach becomes a signal a person reviews instead of a row that stays inside the platform.
the-trade-desk.stackImpact: Choosing The Trade Desk means you want to build a measurement layer around it, because the platform gives you buying power but does not solve cross-device attribution for you. Count on your own tracking and ideally a data layer where the spend stands next to your other channels. The data comes in through the API, so the real question is not whether you can get it out, but whether someone places the contribution of CTV and the open web next to your performance channels. Without that, programmatic stays a large, loose spend whose effect gets assumed.
pitfalls: Leaving programmatic spend in its own silo, separate from your performance channels.
Assuming CTV and the open web contribute without making that cross-device measurable.
Collecting a lot of data without anyone really weighing the contribution per channel.

ticketmaster.shortDescription: Ticket sales data, conversion tracking, and event analytics.
ticketmaster.description: Ticketmaster is the largest ticketing platform. Sales data, conversion rates, and sell-through rates are essential to understanding your live business.
ticketmaster.useCase: Ticket sales monitoring and show performance analysis.
ticketmaster.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI ties ticket sales data to your marketing efforts, so you know which campaigns actually sell tickets.
problemsSolved: Ticket sales are not tied to specific marketing actions
No early warning when a show is lagging in sales
ticketmaster.stevinAngle: Ticketmaster is the largest ticketing platform, and the data underneath is hard: sales figures, conversion, sell-through. That is exactly what you can read your live business off, without the distortion you get from reach or likes. Where it stops is the link with your marketing. The platform shows that tickets sold, but not which campaign sold them, and it does not warn you on its own when a show is lagging. That last point is exactly the moment you can still adjust, and without an early signal you only notice once it is too late to fill the room. Stevin reads the sales data and ties it to your marketing efforts, so you see which actions actually convert tickets. If a show lags in sales, it surfaces as an early warning with a proposal to adjust. You decide what runs.
ticketmaster.stackImpact: Access to Ticketmaster sales data is not a given for everyone, so the first question is whether your role or a connection lets you reach the numbers. If you have them, they tell you what sold but not what drove it, so you need your campaign data alongside it to tie sales to effort. On its own it is a sales count with no cause. In practice: line the sell-through up against your marketing and set a threshold for what counts as lagging, so a disappointing show becomes an early warning and not a nasty surprise in the final week.
pitfalls: Assuming you can just reach the sales data when access depends on your role or connection.
Not tying sales to campaigns, so you do not know which action converted tickets.
Setting no early threshold, so a lagging show only stands out too late.

tiktok-ads.shortDescription: Advertising on TikTok for reach among younger audiences.
tiktok-ads.description: TikTok Ads is growing fast as an advertising channel, especially for brands that want to reach younger audiences. The platform offers unique creative possibilities but demands solid tracking and measurability.
tiktok-ads.useCase: Brand awareness and conversions among younger audiences through short video ads.
tiktok-ads.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI implements the TikTok Events API and connects the platform to your tracking and CRM. That way you measure not only views and clicks, but actual conversions and leads.
problemsSolved: Unreliable conversion data due to privacy restrictions
No connection to CRM or follow-up processes
Hard to measure ROI
tiktok-ads.stevinAngle: TikTok Ads works for the audiences where it works and not for the audiences where it does not. Sounds glib, but in practice it holds: for brands with an 18-34 audience it performs strongly on cost per acquisition, for B2B or 50-plus audiences it is symbolic. We see teams running TikTok because 'you are supposed to' without checking whether their audience is even there. The first step is always: measure whether your buyers are on it, not whether your competitors are advertising on it.
tiktok-ads.stackImpact: The Events API has to be on, otherwise you lose 40 percent of your conversion data to iOS and privacy restrictions. On top of that: TikTok creatives live 3 to 7 days before they hit creative fatigue. Plan a production cadence of at least 5 new creatives a week, otherwise your account goes into a downward spiral within a month. We feed creative performance back to the creative makers with automatic reports per asset.
pitfalls: Running an ad set until it stops working instead of 5 creatives in parallel with natural selection
Not using Spark Ads for creators you already follow organically, a missed lever
Optimizing web conversions in a market where 70 percent of your audience converts natively inside TikTok
Building lookalike audiences on all site traffic instead of on customers, the model gets the wrong signal

tiktok-creative-center.shortDescription: Analyze trending ads, sounds, and formats on TikTok.
tiktok-creative-center.description: TikTok Creative Center shows the best performing ads, trending audio, and popular formats on the platform. Essential for brands that want to make TikTok-native content that actually lands.
tiktok-creative-center.useCase: TikTok trend monitoring and creative inspiration based on what is working right now.
tiktok-creative-center.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI monitors trending formats and ad patterns on TikTok and compares them with your own content performance. The result: creative suggestions that fit what the platform rewards.
problemsSolved: No view of which ad formats perform best on TikTok
Content does not feel TikTok-native
Trending sounds and formats get picked up too late
tiktok-creative-center.stevinAngle: TikTok Creative Center is an honest look at what works on the platform: the best performing ads, trending audio, popular formats. For anyone making TikTok-native content, that beats going on gut, because it shows what the algorithm actually rewards right now. The catch is that it gives inspiration without a connection. It shows what is trending but does not put it next to your own content performance, so you learn what works on the platform without knowing what works for you. And trends move fast, so without something tracking them you often pick up a format once the peak has already passed. Stevin monitors the trending formats and ad patterns and lays them next to your own results, so the creative suggestions that come out fit both what the platform rewards and what you already have. What you do with it is your call. Stevin supplies the leads.
tiktok-creative-center.stackImpact: Creative Center shows platform-wide trends but says nothing about your account, so you need your own TikTok data to turn a trend into something that fits you. The trends are also fleeting, so the value is in picking them up in time, not in a one-off look. On its own it is a source of inspiration without direction for you specifically. In practice: let Creative Center show what the platform rewards and let a layer on top put that next to your own results, so you pick a format that fits your audience instead of chasing a trend that is already past its peak.
pitfalls: Copying a trend without laying it next to your own content performance.
Picking up a format too late, once the peak on the platform has already passed.
Mistaking platform-wide inspiration for what demonstrably works for your audience.

tiktok-creator-tools.shortDescription: Video performance, audience analytics, and trend tracking.
tiktok-creator-tools.description: TikTok is the viral engine for artists and creators. A single video can generate millions of views and directly affect streaming numbers. Real-time insight into what works is crucial.
tiktok-creator-tools.useCase: Viral content detection, audience analysis, and cross-channel momentum tracking.
tiktok-creator-tools.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI monitors your TikTok performance and detects when content goes viral. The Advisor ties TikTok spikes to your streaming data and recommends ads and merch promotion right away.
problemsSolved: TikTok virality is not used for cross-channel promotion
No link between TikTok views and Spotify streams
You miss the best moment to reinforce momentum
tiktok-creator-tools.stevinAngle: TikTok Creator Tools shows you what the app knows internally about your videos: views, watch time, audience, trends. For an artist or creator it is the place where virality becomes visible first, sometimes hours before it turns into streams or sales. The tool is strong at showing what is happening. What it does not do is tell you what to do with it now. A video that takes off is a short window in which you can reinforce momentum with ads or merch, and that window closes fast. Without something that recognizes the moment and ties it to your streaming numbers, you simply miss it. Stevin runs as a layer over Creator Tools, detects when content accelerates, and lines the spike up against your other data. The proposal comes underneath: scale up now, promote here. You press the button, not us.
tiktok-creator-tools.stackImpact: Creator Tools gives you the organic TikTok data, but to scale a viral moment you need TikTok Ads alongside it, plus your streaming and merch data to see whether the views land anywhere. The data alone is a snapshot, the window to act is short, so the value is in speed of response. The question is not whether you see that something is going viral, but whether something is ready to promote within hours. Without that bridge between views and your other channels, virality stays a nice graph with no revenue behind it.
pitfalls: Admiring virality but reacting too slowly, so the window to scale has already closed.
Not tying TikTok views to streams or sales, so you do not know whether it earned anything.
Having no ad budget ready to reinforce a spike at the moment it counts.

treasure-data.shortDescription: Enterprise CDP for large datasets and complex organizations.
treasure-data.description: Treasure Data is an enterprise CDP that collects, unifies, and activates large volumes of customer data. The platform is built for organizations with complex data landscapes and high demands on scalability.
treasure-data.useCase: Enterprise customer data management for large organizations with complex data sources.
treasure-data.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI implements Treasure Data for organizations that want to centralize and activate large amounts of customer data across their full marketing stack.
problemsSolved: Customer data is spread across too many systems
No scalable solution for unifying customer profiles
Data activation is too slow for real-time marketing
treasure-data.stevinAngle: Treasure Data is an enterprise CDP for the genuinely large data landscapes: high volumes, many sources, strict scalability demands. Where lighter CDPs fall over, Treasure Data stays standing, and that is exactly the niche where we run into it. For an SMB it is far over the top, for a corporation with fragmented customer data it is justified. Where teams get stuck: the platform can unify enormous amounts of data, but that power does not make the setup any simpler. Bringing data together from too many systems stays a project, and the promise of real-time activation hides how much modeling comes before it. Stevin connects to Treasure Data, reads the unified profiles and the activation streams, and turns them into signals with follow-up underneath, with a person reviewing every change that carries weight first.
treasure-data.stackImpact: Choosing Treasure Data is an enterprise decision with an enterprise implementation and a matching price tag underneath. It scales to volumes where other CDPs break, but that asks for specialist setup and ongoing maintenance from people who know the platform. The activation is fast once the profiles stand, and getting them to stand costs by far the most work. The practical approach: do not underestimate the unification project and make sure there is a layer on top that turns the activated data into decisions, otherwise you have an expensive machine pumping data around.
pitfalls: Choosing Treasure Data for a scale you do not have: enterprise weight without enterprise volume.
Underestimating the setup of profile unification because the platform can handle the complexity.
Expecting real-time activation without the modeling that comes before it.
Passing activated data along without anything that turns it into decisions.

trengo.description: Trengo combines WhatsApp, email, live chat, and social messaging in one inbox. Ideal for teams that follow up on leads and customers across multiple channels.
trengo.useCase: Centralized communication via WhatsApp, chat, and email.
trengo.howWeUseIt: Stevin connects Trengo to your CRM and lead processes so all communication is logged and follow-up does not slip through the cracks.
problemsSolved: Messages across different channels get missed
No central view of customer communication
trengo.stevinAngle: Trengo solves a familiar problem: messages coming in over WhatsApp, email, live chat, and social, then vanishing into just as many separate tabs. By bringing it all into one inbox, a team sees at a glance what is waiting, and that is exactly why we use it for clients who handle contact across multiple channels. The limit is what it does after that. Trengo bundles the communication, but it is not a CRM and it does not watch follow-up. A message is read, a conversation had, and whether anything comes next is left to people in a busy inbox. At volume, something still slips through the cracks. Where teams get stuck is exactly that: messages get missed across channels and there is no central view that watches follow-up. Stevin connects to Trengo and your CRM through the API, logs the communication in the right place, and turns an unanswered message or an open promise into a signal. The person decides on the follow-up.
trengo.stackImpact: Choosing Trengo means you get a shared inbox across channels, but it does not replace a CRM and it does not enforce follow-up. Count on a connection to your real system of record, otherwise customer communication lives apart from your contact data. It bundles the incoming side, but watching what is still open has to come from somewhere else. In practice: let Trengo bring the channels together and put a layer on top that logs the communication and watches that no message gets left sitting.
pitfalls: Using Trengo as a CRM: it bundles messages but does not record the customer relationship.
Assuming a shared inbox is the same as watched follow-up.
Letting messages slip across channels at volume without a central view.
Decoupling communication from your real system of record so the data drifts apart.

triple-whale.shortDescription: E-commerce attribution and uplift measurement for DTC brands.
triple-whale.description: Triple Whale offers first-party attribution for e-commerce brands. Through server-side tracking and statistical models, you see which channels actually deliver new customers, beyond the limits of pixel-based tracking.
triple-whale.useCase: E-commerce attribution, customer acquisition cost, and uplift analysis.
triple-whale.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI integrates Triple Whale's attribution data into the cross-validation module. Pixel data from Meta and Google gets compared with Triple Whale's first-party measurement for a more realistic picture of your actual ROAS.
problemsSolved: Platform-reported ROAS is unreliable due to privacy limits
No view of incremental versus cannibalizing conversions
Customer acquisition cost is unclear per channel
triple-whale.stevinAngle: For DTC brands, Triple Whale is a serious answer to the problem that pixel tracking has been hollowed out: with server-side measurement and its own models, it gives a more realistic picture of which channels truly bring new customers. For e-commerce that is a useful counter-voice to the figures the platforms report themselves. Just keep in mind that it is its own model, with its own assumptions, and not objective truth: it is a second measurement, not a final verdict. Teams get stuck there: they swap one self-reported set of figures for another and stop comparing. Stevin brings Triple Whale into the cross-validation. It lays Triple Whale's first-party measurement next to the pixel data from Meta and Google, shows where they diverge, and what that means for your actual return. The consultant judges the difference before any budget shifts on it.
triple-whale.stackImpact: Choosing Triple Whale means you lay a measurement next to the platform figures, not a replacement for them. Count on keeping both in comparison instead of sailing blindly on a new dashboard, because this too is a model with assumptions. The value is in the difference between the sources, not in a single source you now believe. Without that cross-comparison you swap one colored number for another and think you now have the truth.
pitfalls: Swapping one self-reported set of figures for another and stopping comparing.
Treating a model with its own assumptions as objective truth.
Sailing blindly on a new dashboard without cross-checking against the platform data.
Seeking the value in a single source instead of in the difference between sources.

trustarc.shortDescription: Enterprise privacy management and consent platform.
trustarc.description: TrustArc is an enterprise privacy management platform that combines consent management, data mapping and privacy assessments. It is aimed at large organizations with complex compliance requirements.
trustarc.useCase: Enterprise privacy compliance and consent management.
trustarc.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI implements TrustArc and makes sure consent is correctly connected to your tracking and advertising platforms for compliant data collection.
problemsSolved: Enterprise privacy compliance is complex and time-consuming
Consent management is not connected to tracking and marketing
trustarc.stevinAngle: TrustArc is enterprise privacy across the board: consent, data mapping and privacy assessments in one platform, aimed at organizations with legal requirements that go beyond a cookie banner. We recommend it where compliance is a discipline of its own and not something marketing does on the side. That is also the trap. TrustArc is heavy and slow to set up, and on smaller setups you pay for governance you never call on while the measurement meanwhile needs attention. Teams get stuck on the assumption that the platform talks to their tracking on its own. That connection has to be right, otherwise your privacy file is in order while your data leaks. Stevin runs as a layer over the consent status from TrustArc and your tag data, and raises a signal the moment measurement drops out or a tag ignores consent. That way the gap between compliance on paper and working measurement becomes visible.
trustarc.stackImpact: Choosing TrustArc means a compliance project, not a quick install. Count on data mapping, assessments and someone to maintain them, plus a separate tag manager and Consent Mode connection for the measurement side. The platform covers the legal breadth, but it says nothing about whether your conversion data still comes in after consent, and those two things get mixed up easily. In practice: let TrustArc do the compliance and separately watch the quality of your measurement with a test on your core conversions. Otherwise you have a sealed file on top of tracking with silent gaps, and that only gets noticed late.
pitfalls: Choosing TrustArc for a setup that does not need the governance.
Expecting consent to talk to your tracking automatically.
Filling in data mapping and assessments once and letting them go stale.
Neglecting the measurement side because the compliance is right on paper.

tunecore.shortDescription: Music distribution, publishing, and royalty analytics.
tunecore.description: TuneCore is one of the largest independent music distributors. Beyond distribution it offers publishing services and detailed royalty reporting.
tunecore.useCase: Distribution management and publishing royalty tracking.
tunecore.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI combines TuneCore data with your streaming and social media analytics for an integrated overview of your release performance.
problemsSolved: Publishing royalties are hard to tie to specific marketing actions
Distribution performance is not visible per platform
tunecore.stevinAngle: TuneCore is one of the larger independent distributors, and beyond distribution it also offers publishing and detailed royalty reporting. That publishing piece is where it sets itself apart, because that is where income sits that many artists otherwise leave on the table. The data is thorough. The bottleneck is in the link. Publishing royalties are hard to trace back to a specific marketing action, and the distribution performance per platform stays a loose overview instead of part of your bigger picture. So you have a lot of numbers and little connection, and the question of what your promotion actually earned stays unanswered. Stevin combines the TuneCore data with your streaming and social analytics into an integrated overview of your release performance, so it becomes visible which effort translates into earnings. A release that stands out financially or in reach surfaces as a signal with a proposal, and you keep the decision in hand.
tunecore.stackImpact: TuneCore delivers distribution and publishing royalties, but publishing income comes in through a slow and complex chain, so the link to a specific action is hard to draw and the data is delayed. Count on exports and on your streaming and social data alongside it to make release performance complete. On their own they are two separate royalty streams with no context. In practice: bring distribution and publishing together with your reach data in one picture and let a layer on top pull out the releases that stand out financially or in growth, so your effort and your return finally sit side by side.
pitfalls: Trying to tie publishing royalties to a single action when the chain is too slow and coarse for it.
Not bringing distribution performance per platform together with your reach data, so the link is missing.
Underestimating the delay in royalty reporting and drawing too current a picture.

twenty.shortDescription: Open-source CRM you host and own yourself.
twenty.description: Twenty is an open-source CRM you can host, fork, and extend yourself. A modern alternative to Salesforce and HubSpot, with a developer-friendly API and full control over your data.
twenty.useCase: A CRM for teams that want to own their data and keep the stack in their own hands.
twenty.howWeUseIt: Stevin runs as a work layer over Twenty. Because Twenty is open with a strong API and webhooks, Stevin reads contacts, pipeline, and activity directly and turns them into signals and follow-up. You own the CRM, Stevin delivers the intelligence on top, with no vendor lock-in.
problemsSolved: A standard CRM is expensive or too heavy
You want to keep your data in your own hands
No smart follow-up without external tools
twenty.stevinAngle: Twenty does something rare in CRM land: it actually gives you your data back. Open-source, self-hostable, forkable, with a developer-friendly API. For clients who have no appetite for vendor lock-in or the price hikes of the big names, that is a serious argument. Honest about the other side: open-source also means you keep it running yourself. Twenty is young, it lacks the polished integrations and the ready-made workflows of the established players, and without someone with technical skills, self-hosting becomes an obligation rather than a freedom. Where teams get stuck is that they have a clean CRM but still no smart follow-up, because that is not built in. Stevin runs as a work layer over Twenty and reads contacts, pipeline, and activity directly through the strong API and webhooks. Loose data becomes a signal with a concrete next action, and the person sees every action that carries weight first.
twenty.stackImpact: Choosing Twenty means you take in control and ownership, but also the responsibility for hosting, updates, and maintenance. Count on someone with technical skills or a party that manages it, otherwise open-source is more a burden than a benefit, and you are tied to a system you have to keep running yourself. You still need a layer for follow-up, because Twenty is a clean database and does not think for you. You also build the integrations with your calling, email, and marketing tools yourself. In practice: let Twenty do what it is strong at, owning your data without lock-in, and build the intelligence and the connections on top.
pitfalls: Choosing self-hosting without someone to carry the maintenance and updates.
Expecting a young open-source CRM to have the same ready-made integrations as the big names.
Setting up a clean CRM and thinking the follow-up comes with it.
Confusing ownership with ease of maintenance: you own it, so you manage it too.

faqs.question: Why Twenty instead of a standard CRM?
faqs.answer: Twenty is open-source and self-hosted, so you own your data and can extend it. Stevin runs on top as the AI layer, just like with any other CRM.

twitch.shortDescription: Live stream analytics, viewer engagement, and subscriber data.
twitch.description: Twitch is not only for gamers. More and more DJs and artists stream live sets. Viewer data and chat engagement offer direct feedback on your performance.
twitch.useCase: Live stream performance tracking and real-time community engagement.
twitch.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI monitors your Twitch metrics and integrates live stream data into your broader performance overview.
problemsSolved: Live stream performance is not factored into your overall analytics
Chat engagement is not analyzed for sentiment
twitch.stevinAngle: Twitch has long stopped being only for gamers, and for DJs and artists streaming live sets it is direct feedback in real time: viewer counts, chat moving along with you, subscribers committing during a good stream. That is valuable, because it is an audience actively choosing to stick with you. The weak point is that this data goes nowhere. A stream ends, the numbers stay inside Twitch, and none of it comes back in your total picture of how you are doing. The chat is full of sentiment no one ever reads. Stevin monitors your Twitch metrics and pulls stream performance out of isolation, so a rising or falling line surfaces as a signal next to your other channels. Whatever needs follow-up comes underneath as a proposal, and you keep your hand on the button.
twitch.stackImpact: Twitch has a usable API, but the data is per stream and tied tightly to the moment, so you need your other channels to see a trend instead of loose spikes. The chat is a rich source of sentiment you have to open up and analyze yourself, because Twitch summarizes none of it. On its own, a stream report is a snapshot with no context. In practice: treat Twitch as one of your signal sources, not a standalone channel, so live performance counts instead of evaporating the moment the stream stops.
pitfalls: Looking at stream numbers one at a time without putting them over time or next to other channels.
Leaving the chat unread, so valuable sentiment and signals get lost.
Keeping live performance outside your overall analytics, so it evaporates after the stream.

usercentrics.shortDescription: Consent management platform with high opt-in rates.
usercentrics.description: Usercentrics is a consent management platform focused on maximizing opt-in rates while staying compliant.
usercentrics.useCase: Consent management with a focus on opt-in optimization.
usercentrics.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI implements Usercentrics with optimized consent banners and connects it to Google Consent Mode for maximum data quality.
problemsSolved: Low consent rates lead to data loss
Consent banner is not optimized
usercentrics.stevinAngle: Usercentrics sells itself on opt-in rate, and that is an honest claim: the banners are better optimized than the average, so you keep more measurable visitors without breaking the rules. That is why we use it where every percent of consent counts for the measurement. What it does not do is check for you whether that higher opt-in actually lands in your tracking. A well-performing banner on a wrongly connected tag setup still produces garbage. That is where it often goes wrong: the banner gets all the attention, the Consent Mode connection does not. Stevin runs on top and reads the consent signals together with your tag data, so you see when consent comes in but measurement still drops out. The difference between a nice opt-in and usable data, with a person checking the correction.
usercentrics.stackImpact: Usercentrics delivers the banner and the opt-in, but you still need a tag manager and a correct Consent Mode connection to get anything out of it. The gain is in consent, the risk is in the assumption that consent equals measurement. In practice: optimize the banner and in the same pass check whether your tags actually pick up the consent. Otherwise you run a high opt-in on data that still does not come through, and the difference only shows up in the report.
pitfalls: Optimizing the banner but not checking the Consent Mode connection.
Confusing a high opt-in with usable conversion data.
Keeping tweaking banner copy without measuring whether consent really comes through.
Adding tags after setup that do not follow the consent logic.

vidmob.shortDescription: Creative intelligence platform for video and display ads.
vidmob.description: VidMob combines AI analysis of creative elements with campaign performance. The platform scans video and display ads frame by frame and links visual choices (color, copy, composition, actors) to KPIs like CTR, VTR, and conversion.
vidmob.useCase: Video ad optimization, creative scoring, and data-driven production.
vidmob.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI uses VidMob's creative intelligence to identify patterns that human reviewers miss. Which opening frames hold attention? Which CTA placement converts? The insights flow straight into the next creative round.
problemsSolved: Video ads get judged on feel, not on data
No frame-level view of what works inside a video
Creative lessons get lost between campaigns
Production and performance sit in separate silos
vidmob.stevinAngle: VidMob goes deeper than most creative tools: it scans video and display frame by frame and links color, copy, composition, and even the actors to KPIs like CTR and watch time. For brands that run a lot of video, it finds patterns the naked eye misses. The flip side is that it is an analysis platform, not a production or follow-through layer. It scores what was there, but the lesson does not land in the next brief on its own, and in practice that knowledge gets lost the moment the campaign ends. Teams get stuck there: rich insights, no memory between campaigns. Stevin sits as a layer over VidMob and holds that memory. It reads the creative intelligence via API, keeps what worked in which audience, and returns it as a concrete instruction for the next round. Every brief with budget impact goes past a person first.
vidmob.stackImpact: VidMob gives you frame-level insight you get nowhere else, but it is a silo next to your production and your media buying. Count on a link that brings the scores back to your creative team and into the next campaign, and on a place where those lessons stay put, otherwise every finding stays a one-off. The data comes out via API, so the real question is not whether you can analyze it, but whether something remembers and reuses the outcome. Without that you start every campaign at zero again, running the same expensive analysis from scratch.
pitfalls: Producing rich frame analyses that stay in a silo next to production.
Forgetting the lesson from a video the moment the campaign ends.
Scoring what was there without anyone bringing it back to the next brief.
Starting every campaign at zero because there is no memory between rounds.

visma-solidbricks.shortDescription: Project administration for construction, part of Visma.
visma-solidbricks.description: Visma Solidbricks is project software for construction: estimating, project administration, hours and invoicing within the Visma ecosystem.
visma-solidbricks.useCase: Administer construction projects within the Visma ecosystem.
visma-solidbricks.howWeUseIt: Stevin puts a work layer on top of Visma Solidbricks and flags what needs attention per project: a quote with no follow-up, a delivery that has not been confirmed, a planning step that is blocked. Connect through the API or an export.
problemsSolved: Quotes and extra work are not followed up in time
Project information is scattered
A planning step gets stuck without anyone seeing it
No early signals per project
visma-solidbricks.stevinAngle: Visma Solidbricks is project software for construction within the Visma ecosystem: estimating, project administration, hours and invoicing. The advantage is clear, it ties into the rest of your Visma administration and that saves double work. The downside is that, like the other construction ERPs, it mainly records and gives no priority on its own. We see construction firms stall on this: a quote that was not followed up, a delivery that has not been confirmed, a planning step that gets blocked without anyone noticing. Solidbricks keeps it neatly, but it waits for someone to look. Stevin puts a work layer on top, through the API or an export, and turns the project data into signals with a concrete action underneath. The system stays your administration, Stevin makes sure what needs attention surfaces in time and lands with the right person.
visma-solidbricks.stackImpact: Choosing Solidbricks makes sense if you are already in the Visma ecosystem, because the fit with your administration is the gain. Functionally there is little you need to add. The monitoring on top is what is missing. The connection runs through the API or an export, and the question is which project moments you want to see early: unfollowed quotes, unconfirmed deliveries, blocked planning steps. Without something watching for that, the information waits in the system and you only see a problem once someone happens to open the right screen.
pitfalls: Leaving quotes and extra work sitting because no signal is set on the follow-up.
Keeping project information scattered with nothing that pulls it together per project.
Only seeing a blocked planning step once the work has already stalled.
Trusting that fitting into Visma also means someone gets warned.

vistar-media.description: Vistar Media is a programmatic DOOH platform that lets you buy digital outdoor advertising using the same logic as online programmatic. Targeting based on location, time and audience data.
vistar-media.useCase: Programmatic DOOH buying with audience-based targeting and location data.
vistar-media.howWeUseIt: Stevin uses Vistar Media for programmatic DOOH and integrates campaign data with your online channels for cross-media reporting and attribution.
problemsSolved: DOOH is not included in digital reporting
No programmatic approach to outdoor advertising
vistar-media.stevinAngle: Vistar Media brings the logic of online programmatic to digital outdoor advertising: you buy DOOH on location, time and audience data, the same way you buy online inventory. That is a real step forward for a medium that long ran only through long contracts. The limit is the same as with all outdoor advertising, and with Vistar it is a touch sharper because it feels programmatic and therefore creates the illusion of full measurability: no click is left behind, and you have to build the link to online conversions yourself. We see advertisers get stuck here: the buying is smart and flexible, but the DOOH data never makes it into the digital reporting. Stevin runs as a layer on top of your stack, reads the campaign data through the API, and places DOOH next to your online channels for cross-media reporting. A person reviews the conclusion before budget moves.
vistar-media.stackImpact: Choosing Vistar gives you a programmatic way to buy outdoor advertising, more flexible than the classic contracts. But buying programmatically is not the same as measuring programmatically: no click is left behind, and the DOOH data does not flow into your digital reporting on its own. Count on a connection that brings it together across media. The data comes available through the API. The real question is how this screen visibility carries through to online conversions, because without that bridge you still judge a flexibly bought channel in isolation.
pitfalls: Not including DOOH data in your digital reporting, leaving you blind across media.
Assuming that buying programmatically also means measuring programmatically, when a click is missing.
Not building a bridge to online conversions, leaving the channel in isolation.
Mistaking the flexible buying for full measurability.

webflow.shortDescription: Visual website builder with a CMS and hosting.
webflow.description: Webflow combines a visual builder with a CMS and hosting. A good fit for design-led websites without technical compromises.
webflow.useCase: Premium websites with visual control and a CMS.
webflow.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI implements tracking, form connections, and CRM integrations on Webflow sites.
problemsSolved: Webflow forms are not connected to the CRM
Tracking is not fully set up
webflow.stevinAngle: Webflow combines a visual builder with a CMS and hosting, and that is where the value sits: design-led sites without making technical compromises. We use it for clients who want a premium look and still want to manage their own content. Nice platform, but it was built to make sites, not to process your data. Where teams get stuck is exactly there: a Webflow form looks good but by default hangs off nothing, and the tracking is often not fully set up. A submission comes in and stays stuck in Webflow. Stevin adds a layer on top, reads the form submissions through a webhook, and turns them into follow-up in your CRM, with a person seeing every action that carries weight first.
webflow.stackImpact: Choosing Webflow means you get a strong site but lay the connections over it yourself: the forms and tracking do not link to your CRM and analytics on their own. Count on a webhook connection to pass submissions through, and on work to get tracking fully in place. It is not a CRM and not an automation tool, so you keep those alongside it. The question is not whether the site looks good, but whether a lead that comes in actually lands somewhere.
pitfalls: Not connecting Webflow forms, so submissions stay stuck in the platform.
Leaving tracking incomplete on a site that was built for conversion.
Trying to use Webflow for data processing instead of as a site layer.

whatagraph.description: Whatagraph is a reporting platform that combines marketing data from different sources into visually attractive reports. Suited to agencies and marketing teams that want to deliver professional reports fast.
whatagraph.useCase: Visual, automated marketing reports for clients and stakeholders.
whatagraph.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI uses Whatagraph to deliver clear marketing reports that combine data from multiple channels into a visual format.
problemsSolved: Reports are not visual enough for stakeholders
Too much time spent assembling reports manually
No centralized overview of marketing channels
whatagraph.stevinAngle: Whatagraph is made to impress the recipient: data from multiple sources in a report that looks sharp, so a stakeholder gets it at a glance. We use it where the presentation counts and a raw export just does not convince. Where it pinches is that the emphasis sits on the form. A visually strong report shows neatly that something went wrong, but the report itself does nothing about it and it arrives at fixed moments, not when it matters. Whatagraph brings the data together nicely, but it does not flag and it does not follow up. That is the layer Stevin adds on top. Through the same channel data, Stevin reads along and gives a heads-up the moment something turns, with concrete follow-up underneath and a person reviewing every action that carries weight first. Whatagraph shows, Stevin watches.
whatagraph.stackImpact: Whatagraph sits on the presentation side of your stack: it pulls data from your channels and makes a polished report of it, but it is not a workspace and not an early warning. Count on it living alongside your sources and bringing them together at fixed moments. In practice: use it to take stakeholders through what happened, and put something next to it that notices what is going on now. A nice report convinces, but it tells you too late that you should have intervened.
pitfalls: Confusing a handsome report with intervening in time.
Letting the form win over the question of who reacts to the numbers.
Assuming combined data equals follow-up.
Only looking at fixed moments and missing ongoing deviations.

wix.description: Wix is an accessible website builder that lets you build a website without technical knowledge.
wix.howWeUseIt: Stevin implements tracking and form connections on Wix sites so your marketing data is reliable, even on a simpler platform.
problemsSolved: Tracking on Wix is set up in a limited way
Form data is not processed automatically
wix.stevinAngle: Wix is made to build a site without technical knowledge, and it pulls that off: for a simple website or landing page it is fast and accessible. The flip side shows up the moment you want to measure more seriously. The tracking is more limited than on an open platform, and form data does not always come into your systems clean. We run into Wix at smaller clients where the platform fits fine, as long as you keep the expectations around data honest. Where teams get stuck is the assumption that tracking and connections are as flexible as on WordPress. They are not. Stevin works within those limits: it reads the form submissions through the available connection or a webhook and turns them into follow-up in your CRM, with the person seeing every action that carries weight first.
wix.stackImpact: Choosing Wix means you trade accessibility for measurability: the tracking options are more limited, so count on a simpler setup and less control than on an open CMS. For a simple site that is no problem, for a data-driven funnel it is. At the very least make sure form data comes through to your CRM, because that is where it goes wrong. The question is whether you will ever want to measure more than Wix allows, because then you are choosing the wrong foundation.
pitfalls: Choosing Wix while you will later want serious tracking: you are stuck within the platform's limits.
Not getting form data connected through to your CRM, so leads get left sitting.
Expecting tracking to be as flexible as on an open CMS.

woocommerce.description: WooCommerce turns any WordPress site into a webshop. Flexible and open-source, with full control over your data.
woocommerce.useCase: E-commerce on WordPress with flexibility and control.
woocommerce.howWeUseIt: Stevin implements tracking, product feeds, and CRM connections for WooCommerce so your webshop is fully integrated with your marketing stack.
problemsSolved: WooCommerce data is not connected to marketing tools
E-commerce tracking is incomplete
woocommerce.stevinAngle: WooCommerce is not an e-commerce platform, it is a WordPress plugin that lets you do e-commerce. That distinction decides when to choose it and when not to. Do: when you already run WordPress for content marketing and the overlap is valuable. Do not: when you are purely transactional. Maintenance is structurally heavier than Shopify (security updates, plugin conflicts, hosting choices), costs look lower but add up. We migrate WooCommerce shops to Shopify on average 3 years after launch, when maintenance time no longer matches revenue.
woocommerce.stackImpact: For your stack: hosting is crucial (Kinsta, WP Engine, or a specialized WooCommerce host, not generic shared hosting). Plugin discipline: WooCommerce Subscriptions, WooCommerce Memberships, a payment plugin, a tax plugin. On top of that, switch ALL caching plugins OFF on /cart, /checkout, /my-account, otherwise customers see old order details. SEO via Yoast or Rank Math, the same hygiene as content WordPress.
pitfalls: Caching on transactional pages. Customers see the checkout of a previous visitor.
Updating plugins without staging. The site goes down on a conflict, sometimes hours of downtime.
Leaving the default WordPress login on /wp-admin. Brute-force attacks run continuously.
GA4 tracking through a free plugin, often outdated or buggy. Conversions get missed.

wordpress.shortDescription: The most widely used CMS in the world.
wordpress.description: WordPress runs on more than 40 percent of all websites. Flexible, extensible, and with a huge ecosystem of plugins and themes.
wordpress.howWeUseIt: Stevin makes sure your WordPress site is properly connected to tracking, forms, CRM, and automation. From GTM implementation to form connections and landing page optimization.
problemsSolved: Tracking is not implemented properly on WordPress
Forms are not connected to the CRM
Landing pages do not convert well
wordpress.stevinAngle: WordPress runs on a huge share of the web, and that is exactly why it works and why it gets messy: it can do anything through plugins, and that is also how it gets out of hand. We run into it at almost every SMB client, and the problem is rarely the CMS itself, but the stack of plugins around it and tracking that is half set up. Where teams get stuck is that forms do not hang off the CRM, that GTM is half installed, and that nobody is sure which conversion lands where. WordPress records the page, but it watches nothing of what should happen after. Stevin puts a layer over that, reads the form submissions through a connection or webhook, and turns them into follow-up in your CRM, with the person seeing every action that carries weight first.
wordpress.stackImpact: Choosing WordPress means you have to set up the tracking and the connections well yourself, because the CMS does not supply them cleanly: count on GTM work and a form-to-CRM connection. The plugin freedom is a blessing and a risk, because every extra plugin is a place where your data flow can break. In practice: keep the plugins limited, set tracking server-side where it counts, and make sure a form submission lands somewhere. Without that, it stays pretty pages.
pitfalls: Plugins keep stacking until your data flow breaks quietly somewhere.
Forms that do not hang off the CRM: a lead comes in and nobody follows up.
Leaving tracking half set up, so you do not know which conversion comes from where.

x-ads.shortDescription: Advertising on X (formerly Twitter) for real-time reach.
x-ads.description: X Ads (formerly Twitter Ads) offers advertising on the X platform with strong real-time conversations, news and B2B reach. Suited to brands that respond to current events and public debate.
x-ads.useCase: Real-time reach, B2B targeting and event-driven campaigns.
x-ads.howWeUseIt: Stevin implements the X Pixel and CAPI connection and integrates X Ads with your CRM and MMM for a complete attribution stack.
problemsSolved: X's contribution is not included in attribution
Conversion data gets lost through cookie loss
x-ads.stevinAngle: X Ads brings you to real-time conversations, news and a B2B audience, strong when you respond to current events or an event. That speed is the value: you are there at the moment something is happening. We use it with brands that can react to current events and want a B2B audience. Where it pinches is measurement. Through cookie loss, conversion data gets lost if you do not lean on the Pixel plus the CAPI connection, and without that, X's contribution stays outside your attribution. You see engagement, but not what it delivers. Stevin runs as a layer on top of your stack and, once the X Pixel and CAPI are in place, reads the campaign data through the API next to your CRM and your other channels. An event-driven campaign that makes noise but no leads, or a spike that does convert: that becomes a signal a person reviews, instead of engagement that feels good without you knowing what sits underneath.
x-ads.stackImpact: Choosing X Ads means the Pixel and CAPI connection have to be in place, otherwise you lose conversion data to cookie loss and measure engagement without return. Count on the server-side connection as a foundation before you place the contribution next to your other channels. The data comes in through the API, but the condition is that the measurement is right. The question that remains is whether real-time reach and engagement translate into leads you can follow, because without that connection X is a channel that is visible but whose return stays uncertain.
pitfalls: Running X without Pixel and CAPI: conversion data gets lost to cookie loss.
Reading engagement as a result without seeing whether there are leads underneath.
Not carrying event-driven spikes through to your CRM, so the contribution gets lost.

youtube-ads.shortDescription: Video advertising on YouTube for reach and conversion.
youtube-ads.description: YouTube Ads is part of the Google ecosystem and offers powerful options for video advertising. From awareness to conversion, video is an increasingly important part of the marketing mix.
youtube-ads.useCase: Brand awareness and retargeting through video ads.
youtube-ads.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI sets up YouTube campaigns inside your Google Ads account and makes sure view-through conversions and audiences are measured correctly and reused across your other channels.
problemsSolved: No insight into the contribution of video to conversions
YouTube audiences are not reused across other channels
youtube-ads.stevinAngle: YouTube Ads is not a standalone channel but part of your Google Ads account, and that is immediately both its strength and its weakness. The targeting and reach are strong, and audiences are directly reusable within Google. But video measures differently from search: someone sees your ad and buys days later through another channel, and by default that contribution falls between the cracks. We see advertisers stall on this: the view-through conversions are not measured well, so on paper video seems to produce little, and the audiences you build with video are left sitting instead of coming back in search and display. Stevin runs as a layer on top of your Google stack, reads the campaign and conversion data through the API and flags where the measurement leaks or where a built audience stays unused. A person sees the advice first, then the change goes live.
youtube-ads.stackImpact: YouTube Ads runs inside Google Ads, so you do not add a separate platform, but you do share the measurement logic with search and that is where it goes wrong. You need a correct measurement setup that keeps view-through separate, otherwise the contribution of video disappears into the figures of your other channels. The connection runs through the Google API. The real question is whether the audiences you build with video also come back in search and display, because otherwise you are paying for reach that you then throw away.
pitfalls: Not measuring view-through separately, so video seems to produce nothing on paper.
Holding video to the same KPI as search, which steers the channel into the ground.
Not reusing built video audiences in search and display, so you throw reach away.
Assuming a conversion inside Google is automatically attached to the right channel.

youtube-studio.shortDescription: Video analytics, subscriber growth, and audience retention data.
youtube-studio.description: YouTube is the platform for long-form content: DJ sets, vlogs, music videos, and live streams. Watch time and audience retention are the metrics that determine whether your content works.
youtube-studio.useCase: Video performance analysis, subscriber growth, and content strategy optimization.
youtube-studio.howWeUseIt: Stevin.AI analyzes your YouTube data and correlates video performance with your broader social media and streaming strategy. Long sets that perform well can be promoted through ads.
problemsSolved: YouTube analytics sit apart from your other channels
No insight into which sets or videos drive streams
Audience retention data is not used for content optimization
youtube-studio.stevinAngle: YouTube Studio is built for long-form: full DJ sets, vlogs, clips, live streams. The metrics that matter are watch time and retention, because they show whether people stay or click away after twenty seconds. Studio measures that sharply and honestly. Where it stops is the bridge to your broader strategy. The data on which set holds viewers sits apart from your streaming and social numbers, so you know a video performs well, but not whether it also earns listeners or fans. You have to draw that link yourself, and in practice it rarely happens. Stevin reads your YouTube data and puts retention and performance next to your other channels, so a set that works surfaces as a candidate for promotion. The recommendation to put media budget behind a strong video you see first, before anything runs.
youtube-studio.stackImpact: YouTube data comes in clean through the official API, so the connection itself is not the problem. What is missing is the link: retention and watch time sit apart from what they earn in streams or fans, so you need your streaming and social data to read a strong video. Studio measures the video, not the effect outside it. If you want to promote a good set with ads, you connect YouTube to your ad account. The win is in lining things up side by side, because high retention with no follow-through is just a nice number.
pitfalls: Treating retention as the final score when it says nothing about streams or fans without a link.
Leaving a strong video idle because there is no bridge to your ad account to push it.
Analyzing YouTube apart from your other channels, so you do not see what really carries through.

zapier.description: Zapier connects apps without code. From pushing leads to your CRM to sending notifications on new form submissions, Zapier is the glue between your tools.
