zapier.useCase: Automating workflows between marketing tools without code.
zapier.howWeUseIt: Stevin uses Zapier as an integration layer where direct connections are not available. We build robust Zaps that automate your marketing processes.
problemsSolved: Tools cannot be connected to each other directly
Manual tasks take too much time
Data has to be moved by hand
zapier.stevinAngle: In 2026 Zapier is a fine duct tape for process automation between tools that do not know each other natively. For an SMB under 100k zaps per month it is cost-efficient. Above that scale, or for business-critical workflows, Zapier is a risk (latency, single point of failure, and debugging is hard when a Zap breaks). We build on Zapier for proof of concept and migrate to n8n (open source) or a custom integration once a workflow becomes business-critical. Pricing: Free is 100 tasks per month, usually too few. Starter gives 750 tasks. Professional at 2k is enough for most SMBs.
zapier.stackImpact: For your stack: use Zapier where volume is low and reliability is not critical (lead routing, tag sync between marketing tools, Slack notifications). For business-critical work (invoice generation, payment acknowledgement, GDPR actions) build it directly via API or a dedicated integration platform like n8n or Workato. Document every Zap in a spreadsheet, otherwise nobody knows what is running when the person who built it is on holiday.
pitfalls: Stacking Zaps into a Rube Goldberg machine. Debug time grows exponentially.
Hitting the task limit without an alert. Zaps stop quietly and processes break without anyone noticing.
Using a webhook trigger without retry logic. Failed events disappear for good.
Forgetting a filter step. The Zap fires on every trigger and burns tasks for nothing.

faqs.question: Do you always use Zapier?
faqs.answer: No. We pick the best integration method per situation. Sometimes that is a direct connection, sometimes Zapier or Make, sometimes a custom build.

zendesk-sell.shortDescription: Sales CRM from Zendesk with a focus on productivity.
zendesk-sell.description: Zendesk Sell is a sales CRM focused on ease of use and productivity for sales professionals.
zendesk-sell.useCase: Sales pipeline management with strong integration into Zendesk Support.
zendesk-sell.howWeUseIt: Stevin connects Zendesk Sell to marketing channels and makes sure leads from campaigns are directly available to the sales team.
problemsSolved: Sales misses leads from marketing campaigns
No automatic connection between marketing and sales
zendesk-sell.stevinAngle: Zendesk Sell has a clear logic: it wins when your support already runs on Zendesk. Tying sales and support together on one platform gives a fuller customer picture, and that is exactly what we use it for. Outside that context the story is weaker. As a standalone sales CRM, Zendesk Sell is fairly ordinary, it lacks the depth and the community of the specialized players, and the development feels less energetic than on the support side. Anyone who chooses it without Zendesk Support is mostly buying middle of the road. Where teams get stuck is that sales misses leads from marketing campaigns and that the link between marketing and sales is absent. Stevin connects to Zendesk Sell through the API, brings campaign leads straight to the sales team, and turns a lead left sitting without follow-up into a signal with a concrete action. The person reviews every intervention first.
zendesk-sell.stackImpact: Choosing Zendesk Sell mainly makes sense if you are already on Zendesk Support, because that is where the added value of a shared customer picture across sales and support sits. Without that context there are stronger CRMs ready for the same money, so weigh it against what you actually need before you commit. The connection to your marketing channels is not a given, so you have to build that bridge to keep sales from missing leads coming in from your campaigns. In practice: worthwhile inside the Zendesk ecosystem, outside it compare critically with the specialized players.
pitfalls: Choosing Zendesk Sell apart from Zendesk Support where stronger CRMs are ready.
Assuming the support tie also pulls your marketing leads in.
Letting campaign leads leak away because marketing and sales are not connected.
Expecting a fuller customer picture without the data from both sides actually coming together.

zoho-crm.shortDescription: Affordable CRM platform with extensive capabilities.
zoho-crm.description: Zoho CRM offers an extensive CRM at a sharp price. With modules for sales, marketing, and support, it is a serious alternative to HubSpot and Salesforce.
zoho-crm.useCase: A CRM for SMBs that need a complete but affordable platform.
zoho-crm.howWeUseIt: Stevin integrates Zoho CRM with your advertising and tracking tools and sets up workflows for automatic lead processing and follow-up.
problemsSolved: The CRM is not connected to marketing channels
Manual processes slow down lead follow-up
zoho-crm.stevinAngle: Zoho CRM gives you a lot for a little. Modules for sales, marketing, and support at a price HubSpot and Salesforce do not come close to, and for an SMB looking for a complete platform that is a strong argument. We use it where budget matters but the need is broad. Honest about the other side: the price translates into an interface that can feel cluttered and into modules that are each a touch less polished than a specialized tool. Everything is there, but nothing is outright strong, and the configuration can turn into a maze. Where teams get stuck is that the CRM sits apart from the marketing channels and that manual steps slow lead follow-up down. Stevin connects to Zoho through the API, brings lead data from your campaigns to the right place automatically, and turns slow follow-up into a signal. The person sees every action that carries weight first.
zoho-crm.stackImpact: Choosing Zoho means you cover a lot of ground at low cost, but you give up depth and sometimes ease of use. Count on time for configuration, because the platform is extensive and that makes setting it up a job. It is not connected to your advertising and tracking tools on its own, so you have to build that bridge to avoid manual handoffs. In practice: let Zoho be the broad foundation and put a layer on top that automates lead processing and guards the follow-up.
pitfalls: Assuming a complete platform is also the best in every module.
Underestimating the configuration: setting it up broadly takes more time than expected.
Disconnecting the CRM from your marketing channels so leads have to be processed by hand.
Confusing a low price with low maintenance: the setup takes work.
